display.fanatic_headline: Western Michigan vs Akron: Salute the Troops Night in Rubber City
display.fanatic_score_line: Projected: Western Michigan Broncos 32, Akron Zips 17
display.fanatic_story:
Western Michigan Broncos vs Akron Zips prediction for Tuesday, November 10: Akron calls it Salute the Troops night at InfoCision Stadium, and on the eve of Veterans Day the Rubber City wants to give everyone who served a reason to stand and roar. Corwin Dahlquist rode in from Kalamazoo with a 6-3 team and a notebook full of blocking diagrams, and Hollister "Zip" Grubbs is waiting at the gate with a 1-8 team, a flag pin and more bounce than any season like this should allow.

"Tonight is for the troops first," Hollister says. "Football second. Then the Zips, then everybody else, and I'll argue with you about the order."

"No argument on the first one," Corwin says. "On the third one, I brought film."

Over on East Buchtel Avenue, Heartland Marimba plays a concert at Guzzetta Recital Hall the same night. Hollister has thought about this. "Mallets on wood over there, shoulder pads on shoulder pads over here. Akron is a percussion town tonight."

"Akron is a rubber town," Corwin says. "You told me four times in the parking lot."

"Rubber bounces. Write it down."

Here's what Corwin has written down. Western Michigan is 6-3 and 4-1 in the MAC, second in the conference, and the Broncos win with the big guys up front. Jalen Buckley has carried 144 times for 711 yards and 8 touchdowns. Cole Cabana ran 7 times for 110 yards against Bowling Green on Halloween. Broc Lowry runs the show without drama: 1,397 yards, 11 touchdown throws and only 3 interceptions. Aveion Chenault is the deep shot, with 540 yards, and 109 of them came in that Bowling Green win.

"That's a full stack," Corwin says. "Buttermilk, warm syrup, the works."

"It's a Tuesday," Hollister says. "Nobody eats a full stack on a Tuesday."

Akron's year hasn't been kind, and Hollister doesn't pretend otherwise. The Zips beat Robert Morris 45-10 back in September and have lost seven in a row since. But he has a case, and he makes it at full volume. Jordan Gant has 730 rushing yards and 7 touchdowns, and he went for 112 against Ohio last Tuesday. Ohio is 7-2 and sits first in the MAC, and the Zips lost to the Bobcats by eight, 28-20. Donelius Johnson has 80 tackles in the middle of the defense, and Cyrus Durham has 3.5 sacks.

"Eight points from the top team in the conference," Hollister says. "We are getting grip, Corwin. You can hear it."

The quarterback picture in Akron is a two-name story. Brayden Roggow has 1,343 yards this year, and Cibastian Broughton took the throws against Ohio, going 22 of 34 for 232 yards. Marcel Williams leads the Zips with 37 catches for 417 yards, whoever is throwing to him.

"Whoever it is," Corwin says, "Austin Alexander has 5 sacks and wants another. Justyce Betts has 65 tackles. Our defense gives up 19.2 a game. Yours gives up 32.2."

Hollister winces, then rallies. "Rubber stretches before it snaps back. That's physics. I did a science fair on it."

"You did a science fair on it in seventh grade."

"And I won."

History sides with Kalamazoo. In the five meetings since 2016, Western Michigan won four. The Broncos won 41-0 in 2016 and 58-13 in 2020, and they beat Akron 34-24 the last time these two met, in 2024. Akron's one win in the stretch was a 14-13 grinder in 2017, and Hollister knows it by heart.

"Fourteen to thirteen," he says. "One point. A one-point game is a coin flip wearing a helmet."

"That was nine years ago," Corwin says.

"Then we're overdue."

Here's how it goes. Akron comes out flying on a night built for big emotion, and Gant finds a crease or two in the first half to keep the student section loud. Then Western Michigan wears them down. Buckley and Cabana take turns, Lowry hits Chenault once over the top, and the Broncos' defense lives in the Akron backfield no matter who is throwing. The Zips earn a late score, the crowd gives it everything, and the band plays for the veterans on the way out.

Corwin packs up his diagrams and pours syrup from an invisible bottle. Hollister salutes the troops one more time, then finds his grin. "Rubber always bounces back," he says. "Always."

My call: Western Michigan Broncos 32, Akron Zips 17.

display.fanatic_headline: Kent State vs Bowling Green: Founders Day Fight for the Anniversary Award
display.fanatic_score_line: Projected: Bowling Green Falcons 27, Kent State Golden Flashes 17
display.fanatic_story:
Bowling Green turns Tuesday night into a birthday party. Kent State Golden Flashes vs Bowling Green Falcons is the Founders Day game at Doyt L. Perry Stadium, and the trophy waiting on the sideline was built for exactly this kind of night: the Anniversary Award, made to honor two schools that were born in the same year, 1910.

Darcy Fenwick has been staring at that trophy since last October, when Kent State kept it with a 24-21 win. Ozzie Brannigan has been staring at the schedule, the weather and the ceiling, because Ozzie expects the worst every week and gets grumpy when he's wrong.

"Founders Day," Darcy says. "Fan and Student Appreciation Night. Students claim free tickets. The whole campus shows up to celebrate the school's birthday, and you're the guy who brought the present we want back."

"I expected a warm welcome," Ozzie says. "I did not get one. This is fine. This is what I expected."

The history of the thing is wonderful, and both of them know it cold. The Lowry Bill created both schools in 1910. The alumni offices dreamed up the Anniversary Award in 1985 to mark their 75th birthdays, and Bowling Green has won it 27 times to Kent State's 13. Darcy says those numbers like a goalie reading off a save chart. Ozzie counters with the recent stuff, because the recent stuff is the only part he enjoys.

"We won it five years in a row," he says. "Twenty-eighteen through twenty-twenty-two. Sixty-two points, twice. Then you won it back two straight, then we took it last year. So it's our turn to lose. I've made peace with that."

"You have not made peace with anything," Darcy says. "You're wearing two jackets."

He is wearing two jackets.

Here's the football. Kent State is 3-6 and 2-3 in the MAC, and the Golden Flashes run their offense through Dru DeShields, who has thrown for 1,629 yards with 9 touchdowns and 7 interceptions. Wayne Harris is the guy he looks for first, with 43 catches for 674 yards and 5 scores, and Harris went for 122 yards at Sacramento State on Halloween eve. When DeShields gets time, he can sling it: 294 yards and four touchdowns against Akron in October.

The trouble has been everywhere else. Kent State scores 14.3 points a game and gives up 30.6. Away from home this year, the Flashes have put up 0 at South Carolina, 3 at Ohio State, 7 at Western Michigan, 2 at South Florida and 10 at Sacramento State.

"Those were tough rooms," Ozzie says. "I expected them to be tough rooms."

"This is a tough room," Darcy says. "It's my room."

Bowling Green walks in at 2-7, also 2-3 in the league, and the Falcons have lost three straight by a combined 21 points. That hurts, but it also tells you how close they've been. Ball State beat them 32-31 in overtime. Buffalo won 31-24. Before that, Bowling Green went to Oxford and beat Miami 24-20, then put 38 on Sacramento State.

Jay Kastantin has completed 150 of his 225 throws for 1,567 yards and 11 touchdowns. Jeremiah Scoby, the tight end, leads the team with 31 catches, and Austyn Dendy has 371 rushing yards and 4 scores. But Darcy's heart lives on the other side of the ball, where Myles Bradley has 9 sacks and Dorian Pringle has 86 tackles.

"Nine sacks," Darcy says. "That's a guy who lives in the crease. Ozzie, your quarterback is going to see him in his sleep."

"I already do," Ozzie says. "I expected to."

Kent State has its own disrupter in Jaihien Roy, who has 5 sacks, and Hayden Dawahare has 50 tackles at linebacker. Ozzie lists them quietly, the way some people list their blessings, then immediately adds that Bowling Green has thrown 8 interceptions and that he will be watching every one of Kastantin's throws like it owes him money.

Here's how the birthday goes. The crowd is louder than a 2-7 team usually earns, because Founders Day crowds don't care about records. Bradley gets home early and DeShields spends the first half running for his life. Harris breaks one deep in the second quarter to keep Kent State close, and Ozzie stands up, then sits back down because he doesn't trust it. Kastantin finds Scoby on the long third downs, Dendy grinds out the clock, and Pringle is in on every tackle that matters. Kent State scores late, but it's too late.

Darcy bangs her stick on the rail like the horn just sounded. Ozzie takes off one of his two jackets, folds it over his arm and stares at the trophy as it heads back across the field.

"I expected this," he says, and for once, he really did.

My call: Bowling Green Falcons 27, Kent State Golden Flashes 17.

display.fanatic_headline: Ohio vs Miami (OH): The Battle of the Bricks Comes to Oxford
display.fanatic_score_line: Projected: Miami (OH) RedHawks 27, Ohio Bobcats 24
display.fanatic_story:
The two oldest universities in Ohio meet for the 103rd time on Tuesday night, and only one side leaves Oxford with a reason to pour something warm into a new mug. Ohio Bobcats vs Miami (OH) RedHawks is the Battle of the Bricks at Yager Stadium, and Penny Trautman and Cordelia Van Doren have been arguing about it since roughly 1804.

That's the year Ohio University was founded, and Penny brings it up before she even sits down. "Eighteen-oh-four. We're older. We were teaching people to read while Miami was still an idea."

"Eighteen-oh-nine," Cordelia answers, adjusting her pearls. "Five years is nothing between friends. And a quiz for you, Penny: who won the very first one, in 1908?"

Penny knows. Everybody in both towns knows. Miami won it 5-0, back when a touchdown was worth five points, and Miami still leads the series 56-44 with 2 ties. Penny counters with the present, which is where she'd rather live. Ohio won the 2024 MAC title game over Miami 38-3 in Detroit and then won last year's meeting in Athens 24-20. Every Ohio win over Miami comes with a commemorative mug for the players and staff, and Penny treats that tradition like scripture.

"Two in a row," Penny says. "I'd like a third."

"You can have tea in one of the ones you've got," Cordelia says. "We'll keep the 100th anniversary game, thank you." Miami won that one at Yager in October of 2024, 30-20, and she keeps the score in her head like a phone number.

Oxford has a little music going before kickoff too. Over at Souers Recital Hall, there's an evening of American Latin music for oboe and piano at 7:30, half an hour before the RedHawks run out. Cordelia says she plans to hear the first piece and then walk briskly. Penny says she'll be in her seat early, wearing green, which in Oxford counts as a form of protest.

Now the football, and both of them shift in their seats.

Ohio is 7-2 and a perfect 5-0 in the MAC, first place in the conference. The Bobcats score 29.4 points a game and give up 21.7. Nick Poulos has taken the most throws in each of the last four games and has 978 yards with 7 touchdowns. Riley Neer is the go-to receiver, with 41 catches for 551 yards and 5 scores, and Dom Dorwart had 108 yards against Akron last week. Duncan Brune ran 10 times for 111 yards in that game. On defense, Michael Molnar is everywhere: 86 tackles and 6 sacks from the linebacker spot.

"Molnar is the whole hill," Penny says. "You go left, he's there. You go right, he's already there and waiting for you."

Miami is 5-4 and 3-2 in the league, and the RedHawks just lost a heartbreaker, 34-31 in overtime to Buffalo. Cordelia doesn't want to talk about it, then talks about it for five minutes. They score 27.4 a game. David McComb leads the team with 1,121 yards and only 1 interception, and Caleb Heavner has taken the most throws in each of the last five games. Maleek Huggins is the big-play receiver, with 473 yards on 27 catches. Rodney Nelson leads the ground game with 436 yards, and D'Shawntae Jones ran for 112 against Buffalo. Roosevelt Andrews III has 5.5 sacks up front, and Malcolm McCain has 70 tackles.

"We've played close all year," Cordelia says. "Twenty to nineteen at Massachusetts. Twenty-eight to twenty-seven at Central Michigan. Our people don't panic. Our people bring blankets."

The recent history is a seesaw. In the ten meetings since 2016, Ohio won six and Miami won four. Penny calls that a trend. Cordelia calls it a sample. They both call the 2021 game, a 35-33 Ohio win, the best one of the bunch.

"So how does it go?" Penny asks.

Here's how it goes. It's tight early, because this one is always tight early. Molnar gets to Heavner once in the first half and the Ohio fans at Yager get very loud. Poulos finds Neer for a big gain to put the Bobcats in front. Then Miami does what it's done all year and hangs around. Jones and Nelson grind out the third quarter. Huggins gets behind the defense once in the fourth. Andrews and McCain make the stop that matters with a few minutes left, and a late field goal sends Oxford home happy.

Cordelia rises, smooths her coat and announces that she'll be heading back toward the recital hall to see if the oboist is taking requests. Penny tucks her travel mug back into her bag, looks at Cordelia and says, "Fine. Next year, Peden Stadium. Bring the pearls."

My call: Miami (OH) RedHawks 27, Ohio Bobcats 24.

display.fanatic_story:
Muncie spends Wednesday afternoon with a cup of tea and a piece of its own history. Buffalo Bulls vs Ball State Cardinals kicks off at Scheumann Stadium that night, but first, over at Minnetrista, local historian Karen Vincent tells the story of Cyrus Dallin's two famous downtown statues, The Passing of the Buffalo and Appeal to the Great Spirit, and Gus Ponder has had his ticket for weeks.

"You have to go," Gus tells Kendra Woolcott. "Three o'clock, the Indiana Room, refreshments included. You learn something, you eat a cookie, you come to the game smarter. That's a Wednesday."

Kendra came in from Western New York with a coat she doesn't plan to wear and a team that hasn't lost in a month. "I'll go," she says. "But I want it on record that I'm only there for the history."

The history is worth it. Dallin made The Passing of the Buffalo in 1929, a Native American chief in full regalia with a bow in his hand and his foot resting on a buffalo skull. It stood first on an estate in New Jersey, came to Muncie in 1975 and was dedicated to the city on April 25, 1976. When construction pushed it off its corner in 1999, it was restored and kept safe in the Minnetrista lobby until September 26, 2007, when it went back up on its original boulder in the roundabout at Walnut and Seymour Streets.

"That's a town that takes care of what it loves," Kendra says, and she means it.

"Now you understand Muncie," Gus says. "Now let me tell you about my football team."

Ball State is 3-6 and 2-3 in the MAC, and Gus is the first to admit the defense has had a rough fall. The Cardinals have given up 34.8 points a game. But look at the last three weeks. Ball State beat Bowling Green 32-31 in overtime, beat Sacramento State 34-17 at Homecoming and lost at UMass last Wednesday 31-30, also in overtime.

"One point," Gus says. "One point at UMass. You know what they call a team that loses by one in overtime? Next week's problem."

Keldric Luster has thrown for 1,482 yards and 10 touchdowns, and he's taken the most throws in eight of the nine games. TJ Horton has 9 rushing touchdowns on just 72 carries, which Gus says is the most efficient thing in Delaware County since the roundabout. Jalen Bonds ran 17 times for 132 yards and 2 scores at UMass. Donovan Hamilton leads the receivers with 354 yards. On defense, Sterling Smith has 46 tackles from the secondary and Ben Marsh has 3 sacks.

Kendra lets him finish, then slides over her own list. Buffalo is 6-3, 4-1 in the MAC and second in the conference. The Bulls have won four straight: 23-8 at Toledo, 25-18 in overtime over Massachusetts, 31-24 over Bowling Green and 34-31 in overtime at Miami last Tuesday.

"We play close, too," Kendra says. "We just finish."

Messiah Burch carries the load, 165 times for 901 yards. Chance Morrow is the one Jason Wright trusts most, with 53 catches for 679 yards and 8 touchdowns, and at Miami he caught 12 for 199 yards and two scores. Wright threw it 46 times that night for 358 yards. SaVeon Brown has 75 tackles at linebacker, and Will Clark has 3.5 sacks.

"Twelve catches," Gus says, shaking his head. "That's not a receiver. That's a subscription."

"He renews every week," Kendra says.

The recent history between these two is a coin toss. Since 2016, Ball State has won three of the five meetings and Buffalo has won two. The last one, in 2024, was absolute madness: Buffalo 51, Ball State 48. Gus remembers every snap. Kendra remembers every snap and the score of every snap.

"Ninety-nine points," Gus says. "My producer at the station still brings it up."

"Your station called it a classic," Kendra says. "I called it Tuesday."

Across campus, the Ball State Campus Orchestra plays a free concert at Sursa Performance Hall at 7:30, the same minute the ball goes up in the air at Scheumann. Gus says he'll catch the encore on the replay. Kendra says the real symphony is a Buffalo drive that takes six minutes off the clock.

So here's the Wednesday script. Ball State comes out loose and fast, and Horton punches in an early score to wake up the student section. Buffalo answers through the air, because Wright keeps finding Morrow in the soft spots. It's tied at the half, and it stays tight all the way into the fourth. Bonds and Horton keep Ball State in it. Then Burch finally breaks one, Brown makes a big stop, and the Bulls kick a late field goal to escape Muncie by two.

Kendra changes into shorts in the parking lot, November or not. Gus packs up his notes, laughs at his own joke one more time and says next week's problem is now Buffalo's problem.

Muncie loses a heartbreaker. Gus laughs the whole way out of the parking lot. My call: Buffalo Bulls 28, Ball State Cardinals 26.

display.fanatic_story:
For one night, Mount Pleasant gets to meet somebody brand new. Sacramento State Hornets vs Central Michigan Chippewas is the first meeting ever between these two programs, and it lands on Veterans Day, Community Night and the last home game of the year at Kramer/Deromedi Field, so Brynn Haverkamp has packed her heaviest coat and her loudest voice.

Mateo Villaseñor flew in from Sacramento with a Hornets scarf and a chef's knife roll he swears is only for show. He's never been to Mount Pleasant. Neither has his team. Sacramento State is a first-year member of the MAC, and this is its first trip here.

"Welcome to the neighborhood," Brynn says. "Ope, sorry, I mean welcome to the tundra. The heaters are by the concourse. The noise is by the student section."

"In Sacramento, November is a light sweater," Mateo says. "Here it's a recipe for soup. I respect it."

Brynn takes this game personally, and not just because it's the last home date. Central Michigan is 4-5 and 2-3 in the MAC, and the school's own game notes lay it out plainly: the Chippewas need two more wins in their last three games to get bowl eligible for a second straight year. That clock begins here.

"Two wins," she says. "Three games. One of them is in my house, on Veterans Day, with the whole town invited. I'm not leaving Mount Pleasant without that one."

She also has to talk about who won't be out there. Central Michigan's notes say the Chippewas play their final three games without several key players, including quarterback Angel Flores and receiver Langston Lewis. That's a lot to lose in November, and Brynn doesn't pretend it isn't. But she likes who stepped up. Jadyn Glasser has been the guy under center the last two games, and he set career highs against Miami with 18 completions on 31 throws for 221 yards. Then at Ford Field against Eastern Michigan, he went 14 of 19 for 175 yards and a score.

"And Woodford," Brynn says. "Did you see Woodford?"

Mateo saw Woodford. Nick Woodford ran 21 times for 123 yards and three touchdowns against Eastern Michigan, all career highs, and the Chippewas held the ball for 40 minutes and 56 seconds. Central Michigan has also converted 18 of its 26 fourth downs this year, which ties the school record. One more sets a new one.

"So you go for it on fourth," Mateo says. "Every time?"

"Every time I'm watching," Brynn says.

Here's the thing about Sacramento State: the record says 2-8, and the Hornets don't play like it lately. They beat Kent State 31-10 on October 30. Then Toledo, a 7-2 team, came to town and barely got out, 20-17. Matt Coleman leads the team with 46 catches for 538 yards and 6 touchdowns, and Raiden Brown had 108 receiving yards against Toledo. Isaiah Ene has 411 yards on the ground. Jackson Sharman has thrown for 1,476 yards and 9 touchdowns, and Brian Salazar Jr. took the most throws against Toledo.

On defense, Mateo cooks from the back. Boogsie Silvera, the safety, has 78 tackles. "A safety with 78 tackles is a sauce that never stops simmering," Mateo says. "It's in every bite."

"That's a lot of tackling for a safety," Brynn says.

"It's a lot of running by your offense into my safety," Mateo says. "That's on you."

Central Michigan's defense is where Brynn hangs her hat. Mayson Hitchens has 68 tackles, Jaxon Cherry has 3 sacks, and the Chippewas give up 23.8 points a game. Coach Matt Drinkall's teams have won all 11 games in which they held the other side under 20 points, according to the school's notes. Sacramento State scores 17.0.

"So all we have to do is be us," Brynn says.

"All we have to do is make you be somebody else," Mateo says.

Sketch it out. The stadium is loud early, louder than you'd expect for a Wednesday in November, because it's the last home game and the town shows up for the veterans. Woodford grinds out the first two drives. Glasser hits a big throw in the second quarter. Sacramento State answers with Coleman, and Silvera makes about a dozen tackles. But the Chippewas keep converting on fourth down, they keep the ball and they wear the Hornets out in the second half. Sacramento State scores late and makes it respectable.

Brynn revs an imaginary snowmobile all the way to the parking lot. Mateo pulls his scarf tighter, takes a long look at the cold, and announces that next year's menu in Sacramento will feature something called revenge.

Brynn's imaginary snowmobile gets a victory lap in Mount Pleasant. My call: Central Michigan Chippewas 30, Sacramento State Hornets 16.

The Fort Meigs Historical Fife & Drum Corps presents the colors in replica uniforms at UToledo's Veterans Day breakfast on Wednesday morning, and that night the Massachusetts Minutemen bring their own old-school name to the Glass Bowl. My UMass vs Toledo prediction lays Toledo Rockets −14.5, takes the Over 52.5 and lands at Toledo Rockets 34, Massachusetts Minutemen 19 for the 7:30 PM ET kickoff on Salute to Service night.

Rocco Szczepanski talks in engine specs. "John Alan Richter has 2,304 yards, 18 touchdowns and 3 interceptions. CJ Miller ran 27 times for 135 at Sacramento State. Andrew Zock has 9.5 sacks. That's horsepower, Abner."

Abner Kettleworth has heard this from Toledo before. "Horsepower needs a road, Rocco. William Watson III threw for 302 against Ball State, and he has 2 interceptions all year. Timmy Hinspeter has 81 tackles. And we're always ready on short notice. It's in the name."

Laying the 14.5 makes sense once you look closer. Toledo scores 35.4 a game and has put 45 on Western Michigan, 41 on San Diego State and 63 on Central Connecticut. The Rockets have won all four meetings since 2021, every one by double digits: 45-7, 55-10, 41-24 and 38-23. UMass has lost four of its last five, and the one win needed overtime to get past Ball State 31-30. My final has Toledo by 15, half a point past the number.

The worry is last week. Toledo escaped Sacramento State 20-17, and Richter threw for only 60 yards on 9 completions. That was a cross-country trip, and Miller carried it 27 times to get it done. Back home, I expect Richter to look like the guy who threw for 391 against Western Michigan. Adjatay Dabbs has 592 yards and 7 touchdown catches.

The UMass quarterback spot has moved around. Watson has taken the most throws in seven of nine games, but Aedan McCarthy and Logan Inagawa each led the way once, against Miami and at Buffalo. Watson has led the throws in each of the last two games and has completed 113 of 163 on the year, so I'm pricing him.

On the over/under, DraftKings opened at 53.5 and it has dipped to 52.5, so I'm getting a point of help on the Over 52.5. UMass scores 27.0 a game and Toledo allows 24.4. My 34-19 lands on 53.

On the side, the room is divided. The Formula has Toledo 32-21, likes Massachusetts Minutemen +14.5 and goes Over 52.5. Next Man Up has 34-20, takes the Minutemen +14.5 and the Over. Letdown Watch has 36-16, likes Toledo Rockets −14.5 and goes Under. In The Trenches has no side and no over/under call this week. Follow The Money is still waiting on a consensus spread, so its side is pending, and it has no total pick.

display.fanatic_story:
Toledo gets up early for Veterans Day. Before most of the Glass City has finished its coffee, Savage Arena fills up for UToledo's 22nd annual Veterans Appreciation Breakfast, and by Wednesday night the Massachusetts Minutemen vs Toledo Rockets game at the Glass Bowl turns into Salute to Service night, with Rocco Szczepanski and Abner Kettleworth both saving a seat for somebody who served.

The breakfast runs from 8 to 11 in the morning, free to every current and former service member and their families, with more than 35 military-focused community groups on hand. The Rossford High School S.O.S. club, short for Serving Our Soldiers, greets people at the door and helps them find a seat and a plate. Fourth-graders from Waterville Primary School handle the music. The Toledo Opera sings the national anthem. And for the country's 250th anniversary, the Fort Meigs Historical Fife & Drum Corps presents the colors in replica uniforms.

Abner, a Minuteman to his boots, nearly falls out of his chair when he hears about the fife and drums. "Replica uniforms," he says. "Rocco, they're dressing up as my mascot. This is the warmest welcome I've ever gotten in Ohio."

"They're not dressing up as your mascot," Rocco says. "They're honoring veterans. And your mascot is about to get run over by a Jeep."

That's how Rocco talks about football, like a family that has built engines in Toledo for generations. He grades his team in horsepower, and this year the engine is a big one. Toledo is 7-2, 4-1 in the MAC and second in the conference. The Rockets score 35.4 points a game. John Alan Richter has thrown for 2,304 yards with 18 touchdowns and only 3 interceptions. He threw for 429 yards and 4 scores in a 49-48 overtime thriller against Temple, and 391 more against Western Michigan in a 45-38 win.

"Four hundred and twenty-nine," Rocco says. "In one night. That's not a quarterback. That's a V8."

CJ Miller is the other half of the engine, with 744 rushing yards and 7 touchdowns, and he carried 27 times for 135 yards in the 20-17 escape at Sacramento State last week. Adjatay Dabbs is the deep threat with 40 catches for 592 yards and 7 scores. On defense, Andrew Zock has 9.5 sacks off the end and Julian Fox has 73 tackles.

Abner listens politely, the way a farmer listens to a weather report he doesn't plan to follow. UMass is 5-4 and 2-3 in the MAC, and the Minutemen opened the year by beating Rutgers 37-21 on the road. That one still makes him smile. Then came a tough October: a 38-14 loss to Eastern Michigan, a one-point loss to Miami, an overtime loss at Buffalo, and a 35-16 loss at UConn. Then last Wednesday, UMass beat Ball State 31-30 in overtime, and Abner's voice still cracks a little when he talks about it.

"William Watson III," he says. "Seventeen of twenty-five for 302 yards. Two interceptions all season. You know what we call a quarterback like that in the Pioneer Valley? Patient."

Watson has completed 113 of his 163 throws this year. T.Y. Harding leads the receivers with 397 yards, and Kezion Dia-Johnson had 97 yards on just three catches against Ball State. Elijah Faulkner has 400 rushing yards. The defense runs through Timmy Hinspeter, who has 81 tackles, and Joshua Iseah, who has 3.5 sacks.

"Our defense gives up 22.1 a game," Abner says. "Yours gives up 24.4. Write that down, Rocco."

"I wrote it down," Rocco says. "Then I wrote down the last four times we played you."

That's the part Abner would rather skip. Toledo has won all four meetings since 2021: 45-7, 55-10, 41-24 and 38-23. Abner has no explanation for any of them. He has a theory that it's the lake air. Rocco says it's the horsepower.

This is the night I see. The Glass Bowl is packed with veterans and families, and the crowd is ready early. Watson comes out sharp and keeps UMass in it for a quarter, finding Harding on the sideline. Then Toledo's engine turns over. Miller grinds, Richter hits Dabbs, and Zock gets to Watson at least once in a big spot. The Rockets build a cushion by halftime and keep it. UMass scores in the second half to make it a game for a while, but Toledo pulls away.

Abner tips his cap to the veterans on the way out and quietly plans to plant a tree back home in honor of a good fight. Rocco closes the hood on his imaginary engine and says the Rockets are running just fine.

Salute to Service night at the Glass Bowl ends with the Rockets finishing the job. My call: Toledo Rockets 34, Massachusetts Minutemen 19.

There will be barbecue smoke over the parking lots at Raymond James Stadium on Thursday, because USF's Office of Veteran Success is throwing a Sonny's BBQ tailgate for its Salute to Service game, and the visitors come from Memphis, a town that takes its barbecue personally. For this Memphis vs South Florida spread, I'm taking South Florida Bulls +5.5 and the Over 48.5, and my final for the 8:00 PM ET kickoff in Tampa is South Florida Bulls 27, Memphis Tigers 26.

Otis Delaney-Crum checks the menu and shakes his head. "Florida barbecue, Reina. That's brave. Marcus Stokes has 25 touchdown passes and 6 interceptions. He threw for 371 against Army last time out. We score 37.6 a game. Bring more napkins."

Reina Valdés-Kowalski doesn't flinch. "We give up 15.1 a game, Otis. Kent State got 2 points in this stadium. UAB got 10. We're 6-3, and nobody has hung more than 31 on us all year."

The 5.5 is worth grabbing. DraftKings opened Memphis −6 and it has slipped to 5.5, so the early market is on the home side. Both Memphis losses came on the road, 38-20 at Boise State and 31-17 at Tulane, and the Tigers needed overtime to get past East Carolina at home. South Florida lost 20-17 at East Carolina last Friday, the same Pirates team that took Memphis to overtime. My score has the Bulls winning outright, and even a Memphis win by a field goal stays inside the number.

The quarterback question is in Tampa. Michael Van Buren Jr. has 1,273 passing yards and led the throws in seven games, but Luke Kromenhoek took the most throws in each of the last two, and he went 17 of 21 for 179 at East Carolina. I'm pricing Kromenhoek. D.J. Crowther ran for 111 in that game and has 689 on the season, and a ground game that moves the chains keeps Stokes on the sideline.

On the over/under, DraftKings opened at 49.5 and it's down to 48.5, and I'm on the Over 48.5. South Florida games have mostly stayed low, but Memphis has scored 38 or more in six of nine. These two also tend to light it up against each other. Five of the last six regular-season meetings went past 48.5 combined, including 59-50 in 2023 and 34-31 last season. My 27-26 lands on 53.

Three of the four cards with a side take the Bulls. The Formula has Memphis 27-24, likes South Florida Bulls +5.5 and goes Over 48.5. Next Man Up has South Florida 27-26 and likes both the Bulls +5.5 and the Over 48.5. Letdown Watch has it tied 26-26, likes the Bulls +5.5 and likes the Over. In The Trenches likes Memphis Tigers −5.5 and makes no over/under call. Follow The Money is still waiting on a consensus spread, so its side is pending, and it has no total pick.

In The Trenches: "I grade the fronts. The scoreboard can sort itself out."

display.fanatic_story:
"Sonny's," Otis Delaney-Crum says, reading the flyer twice. "In parking lot 6D. With a DJ." He folds it up and puts it in his jacket like evidence. "Reina, you invited a Memphis man to a barbecue in Florida. That's either friendship or a dare."

"It's both," Reina Valdés-Kowalski says. "Welcome to Tampa."

Memphis Tigers vs South Florida Bulls on Thursday night is USF's Salute to Service game at Raymond James Stadium, and the Office of Veteran Success teams up with USF Athletics every year to honor past and present military members. This year that means a Sonny's BBQ tailgate and a DJ out in lot 6D before the 8 p.m. kickoff, and then a stadium full of people saying thank you.

Otis is a blues guitarist who sings bass in his church choir back home, and he already has a slow song chosen for the veterans. Reina used to work the Tampa boat shows and now knows the Bulls roster more closely than her own phone number. She has a pirate flag in her bag, and she'd like to wave it on Thursday.

"Seven and two," Otis says, warming up. "Four and one in the American. Second in the conference. We score 37.6 points a game, Reina. That's not an offense. That's a horn section."

He has the names to back it up. Marcus Stokes has completed 179 of 259 throws for 2,532 yards, 25 touchdowns and 6 interceptions. Against Army on Halloween night, he went 29 of 35 for 371 yards and 4 scores. Jaylin Carter has 929 rushing yards and 10 touchdowns. Hunter Tipton, the tight end, leads the receivers with 495 yards, and Jermane Hayes caught 9 balls for 86 yards and 2 scores against Army. On defense, Elijah Kinsler has 5.5 sacks and Mike Montgomery has 67 tackles.

"Stokes hums," Otis says. "Carter hums along. And Tipton keeps time."

Reina lets him finish the verse. Then she pulls out her own sheet music, and it's mostly defense. South Florida is 6-3 and gives up 15.1 points a game. The Bulls held Kent State to 2 points and Bowling Green to 6. They held UAB to 10 on Halloween afternoon in this same stadium. Nobody has scored more than 31 on them all year.

"You're a horn section," she says. "We're the harbor patrol."

The Bulls do have a question at quarterback, and Reina doesn't hide from it. Michael Van Buren Jr. has 1,273 yards on the season, but Luke Kromenhoek took the most throws in each of the last two games, and he went 17 of 21 for 179 yards and a touchdown at East Carolina. D.J. Crowther ran for 111 yards in that one and has 689 yards and 7 touchdowns this year. Bryson Rodgers leads the receivers with 395 yards. C.J. Hicks has 5 sacks and Ayden Jackson has 50 tackles.

That East Carolina game still bothers her. South Florida lost 20-17 in Greenville last Friday. "Rough waters," she says, then catches herself. "No. That was last week. This week I steer."

Otis can't resist. "East Carolina came to Memphis, too," he says. "We beat them 41-34 in overtime."

"Overtime," Reina says. "You needed overtime against the team we lost to by three. Write that in your songbook."

Then there's the history, and Otis has been waiting all week to sing that part. In the last six regular-season meetings, Memphis won five. The Tigers won 34-33 in 2020, 59-50 in 2023, 21-3 in 2024 and 34-31 last season. South Florida's one win in that stretch was 49-42 back in 2016.

"Five out of six," Otis says, low and slow, like the end of a long blues number. "That's not a rivalry, Reina. That's a residency."

"Last year was by three," Reina says. "And the year before that was in a neutral stadium. Tonight you're in mine."

Fast-forward to Thursday night. The tailgate in 6D runs long and smells great, and Otis admits, quietly, that the sauce is fine. Stokes comes out hot, Carter gets his yards, and Memphis scores early. But the Bulls don't panic. Crowther keeps carrying, Kromenhoek keeps it simple, and the South Florida defense makes Stokes earn every yard after the first quarter. It's close all night, with the lead flipping late, and the Bulls get one more stop than the Tigers do. That's enough.

Reina finally pulls the pirate flag out of her bag and yells "Gasparilla!" loud enough to shake the stands. Otis plays the veterans their slow song anyway, because some things matter more than a scoreboard, then takes one last plate of brisket for the road.

Gasparilla by a hair: how else would Reina want it? My call: South Florida Bulls 27, Memphis Tigers 26.

display.story_text:
Monroe's business crowd has its Thursday night planned. The Monroe Chamber of Commerce is hosting a pregame tailgate at Lou St. Amant Field, the ULM baseball park on Warhawk Way, and the whole thing leads into the in-state rivalry game under the lights. In this Louisiana vs UL Monroe spread, my side is Louisiana Ragin' Cajuns −11.5 with the Over 48.5, and my score is Louisiana Ragin' Cajuns 33, UL Monroe Warhawks 18, kicking off at 9:00 PM ET at Malone Stadium.

Mimi Fontenot has her calculator out before the coin toss. "Darnell, cher, you give up 34.8 points a game. My Cajuns score 29.9. I'm an accountant. That math balances itself."

Darnell Vidrine has heard worse on his overnight radio show. "Two straight wins, Mimi. We beat Troy 21-14 and won at Arkansas State 19-17. The Warhawks are rolling."

The 11.5 doesn't scare me. DraftKings opened Louisiana −10.5 and it has climbed a full point since, so the market agrees. UL Monroe is 2-7 and hasn't won at home this year. Three of those four home losses came by 14 or more, including 45-17 to Florida Atlantic and 24-0 to Louisiana Tech. Both wins came on the road, and the one at Arkansas State came with Aidan Armenta throwing 2 interceptions. That's a team living on turnover luck. Louisiana won three of its six games by more than 11.5, and the Cajuns have won the last three meetings, 52-21, 37-23 and 30-27.

The Louisiana engine is Lunch Winfield. He has 1,599 passing yards and leads the team on the ground with 567 yards and 10 rushing touchdowns. JJ Garner ran for 136 on just 10 carries against South Alabama. On the other side, Armenta has thrown for 1,413 yards with 10 touchdowns and 5 interceptions, and Noah Flemmings has 83 tackles. Quarterback Austin Carlisle leads ULM on the ground with 363 yards, and he ran for 111 at Arkansas State. Jake St. Andre has 69 tackles for Louisiana.

On the over/under, DraftKings opened at 48.5 and it hasn't moved, and I'm on the Over 48.5. UL Monroe games have gone past that number in five of nine. In the last ten meetings, seven went past 48.5, including a 56-50 shootout in 2017 and 70-20 in 2020. My 33-18 lands on 51.

The room is almost unanimous on Louisiana. The Formula has Louisiana 34-19 and likes Louisiana Ragin' Cajuns −11.5 and the Over 48.5. Letdown Watch has 34-18 and likes the Cajuns −11.5 and the Over. Next Man Up has 31-17, takes the Cajuns −11.5 and goes Over 48.5. In The Trenches has no side and no over/under call. Follow The Money is still waiting on a consensus spread, so its side is pending, and it has no total pick.

Next Man Up: "Darnell, I want to like the Warhawks. My card just won't let me."

Darnell: "Your card has never been to Monroe on a Thursday night, Next Man Up."

Mimi taps her calculator and saves Darnell a seat for the drive home. Darnell turns his optimism dial up one more notch, because that's what he does.

Louisiana Ragin' Cajuns 33, UL Monroe Warhawks 18. Louisiana Ragin' Cajuns cover the 11.5. Over 48.5.

display.fanatic_story:
Darnell Vidrine walks in through the home entrance on Thursday night and stops to say hello to Coach James Malone. The football stadium in Monroe has a new name this season, FMOL Health | St. Francis Stadium, but ULM made a promise when it announced the deal in August: an installation honoring Malone, the man the school calls the father of ULM Athletics, goes right at the home entrance. Darnell figures a man who coached the Indians from 1934 to 1953 has seen a few hard years. He figures Malone would tell him to keep showing up.

So he shows up. Louisiana Ragin' Cajuns vs UL Monroe Warhawks is the in-state rivalry game on a Thursday night, and Amélie "Mimi" Fontenot has driven up from Lafayette with her calculator, her dancing shoes and a bag of boudin she says is for emergencies.

"Darnell, mon ami," she says. "Two and seven. I'm an accountant, cher. I can't make that add up for you."

"Mimi," Darnell says, "we've won two in a row. Nobody else in this conference is talking about that, so I will."

He's right about the two wins. UL Monroe beat Troy 21-14 on the road on Oct. 24, then won 19-17 at Arkansas State last Saturday. Darnell hosts an overnight radio show in the Delta, and he spent most of Sunday morning telling his callers about it.

But there's a catch, and Mimi finds it fast. ULM hasn't won a game in the newly named stadium yet. The Warhawks are 0-4 at home, losing 38-35 to Southeastern Louisiana, 45-17 to Florida Atlantic on Homecoming, 24-0 to Louisiana Tech and 35-21 to Southern Miss.

"Thursday is the night," Darnell says. "First home win in the new place. I can feel it in my radio."

Mimi likes her own team's chances a lot more. Louisiana is 6-3 and second in the Sun Belt West, scoring 29.9 points a game. Lunch Winfield does a little bit of everything. He's thrown for 1,599 yards and he leads the team on the ground with 567 yards and 10 rushing touchdowns. Last Saturday against South Alabama, JJ Garner carried 10 times for 136 yards in a 28-26 win. KeDarius Wade leads the receivers with 300 yards, and Jake St. Andre leads the defense with 69 tackles.

"Lunch," Mimi says, "is the best meal of the day and the best quarterback in Louisiana. Laissez les bons temps rouler."

Darnell answers with his own list. Aidan Armenta has thrown for 1,413 yards with 10 touchdowns. Austin Carlisle, the other quarterback, leads the Warhawks on the ground with 363 yards, and he ran 19 times for 111 at Arkansas State. Marcellus Jackson has 35 catches for 370 yards. Noah Flemmings has 83 tackles, and Kevontay Wells has 4 sacks.

"Two quarterbacks," Darnell says. "Twice the hope."

Then Mimi brings out the family history. Louisiana's game page lists 35 wins and 26 losses against ULM all-time, and they've won eight of the last ten meetings, including the last three: 52-21 in 2023, 37-23 in 2024 and 30-27 last year.

Darnell has his own memories ready, because of course he does. ULM won 56-50 in 2017, and the Warhawks won 21-17 in 2022. "I was on the air the whole night in 2017," he says. "I lost my voice in the fourth quarter. Best night of my life."

Down Warhawk Way, the Monroe Chamber of Commerce is throwing its pregame tailgate at Lou St. Amant Field, the baseball park, from 5 p.m. on Mimi wants to go. Darnell has already been twice that afternoon to make sure the grills work.

Play it out. Darnell's crowd is loud early, and ULM hangs around in the first half, with Armenta finding Jackson and Carlisle gaining yards on the ground. But Winfield is too much. He runs, he throws, and Garner breaks a long one in the third quarter. Louisiana pulls away after halftime, and the Cajuns make it four in a row in the rivalry.

Mimi two-steps around the press box with an accordion riff on her phone. Darnell sighs, says "Keep the faith, y'all," and resets his optimism counter right back to the top. Then he stops at the home entrance on the way out and tells Coach Malone they'll get the next one.

Mimi two-steps all night while Darnell resets the counter for next week. My call: Louisiana Ragin' Cajuns 33, UL Monroe Warhawks 18.

display.story_text:
Friday the 13th is Senior Night on the North Shore. Pitt closes its home schedule at Acrisure Stadium with a tribute to its seniors, and the school is calling it a season-ending party. For this Florida State vs Pittsburgh spread, I'm laying Pittsburgh Panthers −3.5, going Under 54.5, and my final is Pittsburgh Panthers 31, Florida State Seminoles 23, for the 7:00 PM ET kickoff.

Gianna Ravello opens like she's in front of a committee in Tallahassee. "Let the minutes show we won at Boston College 31-24 last week. Amari Thomas ran for 98 yards and 2 touchdowns. We score 30.7 a game. I yield nothing."

Dominic "Yinz" Bertolucci blows his homemade whistle. "Yinz score 30.7 and give up 28.3, Gianna. We give up 19.8. Damon Ferguson Jr. ran 31 times for 185 against Georgia Tech. That's how you close a game, n'at."

Laying the 3.5 comes down to a few things. DraftKings opened Pitt −3 and it has moved to 3.5, so the market came my way. Pitt is 5-1 at home, and the only loss on this field was 21-17 to North Carolina. Florida State is 1-3 on the road, with losses at Alabama, Louisville and Miami. Ashton Daniels has 2,146 passing yards and 14 touchdowns, but he's also thrown 12 interceptions, and Cruce Brookins has 61 tackles for a Pitt defense that allows 19.8. Pitt beat the Seminoles 34-31 last season.

The Pitt quarterback picture has changed. Mason Heintschel had 14 touchdowns and 1 interception and took the most throws in the first five games. display.fanatic_story:
Some people stay home on Friday the 13th. Dominic "Yinz" Bertolucci is going to a party on the North Shore. Pitt's last home game of the year is Senior Night at Acrisure Stadium, a Friday night tribute to the seniors, and the school promised fans a season-ending party. Yinz has his homemade whistle, a gold Pitt scarf and a seat close enough to hear the seniors' names called.

Gianna Ravello flew up from Tallahassee anyway. She doesn't trust bad luck. She trusts procedure.

"I'd like to enter something into the minutes," she says as she sits down. "Florida State won at Boston College last Saturday, 31-24. Amari Thomas ran for 98 yards and 2 touchdowns. The motion to feel good about ourselves is on the floor."

"Seconded by nobody," Yinz says. "How's it goin', n'at? Welcome to Pittsburgh."

Florida State is 4-5 and 10th in the ACC, and Gianna knows it has been a bumpy year. The Seminoles lost 27-24 to SMU, 50-36 at Alabama, 44-20 at Louisville, 43-35 in overtime at Miami and 36-24 to Clemson. But the wins have been loud. They beat Virginia 38-7, and they scored 30.7 points a game across nine games.

Ashton Daniels does a lot of the talking. He's thrown for 2,146 yards and 14 touchdowns, with 12 interceptions. He threw for 377 at Alabama and 350 against Clemson, and he had 4 touchdown throws at Miami. Ousmane Kromah has 609 rushing yards, and Micahi Danzy leads the receivers with 487 yards and caught 7 balls for 86 at Boston College. On defense, Rylan Kennedy has 6 sacks and Chris Jones has 64 tackles.

"The Daniels administration," Gianna says, "has a strong economy and a few scandals. Every administration does."

Yinz grades it all with his whistle. Pitt is 6-3, 5-1 at home and allows 19.8 points a game. The only team to win on this field this season was North Carolina, 21-17. Pitt opened the year by beating Miami (OH) 59-14 and Bucknell 59-0, and Mason Heintschel threw 7 touchdowns in that first game. He has 14 touchdown throws and only 1 interception this year. Holden Geriner has taken the most throws in three of the last four games, and he threw for 180 and a touchdown against Georgia Tech.

But Yinz's best part of that night was on the ground. Damon Ferguson Jr. carried 31 times for 185 yards and 2 touchdowns in the 34-11 win.

"Thirty-one carries," Yinz says, and blows the whistle twice. "That's not a running back, Gianna. That's a steel mill."

Ferguson has 662 rushing yards this year. Cataurus Hicks has 698 receiving yards and 6 touchdowns. Cruce Brookins leads the defense with 61 tackles, and Jaeden Moore has 4.5 sacks.

Then Yinz brings up last year. Pitt beat Florida State 34-31. Before that, the Seminoles won 24-7 in 2023, and Pitt won 41-17 in 2020.

"Two out of three," Yinz says. "I'd call that a mandate."

"That's my word," Gianna says. "You can't use my word."

"I just did. Filibuster me."

She tries. She talks for almost a full minute about Danzy's route tree, the Seminoles' defensive front and the history of the Sunshine State. Yinz waits her out, then hands her a pierogi from the tailgate on the North Shore.

Run the tape forward. The seniors get their moment before kickoff, and the crowd is loud from the first snap. Daniels hits a couple of big throws early, and Florida State hangs around into the third quarter. But Pitt keeps handing it to Ferguson, and the Seminoles spend the second half chasing him. Brookins and the Pitt defense take one ball away from Daniels late, and Pitt's seniors walk off the field winners on their last night at home.

Yinz jumps up and yells "Yinz SEE that?!" so loud the guy running the scoreboard flinches. Gianna quietly drafts emergency legislation to fix the secondary and promises to bring it to a vote in Tallahassee.

Friday the 13th turns lucky on the North Shore. My call: Pittsburgh Panthers 31, Florida State Seminoles 23.

display.fanatic_story:
Kensington "Kenzie" Rhee has the whole night storyboarded, and she's proudest of the halftime shot: the U.S. Army Golden Knights dropping out of the sky over the Rose Bowl, parachutes open, landing on the field in the middle of UCLA's annual Salute to Service game.

"Act two opens in the air," she tells Margery Vandermolen. "Nobody's ever seen a cold open like that."

"Kenzie, they do it at a lot of games," Margery says. "But I'll admit it's a good one."

Illinois Fighting Illini vs UCLA Bruins is a Friday night game in Pasadena, kicking off at 6 p.m. local time, and UCLA has packed the day with extras. The Bruin Walk begins outside Gate A at 3:20 p.m., with the UCLA Marching Band and Spirit Squad welcoming Coach Chesney and the team. The Sierra Winds from the U.S. Air Force Band of the Golden West perform the national anthem. UCLA will present its 2026 Veteran of the Year award during the game, and Operation Mend will be recognized too.

Then there's the giveaway Margery can't stop thinking about. Two lucky UCLA students will each win one quarter of in-state tuition, but only if they check in and stay for the whole game.

"That's the most effective attendance policy I've ever seen," says Margery, who grew up in Champaign-Urbana with an ag-economics professor for a dad. "I'm taking notes for my own classroom."

Kenzie has a bigger story to tell. UCLA is 9-0, 6-0 in the Big Ten and first in the conference. The Bruins score 33.6 points a game and give up only 14.1. They won 17-15 at Oregon, shut out Nevada 27-0 and beat Minnesota 34-20 on the road last Saturday.

"Nine episodes," Kenzie says. "Nine happy endings. The network's already ordered another season."

Her lead actor might be a running back. Wayne Knight has 789 rushing yards and 13 touchdowns, and he ran 18 times for 109 yards at Minnesota. Ty Dieffenbach has taken the most throws in each of the last four games, and against the Gophers he completed just 8 throws for 303 yards and 3 touchdowns. Aidan Mizell caught 2 of them for 150 yards and 2 scores. Semaj Morgan leads the receivers with 469 yards. On defense, Jalen Woods has 73 tackles and Sammy Omosigho has 5.5 sacks.

"Eight completions, 303 yards," Kenzie says. "That's not a quarterback. That's a highlight reel with a helmet."

Margery pulls out a chart, because of course she does. It's orange, with corn stalks drawn in the margins.

"Illinois is 6-3 and third in the Big Ten," she says, pointing. "We've won four in a row. We beat Michigan State 38-37 in overtime. We beat Oregon 21-10 at home. You beat Oregon by two. I've crunched the numbers, and the numbers say orange."

Margery's headliner is Collin Dixon. He has 68 catches for 910 yards and 12 touchdowns, and he caught 8 balls for 129 yards and 2 scores against Nebraska last Friday. Katin Houser has thrown for 1,955 yards with 16 touchdowns and only 5 interceptions, and he threw for 292 and 3 touchdowns in that 24-13 win. Aidan Laughery leads the runners with 615 yards, and Matthew Bailey leads the defense with 65 tackles.

"Dixon," Margery says, "is what happens when you plant good seed and wait."

Kenzie laughs. "That's a corn joke."

"Every joke in Illinois is a corn joke. It's state law."

The two teams haven't played each other in the regular season in the last ten years, so there's no rerun to watch. Kenzie says that's fine. She likes originals.

Kenzie's storyboard reads like this. The Rose Bowl is loud from the Bruin Walk on, and UCLA scores first behind Knight. Houser and Dixon answer, and Illinois keeps it close into halftime. The Golden Knights land, the crowd goes wild, and the Bruins come out of the break with more energy. Dieffenbach hits one deep shot in the third quarter, Knight grinds out the clock, and Illinois scores late to make it respectable. UCLA stays unbeaten.

Kenzie snaps her clapboard and yells, "And... scene! That's a wrap!" Margery adds one more row to her chart, writes "next time" in orange, and asks if the Golden Knights give lessons.

Kenzie gets her Golden Knights shot, and the Bruins give her an ending worth keeping. My call: UCLA Bruins 29, Illinois Fighting Illini 20.

Friday night at Folsom Field is a Buffs Wear Black game, and Moss takes a dress code seriously when he agrees with it. He also has a thermos of kombucha and a good seat for the halftime drone show. Houston Cougars vs Colorado Buffaloes kicks off at 8:15 p.m. in Boulder, which makes it a school night for a lot of people. CU says classes won't be canceled, you'll need a Buff OneCard to get into the academic buildings, and the Earth Sciences and Map Library closes at 2 p.m. Moss thinks that's the most Boulder sentence ever written.

At halftime, Colorado and the Colorado Tourism Office are putting on a drone show over the stadium. Yolanda "Yo" Pacheco can't wait.

"Drones," she says. "Moss, I'm from Space City. We put people on the moon. You're putting lights in the sky and calling it a show."

"It is a show," Moss says. "It's very chill. You'll like it."

Yo is not chill. Yo has been counting down to kickoff since Monday. Houston is 7-2 and third in the Big 12, scoring 35.4 points a game. The Cougars beat Cincinnati 31-24 last Saturday, and Re'Shaun Sanford II carried 15 times for 126 yards and a touchdown. Amare Thomas caught 6 balls for 78 yards and 2 scores.

Then there's Conner Weigman. He's completed 170 of 257 throws for 2,280 yards with 22 touchdowns and only 2 interceptions. He threw 5 touchdowns against Oklahoma State and 4 each against Georgia Southern and Kansas State.

"Two interceptions in nine games," Yo says. "That's not a quarterback. That's mission control."

Thomas leads the receivers with 698 yards and 8 touchdowns, and Makhi Hughes leads the runners with 606 yards. Kentrell Webb has 50 tackles, and Ashton Porter has 3 sacks.

Moss nods slowly, like he's listening to a song he already knows. Colorado is 3-6 and 14th in the Big 12, and he's not going to pretend otherwise. The Buffs score 19.8 points a game and give up 28.3. They lost 41-7 at Northwestern and 57-24 at Oklahoma State. But then, a week after Stillwater, they beat Kansas State 27-24 in overtime right here on Halloween.

"That's the thing about us," Moss says. "You never know which Buffs show up. Honestly, neither do we. It keeps things interesting."

Isaac Wilson has taken the most throws in each of the last six games and has 1,412 yards with 8 touchdowns. Joseph Williams is his go-to target, though Moss doesn't like ranking his friends. Williams has 58 catches for 853 yards and 6 touchdowns, and he caught 7 balls for 121 yards at Arizona State last week. JaQuail Smith leads the runners with 384 yards.

And then there's Gideon Lampron. The linebacker has 99 tackles and 5.5 sacks.

"Ninety-nine," Moss says, and for a second he sounds almost excited. "Gideon is a whole mountain range."

The two teams met last season, and Houston won 36-20. Yo remembers. Moss says he was at a yoga retreat and only heard about it later, which was probably for the best.

Picture Friday night. Folsom Field is black from top to bottom, and the Buffs come out loud. Lampron makes a big stop early, and Colorado hangs in through halftime. The drones light up the sky, and even Yo admits it's pretty cool. But Weigman settles in after the break. He finds Thomas for one touchdown, Sanford grinds out the clock, and Houston pulls away late. Colorado scores in the fourth quarter to keep it respectable.

Yo jumps up and yells, "Houston, we have a WIN!" loud enough to scare a drone. Moss shrugs, says, "It's all good, man," and quietly opens his laptop in the hammock to re-run the model.

Yo is still yelling when the drones go dark over Folsom Field. My call: Houston Cougars 28, Colorado Buffaloes 20.

display.fanatic_story:
Cincinnati Bearcats vs Iowa State Cyclones is an 11 a.m. Central kickoff at Jack Trice Stadium on Saturday, and the sharpest people in Ames will have eaten long before the band warms up. The Iowa State Department of Animal Science throws open the Hansen Agriculture Learning Center on Mortensen Road for its annual Chuckwagon Breakfast from 8 to 10 that morning, free omelets, pastries, coffee and juice, and Cyclones storm-spotter Twyla Hemmingsen plans to be there at the bell, right before Cincinnati's Lionel "Skyline" Abernathy strolls in asking whether anybody has ever tried chili on eggs.

Twyla: Free eggs, free coffee, and a noon kickoff. This is civilization.

Skyline: In Cincinnati we respect them so much we stack them three high. That isn't breakfast. That's a game plan.

He's half right, because both of these teams show up hungry. Cincinnati is 5-4 after a 24-31 loss at Houston. Iowa State is 4-5 after a 31-42 loss at Baylor. Both sit at 2-4 in Big 12 play, and both know the difference between a winter of bowl prep and a winter of film-room regret is about three Saturdays long.

Twyla: Here's my read on the sky over Ames. Cardinal and gold blowing in early, then steady pressure from Aiden Flora all afternoon.

Flora is the reason she says it with a straight face. The Iowa State back has 1,119 yards and nine touchdowns on 157 carries, and he just went for 182 yards on 26 carries in Waco. When he gets downhill, the whole stadium rises with him, and the Cyclones get to play the way Ames likes it, heavy and patient and mean.

Skyline answers with JC French IV. French has carried Cincinnati with his arm all fall, 1,990 throwing yards with 15 touchdowns and only three interceptions. He threw for 389 yards and three scores in a 45-42 loss at West Virginia and put up four touchdown throws in the 37-24 win over Texas Tech. Behind him, Cole Tabb has 812 rushing yards and 10 touchdowns on just 91 carries, which is the kind of efficiency that makes a defensive coordinator stop eating his breakfast halfway through.

Skyline: I hear you. I just think the loudest day in this series was last October in Cincinnati, when we won 38-30 at Nippert. Thirteen months later, we get to see whether Ames can answer.

Twyla: Answer? Flora already answered Baylor. He'll answer you too.

The key matchup lives in the middle of the field. Iowa State linebacker Sullivan Schlimgen has 84 tackles and spends most Saturdays arriving at the ball carrier like he was mailed there overnight. Cincinnati's Jonathan Thompson has 66 tackles of his own, and Patrick Bauer has 3.5 sacks off the outside. Neither defense has been airtight. Cincinnati allows 29.4 points a game and Iowa State allows 28.9, so the team that gets the first two stops in a row probably gets to dictate the afternoon.

Skyline: Here's the Cincinnati recipe. French moves it around early, Tabb hits you late, and JV Gibson catches the third-down ball when your safeties get greedy.

Twyla: Here's the Ames recipe. Flora on first down, Flora on second down, and Raynor on third down when your linebackers are still out of breath. This is a farm town. We know how to wait for a harvest, and the fourth quarter is harvest.

Saturday's Ames calendar is crowded. The City of Ames runs a free yard-waste drop-off for leaves and grass out on 500th Avenue from 8 to 4, so plenty of locals will rake the front yard at dawn, haul the bags, grab an omelet at Hansen, and still make kickoff in Cyclone colors. That is a full Iowa Saturday, and it ends at Jack Trice with the leaves off the lawn and a Big 12 game that stays one possession deep into the fourth.

Skyline will talk chili. Twyla will talk Flora. The rest of Ames will talk about whether the omelets were better than last year.

Eat the omelet early, Ames. Nobody keeps breakfast down in a fourth quarter like this one. My call: Iowa State Cyclones 30, Cincinnati Bearcats 28.

Even after a 24-31 loss at Notre Dame, this offense is still built to clear 30.

Duke Blue Devils vs Miami Hurricanes lands on Homecoming Saturday at Hard Rock Stadium, presented by The Islands of the Bahamas, and the Law Alumni Association and Student Bar Association are already planning a 10 a.m. tailgate in the parking lots before the noon kickoff. Javi "The Breeze" Castillo is already working the parking lots in orange, talking like the alumni bus never left. Harrison Wexley-Moore IV arrives with a notebook and a warning about Nate Sheppard.

Javi: Homecoming means everybody comes home. Mensah, Toney, Fletcher. The whole catalog.

Harrison: Sheppard just ran for 217 yards and three scores at NC State. Your catalog has a new chapter if you ignore him.

Miami is 8-1 and ranked No. 1 after a 24-31 loss at Notre Dame last Saturday. Duke is 7-2 after that 41-3 road win in Raleigh. The Canes still score 45.0 points a game. The Blue Devils allow 13.0. That is the collision at the heart of this afternoon: the highest-scoring offense in this building against the stingiest defense on the visiting sideline.

Darian Mensah has thrown for 2,694 yards with 28 touchdowns and two interceptions. Malachi Toney has 73 catches for 1,027 yards and 13 scores. Mark Fletcher Jr. has nine rushing touchdowns. Miami put 52 on Pittsburgh and 43 on Florida State in overtime. Even the Notre Dame loss featured a Canes offense that kept answering until the clock ran out. When Mensah gets into a rhythm, Hard Rock starts sounding like a place that forgot what a three-and-out feels like.

Duke's answer is the ground game. Nate Sheppard has 1,189 yards and 17 touchdowns on 191 carries. Walker Eget has 1,849 passing yards with 10 touchdowns and three interceptions. Jonah Burton leads the receivers with 360 yards. The Blue Devils scored 47 against Boston College and 41 at NC State. When Sheppard finds the corner, the whole Duke offense starts looking like a team that belongs in this conversation, and the last two Saturdays say he has found it.

Harrison: We don't need 45 points. We need stops, and we've been getting them all year. Thirteen points allowed a game is not an accident.

Javi: Stops against Toney? Good luck. He already has more touchdowns than some teams have wins. Homecoming is not a day for polite defense.

Marquise Lightfoot has 7 sacks for Miami. Mohamed Toure has 56 tackles. Duke's Kevin O'Connor has 4.5 sacks, and Nick Morris Jr. has 51 tackles. Both fronts can wreck a drive. The difference is what happens when the drive doesn't get wrecked. Miami has spent all fall turning those into 35-point afternoons. Duke has spent all fall turning those into field-position wars. One of those habits is about to meet the other in front of a Homecoming crowd that paid for noise.

Coral Gables residents even get a ticket offer for this game through the city's development agreement with the university, which is the kind of Homecoming detail that tells you the whole metro is treating Saturday like a reunion. Hard Rock will be loud. The alumni will be louder. The Canes will try to make the scoreboard the loudest thing of all.

Javi will talk touchdowns. Harrison will talk Sheppard. Homecoming will talk about who came back, and whether the Canes remembered how to finish after South Bend.

The last time these programs shared a November stage with this much at stake, the conversation was about whether Duke could travel and whether Miami could finish. This week the conversation is simpler. Miami wants Homecoming to feel like a reset after South Bend. Duke wants Hard Rock to feel like Carter-Finley did last Saturday, when Sheppard ran through arm tackles and the Blue Devils left town with a statement win. One of those wishes will survive the fourth quarter. The other will end up as a story the alumni tell on the walk back to the cars.

Javi keeps pointing at the 28 touchdown passes. Harrison keeps pointing at the 13 points allowed. Hard Rock will decide which number mattered more before the sun gets low over Miami Gardens.

Homecoming at Hard Rock ends with the Canes dancing. My call: Miami Hurricanes 35, Duke Blue Devils 21.

display.fanatic_story:
Syracuse Orange vs NC State Wolfpack is Senior Day at Carter-Finley Stadium, a noon kickoff in Raleigh for two teams sitting at 4-5 with November running out of Saturdays. Rutherford "Ruff" Pegram has his red on before breakfast, talking about seniors like they already own the building. Nico Calabrese speaks for Syracuse with a note about Umari Hatcher and a warning that Senior Day does not scare road receivers.

Ruff: These seniors have been through every kind of Saturday. Bailey still has the arm. Aguirre still has the tackles. The rest is noise.

Nico: Hatcher has 964 yards. Angeli just threw for 263 against Clemson. Your noise has to shadow him for four quarters.

NC State is coming off a 3-41 loss to Duke that emptied the building early. Syracuse is coming off a 13-18 loss to Clemson that stayed one score deep into the fourth. Those are two different kinds of pain. One needs a response. The other needs a finish. Senior Day is a good day for both arguments, and Carter-Finley will hear both of them.

CJ Bailey has thrown for 2,078 yards with 13 touchdowns and four interceptions. Keenan Jackson has 477 receiving yards and six scores. Davion Gause leads the rushers with 378 yards. The Wolfpack score 28.9 points a game and allow 27.6, which is the profile of a team that lives in one-possession games and hates when the script gets away from it the way it did against Duke.

Syracuse rides Hatcher's 62 catches and Steve Angeli's 1,450 yards with eight touchdowns. Tylik Hill has 531 rushing yards. The Orange score 29.3 and allow 25.4. Keyshawn Johnson has 7 sacks. Chris D'Appolonia has 62 tackles. When Syracuse keeps the game in the phone booth, it looks like the team that took Clemson to the wire. When it doesn't, Hatcher ends up making contested catches while the clock gets rude.

Nico: We don't need a track meet. We need Hatcher on third down and one more stop than we got last week.

Ruff: Senior Day is not a track meet. It's a reunion with shoulder pads. Bailey will throw it, Aguirre will hit somebody, and the seniors will walk off knowing they got one more Saturday in this building.

Popo Aguirre's 84 tackles are the kind of number that shows up in the fourth quarter. Elijah Satchell has 5 sacks for the Wolfpack. The front seven can shorten a game if the offense stays on schedule. That is the Senior Day recipe Raleigh wants: first downs, tackles for loss, and a send-off that does not end with the visitors celebrating on the logo.

Raleigh will treat noon like a holiday for the seniors. Syracuse will treat it like a road game that can still save a season. One of those moods usually wins in November.

Senior Day always carries two clocks. One is the game clock. The other is the career clock for players who will not get another noon in this stadium. Bailey has spent the year answering both. Angeli has spent the year trying to steal the first one. Hatcher has spent the year making sure the second one never feels settled when he is on the field.

Raleigh knows how to throw a send-off. The question is whether the Wolfpack offense can turn that energy into first downs before Syracuse turns it into a road steal. One stop in the fourth quarter will probably decide which speech the seniors get to give afterward.

Ruff will talk about the seniors. Nico will talk about Hatcher. Carter-Finley will talk about whether 4-5 still has a path worth chasing.

A send-off that goes to the final minute? Raleigh wouldn't take any other kind. My call: NC State Wolfpack 28, Syracuse Orange 26.

Wake Forest at SMU kicks off at noon ET on the Hilltop, a few hours after the Homecoming parade rolls down Bishop Boulevard and on the same morning SMU asks its whole crowd to wear blue for Senior Day. My Wake Forest vs SMU prediction is the visitors in a close one: Wake Forest Demon Deacons 30, SMU Mustangs 28, with Wake Forest Demon Deacons −1.5 and Under 61.5.

Eloise Brightman-Rowe, the Wake insider, packed the black and gold and a framed photo of last October. "Thirteen to twelve, on a walk-off kick. Gio Lopez has 18 touchdowns and one interception, and our defense gives up 15.9 points a game." Tatum Delacroix-Price answers from the Boulevard. "Kevin Jennings has 25 touchdowns. We're 7-2, it's Homecoming, and you're in our house."

The market has already run toward SMU. DraftKings opened Wake Forest −3.5 with 55.5 on the over/under, and the number had come down to −1.5 and 61.5 by Monday morning. I'll take the cheaper price on the better team. Wake is 8-1, scores 43.3 a game and allows 15.9. Its only loss was 33-20 to Miami. SMU is a good team, 7-2 and 6-0 at home, so this is no walkover, and that's exactly why I want the short number instead of the 3.5 that opened. Lopez has protected the ball all season, and that matters on a parade morning when the home crowd wants a turnover to explode on.

The Under is the six-point jump. The over/under climbed from 55.5 to 61.5 without a reason I can find in the box scores. Wake has held seven of nine opponents to 27 or fewer, and SMU's defense allows 22.9. My 58 sits clear of 61.5, and a two-point Wake win clears the 1.5.

The room mostly agrees with me on the over/under and splits on the side. The Formula has Wake Forest Demon Deacons −1.5 and likes Under 61.5, with Wake 30-27. Next Man Up has Wake Forest Demon Deacons −1.5 and Under 61.5 too, at 32-29. Letdown Watch takes SMU Mustangs +1.5 and likes Under 61.5. In The Trenches has no side this week and makes no over/under call. Follow The Money is still waiting on a consensus spread, so its side is pending, and it has no total pick.

Next Man Up to Letdown Watch: "You picked the parade over the 8-1 team? Enjoy the float." Letdown Watch: "I picked Homecoming. Ask the last Deacons team that played in Dallas how that went."

Tatum gets the parade, the choir and a stadium full of blue. Eloise gets Lopez on third down and one more trip home with a story.

Wake Forest Demon Deacons 30, SMU Mustangs 28. Wake Forest Demon Deacons cover the 1.5. Under 61.5.

display.fanatic_story:
Wake Forest Demon Deacons vs SMU Mustangs lands on SMU's Homecoming Saturday in Dallas, and the Hilltop will be wide awake long before the 11 a.m. Central kickoff at Gerald J. Ford Stadium. The Student Foundation's Homecoming parade rolls down Bishop Boulevard at 8, a church choir from St. Luke's Community United Methodist sings on the steps of Perkins Chapel when it ends, and SMU's Tatum Delacroix-Price has already informed Wake Forest's Eloise Brightman-Rowe that the dress code is blue, because the Mustangs asked the whole crowd to wear it.

Tatum: Homecoming, Senior Day and Wear Blue on the same Saturday, Eloise. That isn't a football game. That's a full production with a parade for an overture.

Eloise: A parade, a choir and a dress code. Very Dallas. I brought black and gold, and a very long memory.

The memory is fresh for both of them. These programs had not met in 50 years when they finally played again last October in Winston-Salem, and it ended the way Eloise likes her debates, with the last word. Connor Calvert drilled a 50-yard field goal as time ran out, and Wake Forest won 13-12. Saturday is only the fifth meeting ever, and the first one at SMU since the 1972 season.

Tatum: Thirteen to twelve. You won by one swing of one leg, and you've talked about it for a year.

Eloise: Fifty yards, Tatum. Walk-off. I had the photo framed for the dorm.

Wake Forest earned the swagger it's carrying to Texas. The Deacons are 8-1 and ranked 16th, and the only blemish came in a 33-20 loss to Miami back in September. Gio Lopez has thrown for 2,176 yards with 18 touchdowns and one interception, which is the kind of ball security that makes a coach sleep through the night. Carlos Hernandez has 61 catches for 945 yards, and Ty Clark III has eight rushing touchdowns. The defense is the part nobody in Dallas should skip, though. Wake allows 15.9 points a game, Langston Hardy has 5.5 sacks, and linebacker Vincent Firenze leads the team with 53 tackles.

Eloise: We beat Louisville, NC State and Cal on the road. Your Boulevard is a heck of a tailgate, Tatum, but it isn't the scariest place we've played.

Tatum: Say that again after Kevin Jennings is done with you.

SMU's quarterback is the reason the Boulevard tents fill up early. Jennings has 2,764 throwing yards and 25 touchdowns, and last Friday he threw for 350 yards and four scores in a 51-28 win over Virginia Tech. Yamir Knight caught three of those touchdowns. Kendrick Raphael has 755 rushing yards and 10 touchdowns, and Marques White has 7.5 sacks coming off the end of the SMU front. The Mustangs are 7-2, and both losses came on the road, 41-31 at Louisville and 30-27 at Syracuse. At home this fall they are 6-0, and they haven't given away a thing.

Tatum: It's Senior Day, Eloise, in front of a stadium full of blue. You want to walk into that and try another 50-yarder?

Eloise: I'd rather not need one. Lopez against your secondary on third down is where I'd like to settle this, quietly and early.

That's the heart of the afternoon. Wake Forest has allowed more than 27 points only twice all season, and SMU has scored at least 23 in every game. Whoever wins the third downs in the first half probably gets to play the second half the way it wants, Wake with Clark grinding the clock or SMU with Jennings throwing deep into a loud Homecoming crowd.

The weekend in University Park doesn't stop at the stadium. The Class of 1991 has its reunion tailgate on the Boulevard after the game, near Armstrong Fieldhouse, and somebody there will be telling a Pony Express story before the band packs up.

Tatum: If we win, I'm declaring the Boulevard officially iconic. Again.

Eloise: If we win, I'm rolling the Quad when the plane lands and dedicating every roll to you.

Tatum: Bring me a blue one.

Eloise: Only if you can find a field goal kicker who wants to beat us twice.

The Hilltop gets its parade in the morning. The Deacons get the afternoon. My call: Wake Forest Demon Deacons 30, SMU Mustangs 28.

display.story_text:
Wisconsin at Maryland is the Terps' Military Appreciation Day, a noon ET kickoff at SECU Stadium with a commemorative giveaway at the gates and the College Park Farmers Market smoking brisket on Campus Drive that morning. My Wisconsin vs Maryland prediction respects the Badgers and still takes the points: Wisconsin Badgers 27, Maryland Terrapins 20, with Maryland Terrapins +8.5 and Over 43.5.

Lars "Brat" Ellefson brought cheese curds and a grudge. "You beat us 27-10 in Madison last year. We're 6-3, third in the Big Ten, and we allow 16.3 points a game." Abby Chesapeake has her camo beanie on and her Old Bay ready. "Malik Washington has 2,058 throwing yards. Chris Durr Jr. has 765 receiving yards. And we just won 34-29 at Purdue."

The price is the story here. DraftKings opened Wisconsin −7.5 and has moved to −8.5, with 43.5 on the over/under unchanged. That's a lot of points for an offense that scores 24.4 a game and has a quarterback question. Colton Joseph leads the team in throwing yards, but Ryan Hopkins had the most attempts in the 31-10 win over Rutgers. A Wisconsin team that grinds the clock is great for a Badgers win and tough for laying more than a touchdown. I have Wisconsin by seven, short of the 8.5.

Maryland has lost close games all season, 37-30 to Rutgers and 20-17 to Illinois, and it beat Wisconsin by 17 the last time these two met. The Terps don't need to win. They need to stay within two scores on a day the home crowd shows up for something bigger than football.

The Over feels backward with Wisconsin's defense, but the Maryland side of it carries the total. The Terps allow 31.3 points a game and score 27.7. Wisconsin put up 31 on Rutgers last week. My 47 clears 43.5, and that only needs a normal Maryland afternoon from Washington and Durr.

The room tilts toward Maryland more than you might guess. The Formula has Maryland Terrapins +8.5 and likes Over 43.5, with Wisconsin 29-21. Next Man Up has Maryland Terrapins +8.5 too but goes Under 43.5 at 25-18. Letdown Watch likes Wisconsin Badgers −8.5 and likes Over 43.5, 29-17. In The Trenches likes Maryland Terrapins +8.5 and makes no over/under call. Follow The Money is still waiting on a consensus spread, so its side is pending, and it has no total pick.

Letdown Watch to Next Man Up: "Twenty-five to eighteen? That's a crab feast without the crabs." Next Man Up: "And twenty-nine to seventeen is a brisket platter with no brisket. Sit down."

Abby gets a close game in front of a camo crowd. Brat gets a win and an argument about the margin all the way back to Madison.

Wisconsin Badgers 27, Maryland Terrapins 20. Maryland Terrapins cover the 8.5. Over 43.5.
