display.fanatic_story:
Wisconsin Badgers vs Maryland Terrapins is Military Appreciation Day at SECU Stadium, a noon kickoff in College Park where the first 10,000 fans through the gates get a commemorative giveaway and the Terps honor active duty and veteran service members during the game. Maryland's Abby Chesapeake will be there early in a camo Terps beanie, and Wisconsin's Lars "Brat" Ellefson will be there earlier, because somebody told him the College Park Farmers Market on Campus Drive opens at 8 and the JetSet BBQ truck is bringing brisket.

Abby: You came for the brisket, Lars. Be honest.

Brat: I came for the brisket and the rematch. Mostly the rematch. A little bit the brisket.

The rematch is why Abby has been smiling since the schedule came out. Last September, Maryland went to Madison and won 27-10, and Saturday is the first time Wisconsin has played in College Park since 2015. For Abby, that is a two-game sweep waiting to happen. For Brat, it is a debt with a due date.

Abby: Twenty-seven to ten at Camp Randall. I sprinkled Old Bay on the box score and had it laminated.

Brat: You can keep the lamination. We kept the conference race.

He has a point. Wisconsin is 6-3, sits third in the Big Ten, and plays a style that hasn't changed much since Brat was a Badger fullback himself. The Badgers allow 16.3 points a game. Sebastian Cheeks has seven sacks, and linebacker Cooper Catalano has 89 tackles, which is about what you'd expect from a man who looks like he was raised on cheese curds and film study. The offense is the question. Colton Joseph leads the team in throwing and rushing, but Ryan Hopkins took most of the snaps in last week's 31-10 win over Rutgers and threw for 241 yards and three touchdowns on 18-of-24.

Brat: Whoever's under center, we're going to run it, hit you, and run it again. You know that. Everybody in the Big Ten knows that.

Abby: Everybody also remembers the 30-0 afternoon at Iowa. Running it again didn't do much that day.

Maryland's case comes with a little more fizz. The Terps are 3-6, but they just won 34-29 at Purdue, and Malik Washington has thrown for 2,058 yards with 11 touchdowns. Chris Durr Jr. has 62 catches for 765 yards and caught four balls for 127 yards in West Lafayette. DeJuan Williams ran for 99 yards and a score in that game, and when Maryland gets him going, Washington gets to throw with room. On defense, Zion Elee has six sacks and Daniel Wingate leads the team with 55 tackles.

Abby: We've lost some close ones. Seven points to Rutgers, three to Illinois. This is a team that's been knocking on the door all fall.

Brat: You've also given up 31.3 points a game. Knocking on the door is great until the door is a Wisconsin fullback.

This is the matchup in one sentence: a Wisconsin team that wants every drive to take forever against a Maryland team that would love to make the game feel quick. If the Badgers own the clock, Abby spends the fourth quarter staring at the scoreboard and doing arithmetic. If Washington hits Durr early, the stadium wakes up and the Terps get to play from in front for once.

The day itself belongs to the people being honored. Maryland Athletics is donating two tickets to military members and veterans for every ticket sold in the special beanie package, so plenty of the folks in camo on Saturday will be guests of the program. Both insiders agree that's the best part of the afternoon, and neither one is joking about it.

Brat: That's the one thing nobody argues about. We stand, we clap, and then we go back to hitting each other.

Abby: Then you go back to the farmers market for a second plate of brisket.

Terpsville Fan Fest opens inside the Jones-Hill House practice facility before kickoff, with inflatables, face painting and lawn games for the kids, and Abby has already promised to beat Brat at cornhole. He has already promised to let her.

Brat: I'll be gracious on the cornhole board. On the field I'm bringing a Wisconsin fourth quarter.

Abby: Bring it. Just remember who's holding the mallet when the crabs come out.

Bring the mallet, Abby. You'll need something to take it out on. My call: Wisconsin Badgers 27, Maryland Terrapins 20.

Northwestern at Ohio State is the Military Appreciation Game at Ohio Stadium, presented through the Our Honor Defend program, with a noon kickoff on FOX a week after both teams lost. My Northwestern vs Ohio State prediction is Ohio State Buckeyes 30, Northwestern Wildcats 19, with Northwestern Wildcats +11.5 and Over 47.5.

Brecken "Buck" Holloway, the Buckeyes insider, talks like the band already started. "Julian Sayin has 19 touchdowns. Jeremiah Smith has 1,200 yards. Military Appreciation does not do soft scripts." Ezra Lindqvist, Northwestern's insider, answers with Aidan Chiles. "1,898 yards and one interception. We just played Iowa tough. Your number is still too wide."

The market moved toward Ohio State. DraftKings opened Ohio State −9.5 with 48.5 on the over/under, and it climbed to −11.5 and 47.5. I still want the points on Northwestern. Ohio State is 6-3 after a 28-41 loss to Oregon. Northwestern is coming off a 10-24 loss to Iowa. The Buckeyes score 35.7 a game. The Wildcats allow 19.3. That gap is real, but 11.5 points after an Ohio State loss is a number I will take on a road dog that keeps games ugly.

Sayin has 2,007 passing yards. Smith has 69 catches for 14 scores. Bo Jackson has 685 rushing yards. Ohio State still looks like a top-shelf offense on the weeks it finishes drives. Northwestern's Aidan Chiles has 1,898 yards with 13 touchdowns and one interception. Caleb Komolafe has 643 rushing yards. Griffin Wilde has 813 receiving yards. The Wildcats can move it. They just have to survive Smith's deep shots long enough for the points to matter.

The Over is about Ohio State's floor against a Northwestern defense that just gave up 24 to Iowa. Six of Ohio State's nine games cleared 47.5 combined points. display.fanatic_story:
Northwestern Wildcats vs Ohio State Buckeyes is Military Appreciation Day at Ohio Stadium, presented through the Our Honor Defend program with Anduril, a noon kickoff on a Saturday built for veterans, service members, and a Horseshoe that still expects scarlet and gray to answer Oregon. Brecken "Buck" Holloway is in the Horseshoe before the band, talking about Julian Sayin like the Ring of Honor can hear him. Ezra Lindqvist, purple to the bone, has Aidan Chiles' name already underlined.

Buck: Sayin has 19 touchdowns. Smith has 1,200 yards. Military Appreciation is not a quiet afternoon.

Ezra: Chiles has one interception all year. Komolafe runs downhill. Your afternoon still has to deal with that.

Ohio State is 6-3 after a 28-41 loss to Oregon that put a dent in the Playoff talk. Northwestern is coming off a 10-24 loss at Iowa. The Buckeyes still score 35.7 points a game and allow 18.3. The Wildcats score 31.0 and allow 19.3. Both defenses are respectable. Both offenses can put up a crooked number when the protection holds. The difference is Jeremiah Smith, who has 69 catches for 14 touchdowns and turns ordinary coverages into highlight packages.

Julian Sayin has 2,007 passing yards. Bo Jackson has 685 rushing yards and six scores. Kenyatta Jackson Jr. has 3 sacks. Earl Little Jr. has 53 tackles. When Ohio State stays on schedule, the Horseshoe starts sounding like a place that forgot last week's final score.

Northwestern's counter is patience. Aidan Chiles has 1,898 yards with 13 touchdowns and one interception. Caleb Komolafe has 643 rushing yards. Griffin Wilde has 813 receiving yards and five scores. Braydon Brus has 74 tackles and 4 sacks. The Wildcats keep games in the mud when they can, and mud is how you survive 11-point numbers in Columbus.

Ezra: We don't need to outscore Smith for a full game. We need to keep him from ending drives before we start ours.

Buck: Smith ends drives for a living. Our Honor Defend is going to see a lot of scarlet in the end zone.

Proceeds from officially licensed Our Honor Defend products support Ohio State veterans, ROTC, and military-connected student scholarships, which is the kind of Saturday detail that makes the pregame ceremony feel heavier than a regular noon kickoff. The band will play. The veterans will be recognized. The student section will be loud before the first snap. Then Sayin will try to make the rest of the afternoon feel simple, the way Ohio State afternoons are supposed to feel when Smith is running free and the offensive front is winning first down. Northwestern will try to make it feel like Iowa did last week: long, physical, and short on explosive plays. One of those plans will hold for three hours. The other will show up on the highlight board.

Buck will talk Smith. Ezra will talk Chiles. The Horseshoe will talk about whether Ohio State remembered how to finish.

Ohio Stadium on Military Appreciation Saturday is built for big moments and long memories. Our Honor Defend puts veterans and service members at the center of the pregame, then asks a football team coming off an Oregon loss to answer with something cleaner than last week. Northwestern is happy to make that answer difficult. Chiles does not throw the ball to the other team, Komolafe hits the hole without asking permission, and Brus shows up in the backfield often enough to wreck a drive chart.

Columbus will do the ceremony right. The Buckeyes still have to do the football right. That is the whole afternoon in one sentence, and both sidelines know it.

Buck will talk about Smith. Ezra will talk about keeping him quiet. The Horseshoe will talk about whether scarlet and gray still look like a November force when the points are this wide.

The Horseshoe does the ceremony right. The Buckeyes do the rest. My call: Ohio State Buckeyes 30, Northwestern Wildcats 19.

UConn has dropped two straight, including a 38-21 home loss to North Carolina.

display.fanatic_story:
James Madison Dukes vs UConn Huskies is the middle act of a three-game Husky weekend in Hartford, and Jo Ferrante has the whole weekend mapped like a fast break. UConn men's basketball plays Ohio State at PeoplesBank Arena on Friday, the football team hosts James Madison at noon Saturday in East Hartford for its Huskies & Heroes game, and the hockey team takes on Northeastern back downtown that same Saturday, which leaves JMU superfan Lila Shenandoah wondering whether anybody in Connecticut ever sleeps.

Lila: Basketball, football and hockey in about thirty hours? Jo, we just want a football game. We even brought our own purple.

Jo: You're getting a football game. You're also getting a state that treats every Husky like a cousin. Welcome to the Rent.

This is the first time James Madison has made the trip to Pratt & Whitney Stadium. The only other meeting came in Harrisonburg in November 2023, and Lila still has the confetti from that one, a 44-6 JMU win that Jo would rather discuss in a different decade.

Jo: Forty-four to six. You bring that up every time I see you.

Lila: I bring it up because it's true and because it was wonderful.

The Dukes are 8-2 and sit first in the Sun Belt's East, and they did it without much drama until late October. Then came back-to-back overtime losses, 34-31 at App State and 24-21 to Troy, two games where Lila swears she aged a full semester. James Madison answered by going to Hattiesburg and winning 54-23. The Dukes score 40.6 points a game and allow 19.3, which is the profile of a team that can afford a slow first quarter and still be comfortable by halftime.

Lila: George Pettaway has 824 rushing yards and eight touchdowns. Corey Scott caught six balls for 138 yards at Southern Miss. And JT Hooten has six sacks, so your quarterback is going to see a lot of purple.

The quarterback room is the one thing to watch on the JMU side. Camden Coleman leads the team with 1,814 throwing yards, 17 touchdowns and four interceptions, but JC Evans had the most attempts at Southern Miss and threw for 251 yards on 19-of-26. Either way, Lila says, the Dukes run the same offense with the same attitude.

Jo: That's fine. We've got Kalieb Osborne, and he doesn't need a timeshare.

Osborne is the heartbeat of UConn's offense. He has 2,102 throwing yards with 16 touchdowns and only four interceptions, and he threw for 314 yards and three scores in the 42-41 overtime loss to Syracuse. Cyncir Bowers has 639 rushing yards and eight touchdowns. The Huskies score 32.9 points a game, more than most people outside Connecticut realize. The trouble has been closing. UConn is 4-5, and it has lost two straight, 35-26 at Air Force and 38-21 to North Carolina at home last Saturday.

Jo: We've played Syracuse to overtime and Miami of Ohio to a field goal. This team is close, Lila. Close is the most frustrating word in sports.

Lila: Close isn't a word we use in Harrisonburg. We use dominant, and sometimes overtime.

The best matchup on the field is UConn's linebacker John Lista, who leads the Huskies with 68 tackles, against Pettaway between the tackles. If Lista and K'Von Sherman keep Pettaway in front of them, Osborne gets enough possessions to make this a shootout. If Pettaway breaks loose early, the Dukes get to shorten the game and make the Rent awfully quiet.

The Huskies & Heroes theme gives the afternoon another layer, and both insiders agree that the people being honored deserve the loudest cheer of the day, louder than anything for a touchdown. Jo plans to stand for the whole ceremony. Lila plans to stand for the whole game, because that's just how she watches football.

Jo: After this, I'm driving downtown for the hockey game. You're welcome to come. Northeastern is a lot like you, Lila. They travel well and they never stop talking.

Lila: I'll come if you promise not to mention overtime.

Jo: Deal. You don't mention 44-6, I don't mention App State.

Lila: That's not a deal, Jo. That's a ceasefire, and I'm keeping the confetti.

Lila keeps the confetti. Jo starts talking about hockey. My call: James Madison Dukes 34, UConn Huskies 26.

display.fanatic_story:
Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets vs Clemson Tigers is Senior Day at Memorial Stadium, and Clemson is sending its seniors down The Hill one at a time before the 12:30 p.m. kickoff, a solo run for every one of them. Dixie-Lynn Pruitt, the old Tiger Band flag captain, plans to cry through all of it and blame the wind, while Georgia Tech's Wendell Quist stands at the top of the slope calculating the exact speed of a big offensive tackle on a downhill grade.

Wendell: It's a fascinating slope, Dixie-Lynn. Gravity is doing a lot of the work.

Dixie-Lynn: Gravity has nothing to do with it, Wendell. That's tradition, and it runs on orange.

She has reason to want a good send-off, because the last time these two met, Georgia Tech wrecked her September. Clemson went to Atlanta in 2025 and lost 24-21, the only Yellow Jacket win in the nine meetings since 2016. Wendell has the final score saved as the home screen on his calculator.

Wendell: One win in nine. I'm aware it's not a large sample. I'm also aware it was the most recent one.

Dixie-Lynn: Enjoy it. We had a whole decade before that.

The 2026 Tigers are 6-3 and fifth in the ACC, and they have been winning games the hard way. They went to Syracuse last Saturday and won 18-13, and before that they beat Florida State 36-24 in Tallahassee. Tait Reynolds has thrown for 1,446 yards and does more managing than gunslinging, and Bryant Wesco Jr. caught six balls for 100 yards at Syracuse. Gideon Davidson leads the team with 528 rushing yards, and Jarvis Green ran for 85 at the Dome. The real Clemson story is defense. Will Heldt has seven sacks, safety Corey Myrick has 69 tackles, and the Tigers allow 20.7 points a game.

Dixie-Lynn: When Heldt gets a running start, Wendell, even your calculations get nervous.

Wendell: I don't get nervous. I get recalculated.

Georgia Tech is 2-7, and Wendell won't pretend otherwise. The Jackets have lost four straight, most recently 44-17 at home to Louisville. But they have been in games, too. They lost 14-13 to Colorado in the opener, beat Duke 28-25, and lost by seven at Stanford. Alberto Mendoza has 1,943 throwing yards and 11 touchdowns, and he threw for 335 yards at Virginia Tech. Justice Haynes has 635 rushing yards and ran for 87 against Louisville. Jordan Allen leads the receivers with 49 catches, and safety Tae Harris has 58 tackles.

Wendell: Mendoza is accurate. Our problem has been the other side of the ball, where we give up 32.2 points a game. That isn't a trajectory I enjoy.

Dixie-Lynn: Then don't look at the third quarter.

The football question is whether Clemson can turn its defense into points. The Tigers score 22.7 a game, which is modest for a team with this many wins, and Georgia Tech's defense has given up 34 or more six times. If Reynolds and Wesco hit a couple of early throws, the Tigers can make the afternoon comfortable in time for the seniors to enjoy the second half. If Mendoza keeps converting third downs, Wendell gets to stay in his seat a little longer than anybody in orange would like.

Saturday in Clemson starts early. Fan Fest at The Stacks, the new tailgate green space on the old motor pool site east of the stadium, has free live music before the game, and the BioSci graduate students are running an ice cream scooping fundraiser at the '55 Exchange, which means Dixie-Lynn will be eating a cone in November and calling it a breakfast tradition.

Wendell: Ice cream before noon is not a balanced diet.

Dixie-Lynn: It is on Senior Day. It's practically in the student handbook.

When the last senior hits the bottom of The Hill and the band kicks in, there won't be a quiet seat in the house, and Wendell knows it.

Wendell: I'll give you the run down The Hill, Dixie-Lynn. That's the best tradition in the conference.

Dixie-Lynn: Thank you, Wendell. Now go sit down before Heldt finds you.

Run down The Hill, then run away from Georgia Tech. My call: Clemson Tigers 31, Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets 18.

Nebraska at Rutgers is Military Appreciation Day in Piscataway, a 12:30 PM ET kickoff with the Scarlet Knights in American flag Block R helmets, military vehicles lined up along The Rutgers Boardwalk and a flyover after the anthem. My Nebraska vs Rutgers prediction has the Huskers snapping their skid without running away: Nebraska Cornhuskers 33, Rutgers Scarlet Knights 21, with Rutgers Scarlet Knights +13.5 and Over 53.5.

Darla Rasmussen flew in from Lincoln in red and wants this one badly. "We allow 16.6 points a game, and Anthony Colandrea has 16 touchdowns. Four close losses. Today we're due." Vinny Scolari is holding court at the Boardwalk food trucks. "Antwan Raymond has 789 yards and KJ Duff has 774 receiving. We played USC to 42-35. Two touchdowns is a lot, Darla."

He's right about that. DraftKings opened Nebraska −12.5 with 54.5 on the over/under, and it went to −13.5 and 53.5. Nebraska has lost four straight by 3, 3, 7 and 11 points, and its offense has scored 17 or fewer in each of those games. A team that can't find 20 against good defenses is asking a lot when it lays two scores on the road. Nebraska won the last four meetings, but by 10, 7, one and seven. My Huskers by 12 stay just inside the 13.5.

Rutgers has a quarterback question, which I'm pricing in. Dylan Lonergan leads in throwing yards, while AJ Surace had the most attempts in each of the last three games. Raymond's 149 carries are the constant.

The Over is about the Rutgers defense. The Scarlet Knights allow 32.4 points a game, and six of their nine games finished above 53.5 combined points. Nebraska scored 48 on Maryland and 49 on Ohio earlier this season. Colandrea threw for 284 yards at Illinois even in a loss. My 54 points sit above 53.5, and the move down from 54.5 helps.

Nobody in the room agrees on either call. The Formula takes Nebraska Cornhuskers −13.5 and Under 53.5, with Nebraska 33-19. Next Man Up has Rutgers Scarlet Knights +13.5 and likes Over 53.5, 35-23. Letdown Watch has Rutgers Scarlet Knights +13.5 and Under 53.5, 32-20. In The Trenches likes Rutgers Scarlet Knights +13.5 and makes no over/under call. Follow The Money is still waiting on a consensus spread, so its side is pending, and it has no total pick.

Nebraska Cornhuskers vs Rutgers Scarlet Knights is Rutgers' Military Appreciation game at SHI Stadium, and the Scarlet Knights will take the field in their American flag Block R helmets with military vehicles parked along The Rutgers Boardwalk and a flyover planned right after the national anthem. Vinny Scolari has been on the Boardwalk since it opened at 8:30, working through the food trucks, and Nebraska's Darla Rasmussen arrives in red with the patient look of a fan who has watched four straight close Saturdays slip away.

Vinny: Darla, you came all the way from Lincoln for a flyover and a Jersey food truck. That's the smartest thing anybody in red has done all month.

Darla: I came for a win, Vinny. The food truck is a bonus. The flyover is a blessing.

Both of them mean the second part. The day honors current service members, veterans and ROTC cadets throughout the game, and some lucky fans will help hold the U.S. flag on the field during the anthem. Vinny swears he'll keep quiet for the whole thing, which is a first for a man from Exit 9.

The football part starts with Nebraska's slide. The Huskers began 5-0, beating Maryland 48-23 and Michigan State 31-13 along the way, then lost four in a row by a combined 24 points, 20-17 to Indiana, 17-14 at Oregon, 17-10 to Washington and 24-13 at Illinois. Darla calls it the most frustrating month since she gave up volleyball.

Darla: Four losses, and we were in every one of them. Our defense allows 16.6 points a game. That's a real defense, Vinny.

Vinny: It's a real defense. Your offense just keeps parking in the wrong lot.

Anthony Colandrea is the guy who can fix that. He has 2,109 throwing yards with 16 touchdowns, and he threw for 284 yards on 32-of-43 at Illinois even in a loss. Kwazi Gilmer has 46 catches for 603 yards and seven touchdowns, and Jamal Rule leads the run game with 532 yards. On defense, Jahsear Whittington has 4.5 sacks and linebacker Owen Chambliss has 55 tackles.

Rutgers is 2-7 and has had a long autumn, but Vinny isn't hiding from it. The Scarlet Knights have been close more than once, 28-21 at Boston College, 42-35 to USC and 28-21 to Michigan on Halloween. They also won 37-30 at Maryland, which Vinny considers a holiday. Antwan Raymond is the workhorse, 789 rushing yards and six touchdowns on 149 carries, and KJ Duff has 774 receiving yards and nine touchdowns. The quarterback spot has rotated. Dylan Lonergan leads the team in throwing yards, while AJ Surace had the most throws in each of the last three games.

Vinny: Whoever's back there, Raymond's getting the ball. That kid runs like he's late for the train to Penn Station.

Darla: And our front seven is the reason trains run on time in Nebraska.

That's the heart of the game. Raymond against the Nebraska front, and Colandrea against a Rutgers defense that has given up 32.4 points a game. The Huskers have won the last four meetings, but three of them were close, 14-13 here in 2022, 14-7 in Lincoln in 2024 and 28-21 in 2020. Nobody in Piscataway is conceding anything before kickoff.

Vinny: Four in a row, sure. One by a point and one by a touchdown. Point is, we hang.

Darla: You hang. We win. That's the Big Ten in one sentence.

The Boardwalk has free rides and games for the kids before the pregame parade and the Scarlet Walk, and by the time the team arrives, the whole lot will be red, white and blue. Darla admits the American flag helmets look sharp. Vinny admits Nebraska fans travel like nobody else in the conference.

Vinny: I'll even let you have a sub from the Boardwalk. On the house. Don't tell anybody I'm nice.

Darla: Your secret's safe. Ours is that we've been waiting a month to throw a party, and today's the day we bring the balloons.

Vinny: Bring 'em. Just don't let 'em go before the flyover.

Darla: Vinny, they go up when we score. You'll see plenty.

The flyover gets the loudest cheer of the day, right up until the Huskers pull away. My call: Nebraska Cornhuskers 33, Rutgers Scarlet Knights 21.

Alabama Crimson Tide vs Vanderbilt Commodores is Fan Appreciation Day at FirstBank Stadium, and Vandyville opens at 8:45 a.m. with the player walk at 9:05 and The Spazmatics taking the Commodore Court stage at 9:45 in skinny ties and horn-rimmed glasses. Mary-Kathryn "MK" Strickland is in Vandyville before the gates swing open, talking about Keelon Russell like the free embroidered bandanas are already spoken for. Penelope "Pippa" Ashcroft answers with a reminder that Nashville has beaten this visitor before.

MK: Russell has 18 touchdowns. We just won at LSU. Fan Appreciation is still our kind of Saturday.

Pippa: Sherrill has 747 yards. We won 40-35 over No. 1 Alabama in this building in 2024. Your Saturday still has to climb that memory.

Alabama is rolling after a 31-13 win at LSU. Vanderbilt just won 25-23 at Mississippi State. The Crimson Tide score 37.4 points a game and allow 20.3. The Commodores score 23.0 and allow 29.4. That is a mismatch on paper and a reunion on the calendar, because Nashville has already written one Alabama story that did not follow the paper.

Keelon Russell has 2,263 passing yards with 18 touchdowns and five interceptions. Rico Scott has 501 receiving yards. Trae'shawn Brown has 359 rushing yards and five scores. Devan Thompkins has 5 sacks. Caleb Woodson has 70 tackles. When Alabama's protection holds, FirstBank starts looking like every other SEC venue that tried to host this offense and ended up chasing it.

Vanderbilt's counter is home noise and third-down stubbornness. Jared Curtis has 1,657 yards. Sedrick Alexander has six rushing touchdowns. Junior Sherrill has 56 catches. Issa Ouattara has 4 sacks. CJ Heard has 63 tackles. The Commodores do not need to outscore Alabama for a full game. They need to keep the game close enough for the fourth quarter to remember 2024.

Pippa: Free samples from Dunkin' and Pop-Up Bagels are nice. A stop on third down is nicer.

MK: Bandanas are nice. Russell throwing it over the top is nicer.

Vandyville will have the Max Nance Kids' Zone and local food from Hattie B's and Edley's. The football will have Russell, Sherrill, and a Fan Appreciation crowd that paid for one more memory before the season turns toward Tennessee. One of those plans will feel like a party. The other will feel like a statement.

MK will talk touchdowns. Pippa will talk 2024. Nashville will talk about whether Fan Appreciation came with a sequel.

Fan Appreciation Day at Vanderbilt is built for early arrivals. Free samples from Dunkin', Pop-Up Bagels, Celsius, and Tiff's Treats fill Commodore Court while kids bounce through the Max Nance Kids' Zone. The Spazmatics will play throwback hits from that decade. The football will not. Alabama wants to leave Nashville with a statement after LSU. Vanderbilt wants to leave the alumni with one more memory that feels like 2024. Those two wishes cannot both survive the fourth quarter.

MK keeps pointing at Russell's touchdown total. Pippa keeps pointing at the building's last Alabama story. FirstBank will decide which argument was louder before the last bandana leaves Commodore Court.

The SEC Network cameras will catch The Spazmatics and the bandanas. They will also catch whether Vanderbilt's front can bother Russell long enough for Curtis to keep pace. Alabama has spent all fall turning those possessions into 35-point afternoons. Vanderbilt has spent the last two weeks proving it can win ugly on the road and at home. Fan Appreciation Day is about to ask which habit is stronger when the visitor wears crimson.

Nashville knows how to throw a party. Alabama knows how to end one. FirstBank gets to host both moods until the clock says otherwise.

Nashville throws the party; Alabama ends it in the fourth quarter. My call: Alabama Crimson Tide 35, Vanderbilt Commodores 18.

East Carolina Pirates vs Charlotte 49ers is the Gold Rush rivalry game, and Charlotte's Priya Halloran plans to wear so much gold to Jerry Richardson Stadium for the 1 p.m. kickoff that ECU's Bart Quidley will need sunglasses to find his seat. Bart has been tailgating in the same Greenville spot since before he could walk, and he has driven across the state to tell her that a Pirate ship doesn't care what color the harbor is.

Priya: It's the Gold Rush, Bart. Everybody in gold. Even the risk committee.

Bart: Arrr-guably the most expensive color you could have picked for a 1-8 season, Priya. But I respect the commitment.

The history is shorter than either of them would like and spicier than most rivalries twice its age. Charlotte leads the series 2-1. The 49ers won 10-7 in Greenville in 2023, then drilled the Pirates 55-24 here in 2024, the first and only time this rivalry had been played at Jerry Richardson Stadium until now. Last November, East Carolina returned the favor in Greenville, 48-22.

Priya: Fifty-five to twenty-four. I keep that one in a frame on my desk, right next to my Uptown bank's quarterly report. Both show a positive return on investment.

Bart: Forty-eight to twenty-two keeps me warm at night, matey. We'll call it a running tab and settle it today.

Okay, he said "matey." Pirate talk is allowed, in moderation, and Bart has now used his allotment for the afternoon.

East Carolina comes in 5-4 and feeling better about itself. The Pirates have won two of their last three, 17-9 over Temple and 20-17 over South Florida, and they have been winning ugly with a defense that allows 23.3 points a game. The quarterback job has bounced between Emory Williams and Mitch Griffis, and Williams had the most attempts against USF, going 19-of-27 for 175 yards and two touchdowns. Landon Sides caught 14 balls for 126 yards and both of those scores. TJ Engleman Jr. leads the rushers with 695 yards, Ashton Gray ran for 101 against the Bulls, and DJ Johnson Jr. has 60 tackles on defense.

Bart: Fourteen catches for Landon Sides. That's not a box score, Priya, that's a treasure map.

Priya: It's a lot of catches. I'd underwrite it.

Charlotte's season has been rougher, and Priya won't spin it. The 49ers are 1-8, they allow 38.3 points a game, and their only win came 38-31 at Temple in October. But there were close calls, too. They lost 43-41 in overtime to The Citadel in the opener, 26-21 at App State and 38-31 in overtime to Tulane. Conner Harrell has taken over the offense, with 1,006 throwing yards and six touchdowns against only two interceptions, and Jaden Barnes has 54 catches for 542 yards. Gavin Willis has 74 tackles from the middle of the defense, and he will be busy.

Priya: Harrell protects the football. In my business, that's called a sound fundamental.

display.fanatic_story:
UAB Blazers vs Temple Owls is Senior Day and Family Day at Lincoln Financial Field, a 1 p.m. kickoff in South Philly, and Temple's Teddy Fiorella has already told three strangers in the parking lot that Birmingham is a fine place to visit as long as you leave by dinner. Nobody asked him. Nobody ever asks him. UAB's Ozella Birchfield has made the trip north, and this is a first for her program: the Blazers have never played a football game in Philadelphia before Saturday.

Teddy: Welcome to Philly, Ozella. First time? Don't touch the cheesesteak debate. You're not ready.

Ozella: I come from a city built on iron, Teddy. I can handle a sandwich.

The only previous meeting came in Birmingham in November 2023, and UAB won it 34-24. That gives the Blazers a perfect record in the series and gives Teddy something to complain about, which is what he does best.

Teddy: One game! One game in Alabama three years ago. That's not a rivalry, that's a rumor.

Ozella: It's a forged record, Teddy. Forged, not given.

Here's where the two teams stand. UAB is 5-4 and coming off a 23-12 home win over Charlotte. Rod Robinson II ran for 101 yards that day, and the defense held the 49ers to a dozen points. That defense is the story of the Blazers' season. Marlin Dean has 10.5 sacks, which is the kind of number that makes quarterbacks check their mirrors, and Muaaz Byard has 83 tackles. Ryder Burton runs the offense, with 1,474 throwing yards, and the Blazers have won three of their last five.

Ozella: Marlin Dean plays like a blast furnace. You open the door, you feel the heat.

Teddy: Yeah, well, our guys have been hit by worse. Ya gotta take a punch.

Temple has taken a lot of them. The Owls are 2-7 and have dropped four in a row, and several of the losses were heartbreakers. They lost 49-48 in overtime at Toledo, 21-17 to Army and 38-31 to Charlotte. Last week at Navy they scored 35 and still came home with a 42-35 loss. Ajani Sheppard leads the team with 1,245 throwing yards and eight touchdowns, Jaxon Smolik threw three touchdowns at Navy, Keveun Mason has 588 rushing yards, and Curly Ordonez has 84 tackles and two sacks.

Teddy: Curly Ordonez is the most Philly football player alive. You knock him down, he gets up, he yells at you, he gets up again.

Ozella: I respect that. Birmingham would adopt him.

Teddy: Birmingham can't have him. Nobody insults Curly. Not that you did, but I'm getting ahead of it.

The key for Temple is protection. Dean has been living in opposing backfields, and if the Owls give him a clean run at their quarterback, the afternoon will get long. If Temple can stay ahead of the chains with Mason and let its quarterback get the ball out early, the Owls have enough playmakers to score with anyone in this league. Colin Chase has 381 receiving yards, and Jayce Freeman caught two touchdowns at Navy.

For UAB, the job is ball security. Burton threw three interceptions against Charlotte even in a win, and a Temple defense that has been waiting all month for a break would love a few gifts on Senior Day.

The day itself will be special. Temple will honor its seniors and their families before the game, and Family Day means plenty of kids in cherry and white running around the Linc.

Teddy: Ozella, if the seniors win this one, I'm running up the art museum steps. All of them. In the rain if I have to.

Ozella: And if we win, I'm buying you a sandwich and telling everybody in Birmingham you were gracious.

Teddy: I've never been gracious in my life. Don't go telling people that.

Teddy stays ungracious. The Linc gets its Senior Day win anyway. My call: Temple Owls 27, UAB Blazers 23.

display.fanatic_story:
Arkansas State Red Wolves vs Coastal Carolina Chanticleers is a 1 p.m. kickoff at Brooks Stadium, and Coastal's Goldie Seabrook plans to spend her morning a few miles away at the L.W. Paul Living History Farm, where Syrup Day runs from 9 until noon. Volunteers will crush sugar cane, cook the juice down over a fire into sweet cane syrup, and teach the kids old farm games. Goldie says it's the most Conway way to get ready for a football game, and she will be wearing sandals to it, because November or not, closed-toe shoes are for other people.

Goldie: You cook it slow and you don't rush it, Ty. Same as a good drive.

Ty Doucet-Harmon has come from the Delta with a duck call on a cord around his neck, and he blows it once, just to say hello.

Ty: That's my good-morning call, Goldie. You'll hear a happier one late this afternoon.

Ty: Syrup, huh? Down home we'd pour that on biscuits and call it a holiday.

This is the seventh meeting between these two, and it couldn't be more even. The series is tied 3-3. Arkansas State won the first three, including a 51-17 blowout in Jonesboro in 2017 and a 28-27 thriller in 2019. Then Coastal flipped it, winning 52-23 here at Brooks in 2020, 52-20 the next year, and 27-17 in Jonesboro in 2023. Somebody breaks the tie on Saturday.

Goldie: Three in a row for us. The tide comes in, Ty. It always comes in.

Ty: And then it goes back out. That's the whole point of a tide.

Coastal comes in 3-6 and frustrated. The Chanticleers have scored exactly as many points as they've allowed, 222 each, and last week's 21-8 loss to Old Dominion hurt. Deuce Bailey was intercepted three times in that game, but he has been a playmaker all year, with 2,178 throwing yards and 19 touchdowns. Clayton Coppock Jr. has 408 receiving yards and five scores, Dominic Lee-Knicely has 498 rushing yards, Marcellius Pulliam has 96 tackles and Ibrahim Diawara has five sacks.

Goldie: Marcellius Pulliam hits like a nor'easter. You hear him before you see him.

Ty: Trey Owens hears everybody. He's got 2,133 yards and 12 touchdowns, Goldie. He threw for 418 against South Alabama.

Arkansas State is 4-5 and lost a 19-17 heartbreaker to UL Monroe last week. The Red Wolves have played a lot of tight games, beating Kennesaw State 17-14 and losing 23-20 at Louisiana and 56-49 to South Alabama. Owens is the engine. Jaylen Bonelli has 518 receiving yards, Solomon Baggett leads the rushers with 344 yards, and safety Joe Drew has 83 tackles.

Ty: Joe Drew is a retriever. Ball goes in the water, Joe Drew brings it back.

Goldie, who is unexpectedly fierce about blocking, has her own scouting note.

Goldie: Here's the thing nobody says out loud. Our offensive front has to give Deuce time. When he has time, he finds Coppock deep. When he doesn't, he forces it, and that's how you get three interceptions against Old Dominion.

Ty: And our front has to get after him. If Owens gets rhythm, we score with anybody.

That's the whole game, really. Two quarterbacks who can throw it all over the field, two defenses that have been up and down, and a tie in the series that has to be broken. Both teams have something to fix. Coastal has to clean up the mistakes from last week, and Arkansas State has to finish the close ones it has been letting slip away.

Goldie: The syrup will be done by noon, the sun will be out, and the Teal Nation will be loud.

Ty: Save me a jar, Goldie. I'll need something sweet on the drive home if this goes wrong.

Ty blows the duck call again. It is not clear whether that's a threat or a thank-you.

Goldie saves Ty a jar, and he's going to need it on the drive home. My call: Coastal Carolina Chanticleers 27, Arkansas State Red Wolves 24.

display.fanatic_story:
Kansas State Wildcats vs TCU Horned Frogs is the Freedom Frogs game at Amon G. Carter Stadium, a 1 p.m. kickoff in Fort Worth just a few days after Veterans Day, and it's the next-to-last home game of the year for the Frogs. TCU's Ryder Galloway has his hat on, his boots shined and his evening already planned: Ryan Bingham plays the main stage at Billy Bob's Texas in the Stockyards at 9 p.m., and Ryder intends to be there either celebrating or blaming Dallas.

Ryder: Hattie, this is Cowtown. We drive cattle, we play football, and we don't apologize for either one.

Hattie Brandvold came down from Manhattan with a notebook full of crop names, because she names every K-State drive after something you can grow.

Hattie: Big talk, Ryder. Our first drive is called Winter Wheat. It's slow, it's patient, and it ends with a bumper harvest.

Ryder: You name your drives after plants?

Hattie: You blame your losses on a city down the road. We all have our ways.

The recent history belongs to Kansas State, and Hattie knows every row of it. The Wildcats beat TCU 41-28 last October in Manhattan. They won 41-3 there in 2023, and they won the 2022 Big 12 championship game over the Frogs, 31-28. TCU's last win in the series came here in Fort Worth in October 2022, 38-28. Over the last ten meetings, K-State has won seven.

Ryder: Don't bring up December 2022. I still get upset thinking about it. I blame Dallas for that one too, on principle.

Both teams are 4-5, but they got there in very different ways. TCU's defense has been terrific. The Frogs allow just 15.8 points a game, and their five losses came by five, eight, seven, four and one point. Last week they lost 29-28 at Arizona. That's a season of almosts, and it has Ryder pacing.

Jaden Craig has carried the offense with 2,439 throwing yards and 12 touchdowns. The best target is tight end Kari Ashley, who has 52 catches for 655 yards and caught 14 passes at Arizona. Koron Hayward has six sacks and Hudson Hooper has 62 tackles.

Ryder: Kari Ashley runs routes like a cutting horse. He stops on a dime and leaves a nickel of change.

Kansas State has had a rougher month. The Wildcats have lost four in a row, including a 66-28 loss to Oklahoma State last week, and the passing job has moved around. Avery Johnson leads the team with 1,301 throwing yards and 10 touchdowns, but Jacob Knuth threw the most at Arizona State, and Blake Barnett did it the last two weeks. Rodney Fields Jr. has 574 rushing yards and six scores, and Derrick Salley Jr. caught two touchdowns against the Cowboys.

Hattie: You can't rush a harvest, Ryder. Some seasons you plant, and some seasons you wait. But Rodney Fields is a bumper harvest every week.

Hattie: And we scored 71 in the opener. Just saying.

Ryder: Against Nicholls, Hattie. My cousin's ranch could score on Nicholls.

The key for K-State is simple. The Wildcats have to run the football with Fields and keep the Frogs' defense on the field, because Hayward and that rush up front can make any quarterback uncomfortable. For TCU, the job is turning all that defense into points. Craig and Ashley have to finish drives, because the Frogs have lost too many games by a single score to leave field goals on the board.

Ryder: We're due. We've been knocking on the door all year. Saturday we kick it in.

Hattie: Respectfully, the door has a Powercat on it.

The Freedom Frogs crowd should be loud, and the Stockyards will be full by dark either way.

Ryder: If we win, I'm throwing this hat so high it lands at Billy Bob's.

Hattie: If we win, I'm doing the Wabash Cannonball in my seat, and I'm doing it tidy.

Ryder makes Billy Bob's on time, hat on and the Frogs on top. My call: TCU Horned Frogs 27, Kansas State Wildcats 21.

display.fanatic_story:
Tulane Green Wave vs Rice Owls is Homecoming and Alumni Weekend at First Community Stadium, a 1 p.m. kickoff in Houston, and Rice's Odalys Chen-Moreau has spent the week reviewing the evidence like a stats cop with a badge. Her finding: Tulane has been Rice's Homecoming opponent twice before, and the Owls won both, 42-34 in 2005 and 28-20 in 2009.

Odalys: Two for two, Twan. Small sample, I admit it. But it's a perfect small sample.

Antoine "Twan" Ducros-Labat has driven in from Uptown with his trumpet case, and he insists every road game deserves a brass-band parade.

Twan: Odalys, two games from before some of these players were born is not evidence. That's a bedtime story.

Odalys: N is too small to panic. I'm not panicking. I'm noting.

This is the 39th meeting between two old conference rivals, and the series is about as even as it gets. Rice leads 20-17-1. But Tulane owns the recent part of it. The Green Wave won 30-28 here in 2023 and 24-10 at home in 2024, and Rice hasn't beaten them since a 17-13 win in 2013.

Twan: Thirteen years, Odalys. That win deserves a beignet and a museum.

Odalys: Thirteen years is just a longer sample. Patience.

Now the hard part, because neither fan base is enjoying this season. Rice is 1-8, and the Owls have lost eight straight since beating Houston Christian in the opener. A few of those were painful. They lost 51-49 at Florida Atlantic, 16-14 to UTSA and 28-21 to Western Michigan. Jacurri Brown is the heartbeat of the offense. He's the leading rusher with 686 yards and six touchdowns and has also thrown for 478, and Gael Ochoa has handled most of the throwing the last two weeks. AJ Brown has 65 tackles in the secondary.

Odalys: Jacurri Brown is statistically significant. That's my highest compliment.

Twan: He's a whole brass section by himself. I'll give you that one.

Tulane is 4-5 and coming off a rough one, a 60-10 loss to Tulsa that Twan will not be discussing at length. Before that, the Green Wave had won two of three, beating Memphis 31-17 and Charlotte 38-31 in overtime. Trace Johnson has taken over at quarterback, Johnnie Daniels has 542 rushing yards and six touchdowns, Destyn Hill has 445 receiving yards, and Dickson Agu has 86 tackles.

Twan: Dickson Agu is the bass drum. Everything else marches to him.

Odalys: The MOB has a bass drum too. Ours occasionally wears a costume.

The Marching Owl Band is famous for halftime shows nobody can predict, which is the whole point. Odalys hopes for something nerdy. Twan hopes for a song he can play along with.

The key for Tulane is getting back to its identity. The Green Wave need Daniels running downhill so Johnson doesn't have to throw from behind all day. For Rice, it's turning Brown loose. If Brown can get outside and gain yards with his legs, the Owls can control the clock and keep the Tulane offense on the sideline.

Twan: If we win, I'm leading a brass-band parade around the stadium. Trumpet up, umbrella in the air, the whole thing.

Odalys: If we win, I'm doing a nerdy dance and publishing the results. Peer review optional.

Homecoming crowds bring out the alumni, the old jerseys and a lot of hope, and Rice has had plenty of reasons to need all three.

Odalys: It's a perfect Homecoming sample, Twan. Two for two. We make it three.

Twan: Ask me again at the final whistle. I'll be the one with the trumpet.

Three for three on Homecoming, by a single point. Odalys called it. My call: Rice Owls 26, Tulane Green Wave 25.

Lem keeps talking about Landyn's touchdowns. Ximena keeps talking about Woods' scores. Bowers Stadium will decide which family goes home happier.

Tennessee at Texas A&M is Operation Blackout at Kyle Field, with the 12th Man in black and kickoff set for 3:00 PM ET. My Tennessee vs Texas A&M prediction has the Vols winning a close, physical game that finds more points than this price expects: Tennessee Volunteers 25, Texas A&M Aggies 23, with Texas A&M Aggies +2.5 and Over 42.5.

Earl Haskew tuned his banjo before he said a word. "DeSean Bishop has 1,066 yards and 13 touchdowns. We allow 15.1 points a game. Our two losses were by three each." Colt Wendeborn is in full Blackout. "We allow 18.7, Earl. Rueben Owens ran for 137 at South Carolina. And we're 2-1 against you in the last three meetings."

This is the biggest market move of my week. DraftKings opened Texas A&M −9.5 with 55.5 on the over/under. By Monday morning it had Tennessee −2.5 and 42.5. That's a twelve-point swing on the side and thirteen points off the total, and there is no injury report here to explain it, so I won't guess. What I can see is the season. Tennessee is 7-2 and beat Alabama 26-10. A&M is 4-5 and 1-5 in the SEC and has lost its last two, 31-20 at Alabama and 17-9 at South Carolina. That's why the price flipped. But it flipped all the way to a road favorite in a stadium where the Aggies beat the Vols 45-38 the last time they came here. My Vols by 2 means the 2.5 on A&M is the right side of a close game.

The Aggie defense keeps it close. A&M shut out Missouri State and The Citadel and held Arkansas to seven. Marcel Reed threw 43 times at South Carolina without an interception. Tennessee's quarterback position moved from Faizon Brandon to George MacIntyre in October, and MacIntyre has two touchdown passes for the season.

The Over is about how far the total fell. At 42.5, Tennessee's offense has to do little more than its usual work. The Vols have scored at least 24 points in eight of their nine games, with 34 against Kentucky last week. A&M has scored 20 or more in six of nine. My 48 points sit comfortably above 42.5, and the drop from 55.5 gives me plenty of room.

The room is split on the side and with me on the total. The Formula has Texas A&M Aggies +2.5 and likes Over 42.5, with Tennessee 25-23. Next Man Up likes Texas A&M Aggies +2.5 and has Over 42.5, with A&M 22-21. Letdown Watch has Tennessee Volunteers −2.5 and likes Over 42.5, 26-22. In The Trenches likes Tennessee Volunteers −2.5 and makes no over/under call. Follow The Money is still waiting on a consensus spread, so its side is pending, and it has no total pick.

Letdown Watch to Next Man Up: "You've got A&M winning outright? They've lost two straight." Next Man Up: "At home, in the dark, against a quarterback with two touchdown passes. I'll take it."

Earl gets a win and a long banjo ride home. Colt gets a Blackout crowd that never sits down and a game decided late.

display.fanatic_story:
Tennessee Volunteers vs Texas A&M Aggies is Operation Blackout at Kyle Field, and the Aggies want every one of those seats filled with black when the gates open at 12:30 and the ball goes up at 2 p.m. Colt Wendeborn has been practicing his yells all week in a closet so the neighbors don't complain, and he has a black shirt, black hat and black socks ready to go.

Colt: This is the third Blackout since Coach Elko got here, Earl. The first one, we beat No. 8 LSU, 38-23. Last year, we held Mississippi State to nine. Darkness is good to us.

Earl "Rocky Top" Haskew, a former Vol long snapper, plays a banjo intro before he answers, because Earl plays a banjo intro before everything.

Earl: Colt, I'm bringing orange into the dark. A little checkerboard never hurt anybody.

Colt: It hurts the Blackout, Earl. That's the whole point of the Blackout.

Colt then explains the Blackout. Then he explains why the 12th Man stands the entire game. Then he explains the explanation. Earl strums through all of it.

The meetings between these two have been memorable. In 2016, the Aggies won a wild one here, 45-38. In 2020 they went to Knoxville and won 34-13. Tennessee got one back at home in 2023, 20-13. That puts A&M up 2-1 in the recent meetings, and Colt will mention it several times.

Earl: Two-one isn't a dynasty, Colt. It's a bluegrass tune with three verses, and we're about to write the fourth.

Tennessee comes in 7-2 and playing the kind of football Earl's banjo was made for. The Vols score 32.4 points a game and allow just 15.1. They beat Alabama 26-10, won at Arkansas 24-17 and handled Kentucky 34-6 last week. Their two losses came by three points apiece, 20-17 to Texas and 27-24 at South Carolina. George MacIntyre has taken over the passing in October, and DeSean Bishop is the engine of the whole thing, with 1,066 rushing yards and 13 touchdowns. He ran for 109 and two scores against Kentucky. Mike Matthews has 566 receiving yards, Tyree Weathersby has seven sacks and Arion Carter has 59 tackles.

Earl: DeSean Bishop runs like Rocky Top on fast tempo. You can't stop him, you can only hum along.

Texas A&M is 4-5, and Colt is processing it in his closet. The Aggies are 1-5 in the SEC and lost their last two, 31-20 at Alabama and 17-9 at South Carolina. But the defense has been better than the record. A&M allows 18.7 points a game, and it shut out Missouri State and The Citadel. Marcel Reed has 1,641 throwing yards, Rueben Owens II ran for 137 yards at South Carolina, Isaiah Horton leads the receivers and Ray Coney leads the defense in tackles.

Colt: Rueben Owens ran like a Yell Leader on a dead sprint. That's a tradition, too. I just made it up, but it's a tradition now.

Earl: That's how all traditions get made, Colt. Somebody yells it first.

The key for the Aggies is the run defense. If Bishop gets 25 carries again, the Vols can play the way they want, keep the ball and wear down a defense in the fourth quarter. A&M has to win early downs and get Tennessee into passing situations, then let Marco Jones and the front go after MacIntyre. For Tennessee, the job is staying patient. Kyle Field gets loud, and the Blackout will make it look like midnight in the middle of the afternoon.

Colt: When that crowd sways, Earl, you'll feel it in your banjo strings.

Earl: My banjo has been to Razorback Stadium and Williams-Brice this year. It's not scared of a little darkness.

These two programs share a lot. Big stadiums, loud crowds and fans who will tell you every tradition whether you ask or not. Colt says the Aggies need this one for the season. Earl says the Vols need it for something bigger.

Earl: If we win, I'm playing Rocky Top on the drive back to Knoxville. The whole way home.

Colt: If we win, I'm yelling. Just yelling. Joyfully. For about an hour.

Colt yells for an hour. Earl plays Rocky Top all the way to Knoxville. My call: Tennessee Volunteers 25, Texas A&M Aggies 23.

FIU Panthers vs Delaware Blue Hens is Homecoming in Newark, a 3 p.m. kickoff at Delaware Stadium that also doubles as Military Appreciation and a Celebration of Champions, with a thank-you to the university's faculty and staff on top of it. Henrietta "Hen" Lofland, a librarian by day, has checked out every book on Homecoming traditions just to be thorough, and she has returned them all on time, because of course she has.

Hen: Small state, big Saturdays, Lourdes. Welcome to Homecoming.

Lourdes Ibarguen-Tate has flown up from Sweetwater with a thermos of cafecito and a warning from her abuela, who told her to wear a real coat this time.

Lourdes: My abuela says November up here is not weather, it's a punishment. She also says we win today. She said it first, so it counts.

Hen: Your abuela is welcome at my tailgate. I'll even let her choose the music.

These two have met once, last September in Miami, and Delaware won it 38-16. Lourdes remembers it. Lourdes would prefer to remember it differently.

Lourdes: That was a long night. I don't talk about it. My abuela doesn't talk about it either, and she talks about everything.

Delaware is 4-5 in this new chapter of Blue Hens football, and Hen loves every page of it. The offense can really go. Delaware scores 30.3 points a game, and Nick Minicucci has 1,885 throwing yards, 16 touchdowns and only four interceptions. He threw for 414 yards at Western Kentucky and 408 at Kennesaw State last week, in a 42-40 loss that still has Hen muttering. Sean Wilson has 639 receiving yards, Bryson Graves caught seven passes for 125 against the Owls, and Blake Matthews has five sacks.

Hen: Nick Minicucci reads a defense like I read a card catalog. Quietly, carefully and then all at once.

Lourdes: That's very nice, Hen. Our defense eats card catalogs for breakfast.

FIU is also 4-5, and the Panthers are built differently. The defense allows just 20.3 points a game, and DeeJay Holmes Jr. has seven sacks. JJ Kohl has thrown for 2,035 yards, and Maguire Anderson has 610 receiving yards. The big news is Devonte Lyons, who ran for 216 yards and two touchdowns in last week's 23-20 win over Missouri State.

Lourdes: Two hundred sixteen yards, Hen. Devonte Lyons ran like he smelled croquetas at the other end of the field.

Hen: I'd run that fast for croquetas too. I'm a librarian, not a saint.

The Panthers have been in plenty of tight ones. They lost 27-24 at Jacksonville State, 26-23 to Middle Tennessee and 16-10 at Florida Atlantic, so a close game in the fourth quarter won't rattle them. Delaware has been in its share of shootouts, including a 61-38 win over Missouri State on Senior Day back in October.

The key for FIU is the ground game. If Lyons can keep running the way he did last week, the Panthers can shorten the game, keep Minicucci on the sideline and give their defense a chance to rest. For Delaware, it's protecting Minicucci from Holmes. If he has time, he will find Wilson and Graves, and Delaware Stadium will get very loud very fast.

Hen: You know what Homecoming means here, Lourdes? Alumni coming back to see what this program is becoming. It's a new chapter. Nobody skips to the end.

Lourdes: My abuela always skips to the end. She says life is short and dominoes are long.

Military Appreciation gives the afternoon some extra meaning, too, and both of them agree on one thing: thanking the people who serve matters more than any score.

Hen: If we win, I'm doing a bird pun so bad you'll have to report it.

Lourdes: If we win, I'm calling my abuela from the parking lot, and she's going to say she told me so.

The Blue Hens win it, so brace yourself for Hen's bird pun. My call: Delaware Blue Hens 28, Florida International Panthers 22.

Orlando books two loud stages for Saturday of Week 11. Vans Warped Tour plugs in at the Camping World Stadium campus downtown, while out east the Arizona State vs UCF spread reads UCF −3 with a 48.5 over/under at the Acrisure Bounce House, and my pick is UCF Knights −3 and Over 48.5.

Knox Brevard-Stiles, a ride engineer who swears the Bounce House stands really move, is still dizzy from the last drop. "We won 33-32 at Kansas. Alonza Barnett III threw for 251 yards, and Josh Derry caught eight balls for 143. One week after Baylor beat us 41-9. That's a full loop in seven days."

Skylar Vanterpool flew in from Tempe with sunscreen in November. "Hydrate and dominate, Knox. Jake Fette went 13 of 19 for 187 against Colorado, Reed Harris has 907 receiving yards and nine touchdowns, and we won the last meeting 35-31."

She's right about Harris and right about 2024. Here's my problem with the Sun Devils on this trip: they have played three true road games and lost all three, 20-48 at Texas A&M, 25-53 at Texas Tech and 20-27 at BYU. They have also cycled through three quarterbacks, Cutter Boley, Mikey Keene and, most recently, Fette, who has taken the throws in each of the last two games. UCF has its own two-man room in Keyone Jenkins and Barnett, but both have won games this year, and the Knights score 30.1 points a game at home and away while Arizona State allows 27.3.

Three points is a short lap for the home team. My final is UCF Knights 29, Arizona State Sun Devils 24, a five-point game that clears the 3 with room to spare.

The over/under has already dropped. DraftKings opened it at 52.5, and it was down to 48.5 by Monday morning. I'll take the dip. UCF allows 26.0 a game, Arizona State scores 28.4, and Cardae Mack has 603 rushing yards to keep the clock moving. Duke Watson adds 596 for the Knights. Two run games plus Harris and Derry gets you to 53 without anyone needing a miracle, so I'm on the Over 48.5.

The room mostly agrees with me. The Formula has UCF 29-25, sits on UCF −3 without loving it, and likes the Over. Next Man Up likes UCF and the Over at 32-24. In The Trenches likes UCF at 28-21 and makes no over/under call. Letdown Watch breaks ranks with Arizona State +3 at 27-26, though it likes the Over too. The Formula: "And Letdown Watch brought a beach towel to Orlando. Somebody check its pulse."

Warped Tour will keep the guitars loud downtown into Sunday. The Bounce House needs only four quarters, and I trust the Knights' offense to rattle more bleachers than the Sun Devils can quiet.

UCF insider Knox Brevard-Stiles, a theme-park ride engineer, swears the Acrisure Bounce House will out-shake every mosh pit downtown, and Arizona State insider Skylar Vanterpool says Jake Fette, Reed Harris and the Sun Devils packed sunscreen for a November road win.

Knox: Welcome to Orlando, Skylar. Downtown has Third Eye Blind, Simple Plan and Jimmy Eat World this weekend. We have a stadium that moves when the students jump. Keep your hands inside the stadium at all times.

Skylar: Knox, I came from Tempe, where November is still pool weather. A bouncing bleacher does not scare me. Hydrate and dominate.

Here's why both of them showed up a little jittery. UCF just survived the wildest ride of its season, a 33-32 win at Kansas. Alonza Barnett III threw for 251 yards and two touchdowns, and Josh Derry caught eight balls for 143 yards and a score. One week earlier, Baylor beat the Knights 41-9 in Orlando, so this fan base did the full loop-the-loop in seven days.

Knox: That isn't a slump and a rebound. That's a launch track. You never judge a coaster by the first hill.

Skylar: You judge it by how many people need a bench afterward.

Arizona State's road has been just as twisty. The Sun Devils beat Colorado 20-10 last Saturday. Fette went 13 of 19 for 187 yards and a touchdown, and Harris caught four balls for 103 yards and a score. Harris has 52 catches for 907 yards and nine touchdowns this season, the kind of production that makes a secondary check where the exits are.

Skylar: Reed Harris is my entire personality right now. Long strides, soft hands, zero fear. Your safeties are going to need a cooldown tent.

Knox: Our safeties have Tackett Curtis behind them. Fifty-nine tackles. He meets people at the bottom of the drop.

The quarterback story is a two-park ticket of its own, minus the gift shop. Arizona State has had three different quarterbacks lead it in throws this fall: Cutter Boley early, then Mikey Keene, then Fette the last two weeks. Boley still owns the team lead with 1,360 yards and 13 touchdowns. UCF has two. Keyone Jenkins leads the Knights with 1,181 yards and 11 touchdowns, and he went 19 of 20 against TCU, but Barnett handled the throwing at Kansas.

Knox: Two quarterbacks, one ride. Jenkins was nearly perfect against TCU. Barnett went into Lawrence and came home with a win. Either one can sit in the front car.

Skylar: We've had three. That's not a quarterback room, Knox. That's a carpool. And the carpool keeps arriving.

Baylor Bears vs BYU Cougars begins long before kickoff on Canyon Road, where Cougar Canyon opens three and a half hours before the game and the Cougar Walk routes players and coaches straight through a corridor of fans outside LaVell Edwards Stadium. Bryce Halvorsen-Tuilagi has been on Canyon Road since Cougar Canyon opened, talking about Bear Bachmeier like the Walk is already a highlight reel. Magnolia "Maggie" Whitlock carries the Baylor flag into Provo with DJ Lagway's touchdown total written on a napkin from the drive.

Bryce: Bachmeier throws it and runs it. Glasker wins the route. Cougar Canyon will be loud for that.

Maggie: Lagway has 15 touchdowns. Freeman has 852 yards. Your canyon still has to hear us.

BYU is 7-2 after a 20-28 loss at Utah that snapped some of the November shine. Baylor just beat Iowa State 42-31 and scored 31.9 points a game overall while allowing 17.0. The Cougars score 31.0 and allow 19.8. That is a Big 12 game between two offenses that can hurt you and two defenses that can keep a Saturday from turning into a track meet.

Bear Bachmeier has 2,022 passing yards with 13 touchdowns and eight interceptions, plus 395 rushing yards and seven scores with his legs. Legend Glasker has 703 receiving yards. Tausili Akana has 3.5 sacks. Cade Uluave has 59 tackles. When Bachmeier gets downhill, Edwards Stadium starts sounding like a place that forgot last week's final in Salt Lake City.

Baylor's answer is Lagway and a defense that has been stingy all fall. Lagway has 1,900 yards. Caden Knighten has 361 rushing yards. Gavin Freeman has 69 catches. Garrick Ponder has 4 sacks. Travion Barnes has 63 tackles. The Bears do not need to out-Provo Provo. They need to keep Bachmeier from ending drives early and then let Lagway answer.

Maggie: The Walk is nice. A third-down stop is nicer.

Bryce: The Canyon is nice. Bachmeier in the end zone is nicer.

Provo will treat the afternoon like a festival that happens to include football. Baylor will treat it like a road test that can still reshape a résumé. One of those moods usually wins in November, and Edwards Stadium will decide which one before Cougar Canyon packs up for the night.

Bryce will talk Bachmeier. Maggie will talk Lagway. The Canyon will talk about whether the Walk led to a finish.

Cougar Canyon stays open until 30 minutes before kickoff, which is enough time for a full festival and a football argument. BYU wants Bachmeier to look like the dual-threat problem Utah just slowed down. Baylor wants Lagway to look like the quarterback who lit up Iowa State. Edwards Stadium will get both wishes for a while. Only one will still be standing when the Canyon lights shut off.

Bryce keeps talking about Bachmeier's legs. Maggie keeps talking about Lagway's arm. Provo will decide which one traveled better.

Big 12 road trips to Provo are a full sensory test. The Canyon noise, the Walk, the altitude talk, the early jump balls. Baylor has already proved it can score on anybody in this league. BYU has already proved it can defend enough to stay in every November conversation. The team that wins the first two third downs will probably win the afternoon, and both coaching staffs know it.

Lagway will keep throwing it. Bachmeier will keep running it. Edwards Stadium will keep asking which one breaks first.

Provo will sell the Walk. Baylor will sell the answers. Somebody has to sell a stop.

The Walk will be packed. The stands will be louder. Somebody still has to win third down.

Provo gets its Walk first and its win second. My call: BYU Cougars 27, Baylor Bears 21.

display.story_text:
Hesburgh Library has an exhibit on the Irish nation's sacrifices hanging in its rare books room this weekend, and Boston College walks into Notre Dame Stadium needing a little of that courage. My Boston College vs Notre Dame pick against the spread is Notre Dame Fighting Irish −29.5, with Under 52.5 on the over/under, and I know that's a lot of points to ask of anybody in Week 11.

Declan Moriarty-Chen, who can recite Notre Dame schedules back to the leather helmets, opens with a thesis. "I would posit that CJ Carr has thrown 21 touchdowns and one interception. One. He just went 29 of 40 for 319 yards and three scores against Miami."

Siobhan Dunleavy, Boston College's resident debate champ, objects before he finishes. "Mason McKenzie leads us in throwing and running, Declan. He has 676 rushing yards. You can't tackle an argument you can't catch."

The Irish can carry the big number, and this is how. Notre Dame allows 14.6 points a game. Boston College scores 21.9 and just went to Duke and scored two points in a 2-47 loss. The Irish have beaten the Eagles five straight times in this series since 2017, by scores of 49-20, 40-7, 45-31, 44-0 and 25-10, and two of those margins topped this spread. At home this year Notre Dame beat Rice 52-0 and Stanford 58-7.

The Eagles do get one honest argument from me. McKenzie is a load on the ground, and Bo MacCormack III ran for 105 yards against Florida State. If Boston College can keep the ball, the clock becomes its friend. That's exactly why I trust the Under as much as the side.

DraftKings opened Notre Dame −31.5, and the market has come down two points. I'm fine there. Nolan James Jr. has nine rushing touchdowns, Jordan Faison has 574 receiving yards, and Micah Gilbert caught two scores against Miami. My final is Notre Dame Fighting Irish 41, Boston College Eagles 9, a 32-point margin and 50 combined points, which keeps me under 52.5.

The room is crowded on my side of the field. Next Man Up likes Notre Dame −29.5 and likes the Under at 42-8. Letdown Watch likes the Irish too, 43-9, and has the Under without loving it. The Formula has Notre Dame 40-11 but sits on Boston College +29.5 and the Under. In The Trenches has no side and no over/under call on this one. Follow The Money is still waiting on a consensus spread, so its side is pending, and it has no total pick.

Next Man Up: "Forty-two to eight. The Formula took the Eagles because it felt sorry for the visitors' bus."

The Formula: "Next Man Up thinks every Saturday ends in a shutout. Ask Rice how that felt."

Siobhan will argue every snap, and she should. But Notre Dame has the quarterback, the defense and the series history, and Saturday at the Stadium feels like the Irish keep writing the chapter.

Notre Dame Fighting Irish 41, Boston College Eagles 9. Notre Dame Fighting Irish cover the 29.5. Under 52.5.

display.fanatic_story:
Boston College Eagles vs Notre Dame Fighting Irish in Week 11 arrives the same weekend Hesburgh Library is showing "The Delirium of the Brave: Sacrifice for the Soul of the Irish Nation" in its rare books room, so two very Irish fan bases are walking past the same history on the way to Notre Dame Stadium. Notre Dame insider Declan Moriarty-Chen has already read every placard twice, and Boston College insider Siobhan Dunleavy says Mason McKenzie and the Eagles are here to file a formal objection to the whole idea of an easy afternoon.

Declan: Siobhan, I would posit that you chose the most dangerous possible weekend to visit. We have an Irish history exhibit in the library, the Marching Band parading from the Main Building on Friday afternoon and an organ concert in the Basilica called Thunder from the Sky.

Siobhan: Objection. Boston has been Irish for a long, long time, Declan. We brought our own thunder, and it's wicked loud.

The trouble for Siobhan is that the recent history in this series belongs to the Golden Dome. Notre Dame has won all five meetings since 2017: 49-20, 40-7, 45-31, 44-0 and 25-10. The Irish are 8-1, ranked No. 11, and their only loss came at BYU, 28-24.

Declan: Five straight. I keep them in a binder with tabs. The 44-0 tab is laminated.

Siobhan: The 25-10 tab is the newest one, Declan. That's a trend of a different sort. Every year we get closer to the courtroom door.

Here's what Siobhan is selling. Mason McKenzie is the whole Boston College offense in one jersey. He leads the Eagles with 1,616 throwing yards and 10 touchdowns, and he also leads them in rushing with 676 yards and five scores on 145 carries. Against Florida State last week, Bo MacCormack III ran 16 times for 105 yards and a touchdown in a 31-24 loss that stayed close all afternoon.

Siobhan: McKenzie runs like he's late for a final exam. You can't defend a quarterback who refuses to stay in the pocket. That's not a scheme, that's a closing argument.

Declan: And Notre Dame's defense is the judge. We give up 14.6 points a game. The jury has been seated since September.

The Irish have their own exhibit hall of weapons. CJ Carr has thrown for 2,168 yards with 21 touchdowns and one interception all season. Against Miami last Saturday he went 29 of 40 for 319 yards and three scores, and Micah Gilbert caught nine balls for 98 yards and two touchdowns. Nolan James Jr. has run for 571 yards and nine scores, and Jordan Faison leads the receivers with 574 yards.

Declan: One interception. One. I've seen more turnovers at a bake sale outside the Basilica.

Siobhan: Give it time. The rare books room has plenty of stories about the mighty getting humbled.

Boston College's defense has some fight in it. Linebacker Anthony Palano has 76 tackles, and Demetrius Ballard has 4.5 sacks. The problem is the scoreboard on the road. The Eagles lost 47-2 at Duke two weeks ago, and they lost at Cincinnati and SMU too, with their lone road win a 49-27 shootout at Georgia Tech.

Declan: I don't want to bring up Duke.

Siobhan: Then don't. That game has been sealed by court order.

The Irish defense up front is led by Boubacar Traore with four sacks, and Drayk Bowen leads the team with 45 tackles. At home this fall, Notre Dame beat Rice 52-0, Stanford 58-7, Michigan State 27-10 and Miami 31-24. The Stadium has been a hard place to make a point.

Siobhan: Here's my plan. McKenzie keeps it, Palano hits somebody, and we keep the ball long enough to make Carr sit on the bench and read a book.

Declan: That's a good plan. It is also the same plan the last five Boston College teams brought. The exhibit upstairs is about the brave. It isn't about the ones who won.

There is real affection under the arguing. These are two Catholic schools with deep Irish roots, and both fan bases will walk past the same Dome and the same Basilica before kickoff. One of them walks back out a lot happier.

Siobhan: If we pull this off, I'm taking a photo with the exhibit and captioning it "Sustained."

Declan: If we win big, I'm adding a sixth tab to the binder and calling it Exhibit F.

Siobhan: Objection.

Declan: Overruled. The exhibit room closes at five on Friday. Bring a pencil.

Declan gets his history lesson, plus a blowout for extra credit. My call: Notre Dame Fighting Irish 41, Boston College Eagles 9.

The Cal vs Virginia spread is Virginia −12.5 and the over/under is 47.5, and I'm taking Virginia Cavaliers −12.5 with the Over 47.5 in a Week 11 game where both teams are trying to end three-game skids.

Pribula is efficient, and Da'Shawn Martin has six touchdown catches on 26 grabs.

I won't pretend Virginia's last outing was pretty. Wake Forest beat the Cavaliers 51-7. Cal's last game was rough too, and both teams have had an extra week to stew. Coming off the same week of rest, I'd rather back the team with the better home form and the quarterback who protects the ball.

display.fanatic_story:
Charlottesville sets aside Saturday for its annual Heroes Appreciation Game at Scott Stadium, and the California Golden Bears vs Virginia Cavaliers matchup in Week 11 gets an extra jolt of purpose from it. Virginia insider Prescott Ashby-Lowell plans to thank every veteran in his section before kickoff, while Cal insider Quentin Oyelaran-Fitch has flown cross-country with a hand-lettered sign that reads "Jaron-Keawe Sagapolutele for Mayor."

Prescott: Welcome to the Grounds, Quentin. Through the Seats for Service program, fans can buy $25 tickets that Virginia Athletics donates to veterans and active-duty service members. Mr. Jefferson would approve.

Quentin: That's the most Berkeley thing a Virginia fan has ever said to me. I respect it. I'm still here to organize a peaceful takeover of your end zone.

This is only the second meeting ever between these programs. Last year in Berkeley, Kam Robinson's fifth career interception with under a minute left sealed a 31-21 Virginia road win, and Quentin has been drafting a strongly worded essay about it ever since.

Quentin: Under a minute, Prescott. Under a minute. I have a whole dissertation chapter on that throw.

Prescott: Chapter one should be titled "Kam Robinson Was There."

Both sides arrive a little bruised. Each is trying to snap a three-game skid. Virginia lost to SMU, Duke and then Wake Forest, 51-7, in its last game on Oct. 31. Cal dropped games to Wake Forest, SMU and NC State. Both teams had last weekend off, so neither fan base can blame fatigue.

Prescott: An extra week of rest is how a gentleman prepares. We spent ours studying tape and sending a formal letter of complaint to the Wake Forest scoreboard.

Quentin: We spent ours in a teach-in. The topic was tackling.

Home has been kind to the Hoos. Virginia is 4-1 at Scott Stadium this season and has won 10 of its last 12 games there since 2025. The Cavaliers beat NC State 34-8, Delaware 42-3 and Syracuse 28-25 on the Grounds, and their lone home loss was 19-16 to Duke. On the road, Cal's only win this season came at Syracuse, 21-18, back on Sept. 12.

Quentin: One road win is not a flaw. It's a rare edition. Collectors pay extra.

Prescott: Collectors also check the condition, my friend.

The Virginia offense runs through Beau Pribula, who has thrown for 1,581 yards with 14 touchdowns and only three interceptions. Jekail Middlebrook leads the ground game with 513 yards, and Da'Shawn Martin has turned 26 catches into 366 yards and six touchdowns. In the Wake Forest game, Martin still caught nine balls for 119 yards.

Prescott: Pribula protects the football the way Mr. Jefferson guarded his books. Carefully.

Quentin: Sagapolutele has thrown for 1,751 yards and 11 touchdowns. He once threw for 413 yards against Wagner. That's not a quarterback, that's a movement.

Cal's top target is Chase Hendricks, who has 61 catches for 565 yards and four touchdowns, and he caught seven for 67 and a score at NC State. Adam Mohammed leads the backfield with 363 yards. On defense, AJ Tuitele has 52 tackles and JD McKinley has three sacks.

Virginia's front is the scariest thing Quentin has to protest. Matthew Fobbs-White has five sacks, and Maddox Marcellus leads the Cavaliers with 44 tackles.

Quentin: Fobbs-White is a five-sack argument. I need a bigger sign.

Prescott: Bring two. The man reads quarterbacks like a newspaper.

The hard truth for the Bears is the scoreboard against them. Cal allows 31.6 points a game, and SMU put up 59 on them in October. Virginia scores 25.9 a game and gives up 23.1, and it looked much more like itself at home than on the road.

Quentin: Here's my manifesto. Sagapolutele to Hendricks early. Tuitele everywhere. Nobody mentions the Wagner game, because it'll make the Hoos feel bad.

Prescott: Here's my reply, written in fountain pen. Pribula keeps it clean, Martin finds the end zone, Fobbs-White visits your quarterback, and every veteran in the house gets a standing ovation at the first media timeout.

Quentin: I'll stand for that part. Only that part.

Prescott: That's all the Grounds ask. Well, that and a win.

Quentin's sign stays up. So does Virginia. My call: Virginia Cavaliers 31, California Golden Bears 17.

Bloomington has a full Saturday planned, with the musical SIX running matinee and evening shows at IU Auditorium on either side of a 3:30 kickoff at Memorial Stadium. In the USC vs Indiana spread battle, I'm on Indiana Hoosiers −7.5 and the Over 49.5, with a Week 11 crowd chasing something that has never happened.

The Daily Hoosier puts it plainly: Indiana has never beaten USC. Mallory Penhallow, the Indiana season-ticket holder who keeps a 40-tab spreadsheet on the Hoosiers, has highlighted that sentence in crimson. "Tobi Osunsanmi has 10 sacks. Josh Hoover has 19 touchdowns and two interceptions. Grace in victory, Sterling. We'll practice."

Sterling Ashworth-Vance, the USC film-school grad, answers in trailer voice. "In a world where Indiana hasn't scored 24 since early October, one quarterback has thrown for 2,524 yards and 20 touchdowns. Jayden Maiava. Coming to Bloomington."

He has a point about the recent scripts. Indiana beat Michigan 13-6 in overtime and Minnesota 23-16 in overtime, and Hoover went 8 of 18 and 8 of 19 in those games. The market noticed. DraftKings opened Indiana −10.5 with 58.5 on the over/under, and it's down to −7.5 and 49.5.

That move is why I like both sides of my ticket at these prices. Indiana's defense allows 12.4 points a game, the best number on this field, and Osunsanmi is the most disruptive player in the game. USC lost 7-24 at Wisconsin, its only road loss, against the kind of defense it sees again here. Both teams had last week off, so nobody gets a rest bump.

The Over is about talent over recent box scores. Indiana still scores 32.4 points a game, and Charlie Becker has 875 receiving yards and nine scores, with eight catches for 149 against Minnesota. Turbo Richard has 745 rushing yards. USC scores 32.4 too, gives up 24.2 and has King Miller's 680 rushing yards plus Trent Mosley, who had 101 receiving yards against Ohio State. A total that fell nine points from its open is a gift if either offense wakes up, and I think Indiana's does.

My final is Indiana Hoosiers 31, USC Trojans 20. That's 11 points, past the 7.5, and 51 combined, over the 49.5.

The room lines up with me for once. The Formula has Indiana 29-22 and sits on Indiana −7.5 and the Over. Next Man Up has the same side and Over at 30-21. Letdown Watch likes Indiana −7.5 at 33-17 and has the Over. In The Trenches has no side and no over/under call this week. Follow The Money is still waiting on a consensus spread, so its side is pending, and it has no total pick.

Letdown Watch: "Thirty-three to seventeen. The Formula left seven points on the IU Auditorium stage."

The Formula: "Letdown Watch thinks Paddy McAteer bails Indiana out every week. He did it once."

The queens of SIX get two curtain calls Saturday. Indiana gets one chance at a first, and I think the Hoosiers take it with the defense doing the singing.
