display.fanatic_story:
USC Trojans vs Indiana Hoosiers in Week 11 shares a Bloomington Saturday with the musical SIX, which plays IU Auditorium at 1 p.m. and 8 p.m., so the 3:30 kickoff at Memorial Stadium sits right between two shows about six queens fighting for the crown. Indiana insider Mallory Penhallow calls that "perfectly on brand," and USC insider Sterling Ashworth-Vance says Jayden Maiava and the Trojans are here to steal the third act.

Sterling: In a world where one program has never lost to the other, a visitor arrives from Los Angeles. He brings a quarterback. He brings a running back. He does not bring a winter coat.

Mallory: Sterling, you're right about one thing, and the Daily Hoosier said it first. Indiana has never beaten USC. That's not a curse. That's a streak with an expiration date.

That is the stake in Bloomington. The Hoosiers are 8-1 and ranked No. 4, the Trojans are 7-2 and ranked No. 20, and both teams spent last weekend resting. USC arrives hot after a 30-18 win over Ohio State, while Indiana is coming off back-to-back overtime wins over Michigan, 13-6, and Minnesota, 23-16.

Sterling: Two overtimes in a row? That's not a season, Mallory. That's a director's cut.

Mallory: And both endings were happy. Did you see Paddy McAteer? Sixty yards to tie Minnesota with two seconds left. Program record. Big Ten co-special teams player of the week. I screamed so loud the guy behind me checked my pulse.

The Indiana defense is the main reason Mallory sleeps at night. The Hoosiers give up 12.4 points a game, and Tobi Osunsanmi has 10 sacks, the kind of season that gets a quarterback to check the stands for exits. Isaiah Jones leads the team with 67 tackles.

Mallory: Tobi is the showstopper. Ten sacks. When he gets home from practice, the furniture braces itself.

Sterling: Our quarterback has been sacked by better choreography. Maiava has thrown for 2,524 yards with 20 touchdowns and five interceptions. Against Ohio State he was 15 of 22 for 222 yards. Efficient. Cinematic. Oscar-worthy.

The Trojans' supporting cast is real. King Miller has 680 rushing yards and five touchdowns, and he scored against Ohio State. Trent Mosley has 512 receiving yards and six touchdowns, and he went for 101 yards against the Buckeyes. On defense, Deven Bryant has 55 tackles, and safety Kennedy Urlacher leads the team with three sacks.

Sterling: Kennedy Urlacher. Say it slow. It sounds like a closing credit.

Mallory: It sounds like a guy who's about to meet Charlie Becker.

Becker is Indiana's leading man. He has 50 catches for 875 yards and nine touchdowns, and he caught eight balls for 149 yards against Minnesota. Josh Hoover has thrown 19 touchdowns against two interceptions, though he went 8 of 19 against the Gophers. Turbo Richard leads the backfield with 745 yards and six scores.

Sterling: Your quarterback went 8 of 19 and you're calling it a hit?

Mallory: Sterling, we won. In Bloomington we call that a win. Then I opened tab 41 and found the problem. It's fixed.

USC has its own weak spot to hide. The Trojans lost 24-7 at Wisconsin, their only road loss, and Big Ten weather in November is not a soundstage. They did win at Rutgers 42-35 and at Penn State 31-23, so Sterling is not packing light.

Sterling: Penn State. Happy Valley. Night game energy. We walked in there like a premiere and walked out with the reviews.

Mallory: Memorial Stadium in November will be colder and louder. Bring a scarf. Bring two.

Both offenses score 32.4 points a game, which is a funny coincidence and a real problem for anybody who wants a quiet afternoon. The difference is the defense. USC gives up 24.2 points a game. Indiana gives up about half that.

Mallory: Here's the whole show. Osunsanmi puts Maiava on his back, Becker breaks loose, and Hoover walks off with the game ball.

Sterling: Here's the trailer. One quarterback. One road trip. One history book that refuses to change. Coming this Saturday.

Mallory: The queens in SIX get two curtain calls Saturday. We only need one.

Sterling: Roll credits.

Mallory: Not yet. Final act's ours.

First the Hoosiers make history at Memorial Stadium, then SIX gets the night show. My call: Indiana Hoosiers 31, USC Trojans 20.

display.story_text:
Oregon's game page carries two words for Saturday, "Wear Green," and Eugene will show up that way at Autzen Stadium. The Michigan vs Oregon spread is Oregon −10.5 with a 39.5 over/under, and my Week 11 pick is Oregon Ducks −10.5 with the Over 39.5.

Phoenix "Nix" Wyatt-Aldana, the Eugene sneaker designer who keeps a scouting note on every Oregon route tree, is still riding high from Columbus. "We won 41-28 at Ohio State. Dylan Raiola threw for 257 yards, and Dierre Hill Jr. scored twice. Ten out of ten, uniform and execution."

Augustin "Gus" Hartwell, Michigan's maize-sweater stats savant, has a different exhibit. "Our defense has allowed 16.2 points a game and has not given up more than 21 all season. Michigan Monday says we're fourth in the country in yards allowed."

Gus is right, and that's why the over/under crashed. DraftKings opened this game at Oregon −13.5 with 53.5 on the over/under, and by Monday morning it was −10.5 and 39.5, a 14-point drop on the over/under. I think the market went too far. Michigan's offense is the problem in this matchup, not its defense. Tommy Carr went 14 of 26 with two interceptions in a 15-6 loss to Michigan State, and the Wolverines have scored 19.6 points a game.

That's also my side. Oregon scores 34.1 points a game, and its offense has scored 34 or more in five of nine games. Raiola has 11 touchdown throws against two interceptions, and Dakorien Moore has seven receiving scores. Michigan has dropped two of its last three, and in losses to Indiana and Michigan State it scored six points each time. Asking that offense to keep pace on the road at Autzen is a tall order.

My final is Oregon Ducks 29, Michigan Wolverines 15. That's a 14-point margin, past the 10.5, and 44 combined, over the 39.5.

Here's the room. The Formula has Oregon 29-18, sits on Oregon −10.5 and likes the Over. Next Man Up likes Oregon −10.5 at 30-11 and has the Over. Letdown Watch has Oregon −10.5 at 29-17 and likes the Over. In The Trenches has no side and no over/under call here. Follow The Money is still waiting on a consensus spread, so its side is pending, and it has no total pick.

Next Man Up: "Thirty to eleven. The Formula gave Michigan seven extra points for good manners."

Letdown Watch: "Next Man Up thinks Michigan's offense took a red-eye and never landed. It still has JJ Buchanan."

Buchanan, with 646 receiving yards, is the one Wolverine who can change my math, and John Henry Daley's six sacks can make Raiola uncomfortable. I still think Oregon gets to 29, and Michigan's defense can't win this alone.

Green is the dress code in Eugene. The Ducks look ready to match it with a double-digit win.

Oregon Ducks 29, Michigan Wolverines 15. Oregon Ducks cover the 10.5. Over 39.5.

Eugene has its Saturday dress code posted: Oregon's game page for Michigan Wolverines vs Oregon Ducks in Week 11 says "Wear Green," and the Lane County Farmers Market will be selling greens downtown until 2 p.m., an hour and a half after the 12:30 p.m. Pacific kickoff at Autzen Stadium. Oregon insider Phoenix "Nix" Wyatt-Aldana has a custom green jacket ready, and Michigan insider Augustin "Gus" Hartwell has packed a maize sweater and a spreadsheet that says Dylan Raiola is about to face one of the stingiest defenses in the country.

Nix: Gus, welcome to the greenest stadium in America. Look at it. Wall-to-wall green, and every one of them is going to scream through your third downs. Ten out of ten before anybody even kicks off.

Gus: Nix, I respect the paint job. But I'm an engineer. I don't care what color the crowd wears. I care that our defense has allowed 16.2 points a game.

This is only the seventh meeting between these two programs, and the all-time series is tied at three wins apiece, according to Michigan's weekly notes. Michigan won the first three, in 1948, 1960 and 1973. Oregon won the last three, in 2003, 2007 and 2024, when the Ducks went into Michigan Stadium and won 38-17. Michigan is 0-1 all time at Autzen.

Gus: Three and three. That's a perfectly balanced equation. I would like to solve for x on Saturday.

Nix: Solve for green, Gus. The answer is always green.

Oregon comes in walking ten feet tall. The Ducks won 41-28 at Ohio State last Saturday. Raiola went 25 of 40 for 257 yards and two touchdowns, Dierre Hill Jr. ran for 75 yards and two scores, and Dakorien Moore caught a touchdown among his seven grabs.

Nix: Columbus was a clinic. Forty-one points in the Horseshoe. Clean throws, sharp cuts, two Hill touchdowns. I'd frame that game film and hang it over the fireplace.

Gus: And I'd frame our defense. Nobody has scored more than 21 on us all season. Michigan's notes say we're fourth in the nation in yards allowed, and the Associated Press says we're the 15th team in the last 15 seasons to hold every one of its first nine opponents to 21 or fewer.

That defense is the real thing. Linebacker Troy Bowles leads it with 72 tackles, and John Henry Daley has six sacks and 9.0 tackles for loss. The offense is where Gus begins staring at the ceiling. Michigan scores 19.6 points a game, and it lost to Michigan State 15-6 last week. Tommy Carr, whose first game as the No. 1 quarterback came against Indiana, went 14 of 26 for 138 yards with two interceptions against the Spartans.

Gus: Tommy Carr went 22 of 27 at Rutgers two weeks ago. Michigan's notes call it the best completion rate ever for a freshman in that role at Michigan. I have the decimal points.

Nix: I have the scoreboard. Six points last week. That's a sample-size problem and a style problem.

Michigan's best weapon in Nix's nightmares is JJ Buchanan, who has 40 catches for 646 yards and five touchdowns. Andrew Marsh has 44 catches. Oregon's defense lives on Matayo Uiagalelei, who has 7.5 sacks, and Koi Perich, who leads the Ducks with 58 tackles.

Nix: Matayo is a wrecking ball. He shows up in the backfield like he was invited.

Gus: Then Carr gets it out quick to Buchanan, and Matayo spends the afternoon chasing.

The Ducks have scored 34.1 points a game this season. They also have a home loss to UCLA, 17-15, in a game where the offense never found its stride, and Gus has written that score on an index card.

Gus: UCLA got you at home. Every engineer knows a structure can crack.

Nix: And every Duck knows you burn last month's tape. We beat Nebraska and Northwestern at Autzen after that.

Here is the matchup that decides it. If Michigan's defense keeps Raiola from hitting Moore downfield, the Wolverines can drag this into the fourth quarter. If Oregon gets Hill going early, Gus's equation runs out of variables.

Gus: Hail to the Victors, Nix. Off-key, but proud.

Nix: Sing it at the farmers market before kickoff. Once we're inside Autzen, the only song anybody hears is Mighty Oregon.

Autzen goes green from top to bottom, and the Ducks send Michigan home quiet. My call: Oregon Ducks 29, Michigan Wolverines 15.

Tulsa brings the alumni home Saturday, and the homecoming guest list at H.A. Chapman Stadium includes the one program that keeps spoiling the party. Florida Atlantic leads the all-time series 4-1, per Tulsa Athletics, and has won the last three meetings, but my FAU vs Tulsa pick is Tulsa Golden Hurricane −5.5 with the Under 74.5 on the over/under for Week 11.

Wiley Pettibone, the petroleum-geology grad who calls every long drive a gusher, has been yelling since Tulane. "We won 60-10 at Tulane. Baylor Hayes went 26 of 33 for 338 yards and four touchdowns, and Oran Singleton Jr. caught 13 balls for 177 and three scores. Gusher!"

Kaia Brightwater, Boca Raton's beach-volleyball scout, is unbothered. "Caden Veltkamp has 27 touchdown throws and five interceptions, Wiley. Easton Messer has 12 touchdown catches. That's a perfect swell. We beat you 63-16 in this building two years ago."

She's right about the swell, and I still want the Hurricane. Florida Atlantic gives up 35.0 points a game. On the road the Owls are 1-3, with losses of 21-66 at Florida, 24-56 at Army and 41-48 at North Texas. Tulsa allows 22.8 points a game and has a quarterback in Hayes who has thrown only two interceptions all year. Kyran Duhon's seven sacks give Tulsa a way to speed up Veltkamp, and Chris Thompson Jr. leads the defense with 84 tackles.

My final is Tulsa Golden Hurricane 37, Florida Atlantic Owls 29. That's eight points, clear of the 5.5.

Then there's the over/under, which is the strangest number on the board. DraftKings opened it at 66.5, and it has climbed to 74.5. I understand why. Florida Atlantic scores 40.2 a game and just put up 60 on UTSA. But eight points of movement is a lot to chase, and my score adds up to 66, right around where the market opened. Tulsa's home games this year finished 24-10, 42-0, 44-45 in overtime and 35-38. Only one of those got past this over/under. Give me the Under 74.5.

The room is mostly with me on both counts. The Formula likes Tulsa −5.5 and likes the Under at 34-26. Letdown Watch likes Tulsa too and likes the Under at 35-27. Next Man Up likes Tulsa at 42-33 but has the Over. In The Trenches has no side and no over/under call here. Follow The Money is still waiting on a consensus spread, so its side is pending, and it has no total pick.

Next Man Up: "Forty-two to thirty-three. The Formula priced this one like a Tuesday in Tulsa."

The Formula: "And Next Man Up priced it like Kaia's beach volleyball tournament. Somebody take away the scoreboard."

Homecoming crowds want to see the old guard return to form. Hayes and Singleton look ready to give them a Saturday worth retelling at the next reunion.

Tulsa Golden Hurricane 37, Florida Atlantic Owls 29. Tulsa Golden Hurricane cover the 5.5. Under 74.5.

display.fanatic_story:
Homecoming week in Tulsa means alumni filling the tailgates around H.A. Chapman Stadium, and Florida Atlantic Owls vs Tulsa Golden Hurricane in Week 11 hands them a guest who has crashed this party before. Tulsa insider Wiley Pettibone wants Baylor Hayes to send everybody home happy, while Florida Atlantic insider Kaia Brightwater reminds him that the Owls lead the all-time series 4-1 and won 63-16 the last time they came to town in 2024.

Wiley: Welcome to homecoming, Kaia. We've got alumni, we've got a crowd, and we've got a quarterback who just struck oil at Tulane.

Kaia: Wiley, I'm from Boca. Every day is homecoming. I brought sunscreen and a scorebook, and I plan to fill one of them.

This is the sixth meeting between the programs, and history tilts hard toward the visitors, as Tulsa's own announcement points out. Florida Atlantic won 20-17 in 2023, 63-16 in Tulsa in 2024 and 40-21 last season. Wiley has been waiting all year to change that sentence.

Wiley: Three in a row is a dry well, Kaia. Dry wells end. You drill a little deeper.

Kaia: Or you move to the beach.

The good news for Wiley is the most recent game. Tulsa traveled to Tulane last Saturday and won 60-10. Hayes went 26 of 33 for 338 yards and four touchdowns, and Oran Singleton Jr. caught 13 balls for 177 yards and three scores. Singleton leads the Golden Hurricane with 712 receiving yards and seven touchdowns, and Damari Alston has run for seven scores.

Wiley: Thirteen catches. Thirteen. I yelled "gusher" so many times my neighbor called the fire department.

Kaia: Nice stat. Here's a bigger one. Caden Veltkamp has thrown for 2,746 yards with 27 touchdowns and five interceptions. He threw for 452 yards at North Texas. He's not a quarterback, he's a tide chart.

Florida Atlantic arrives rested, too. The Owls played last Thursday night and beat UTSA 60-29. Veltkamp threw four touchdowns, Leonard Farrow ran for 126 yards and a score, and Easton Messer caught three touchdowns. Messer has 81 catches for 983 yards and 12 scores, which means Tulsa's secondary has a long afternoon in front of it.

Kaia: Easton Messer finds open water like a dolphin finds a wave. You can't tackle the ocean, Wiley.

Wiley: You can if Kyran Duhon gets there first. Seven sacks. He shows up in the backfield like a pressure gauge about to blow.

Tulsa's defense has been the steadier side of this matchup. The Golden Hurricane give up 22.8 points a game, while Florida Atlantic gives up 35.0. Chris Thompson Jr. leads Tulsa with 84 tackles, and the defense held Oklahoma State to 10 points in the opener.

Kaia: Our defense isn't built to hold anybody to 10. It's built to hand the ball back to Veltkamp as fast as possible. That's a strategy. Ask Rice. We beat them 51-49.

Wiley: Kaia, that's not a strategy. That's a fireworks show with a scoreboard.

The Owls have had a harder time on the road. They lost 66-21 at Florida, 56-24 at Army and 48-41 at North Texas, with their only road win coming 45-17 at UL Monroe. Tulsa, meanwhile, has two home losses by a combined four points, a 45-44 overtime loss to North Texas and a 38-35 loss to Army.

Wiley: Four points, Kaia. We are four points from being perfect at home. That's practically a gusher.

Kaia: It's practically a wipeout. But I'll give you this: your quarterback doesn't hand the ball away. Two interceptions all year.

Wiley: Hayes treats the football like a family deed. Nobody touches it.

So it comes down to Veltkamp and Messer against Hayes, Singleton and a Tulsa defense that has been better at home than the Owls have been on the road. Homecoming brings out the best in a building, and Chapman wants a different ending to this series.

Kaia: If Messer scores early, I'm doing a slow-motion hair flip in your end zone.

Wiley: If Hayes hits Singleton deep, I'm handing out hard hats at the alumni tent.

Kaia: Fine. Save me one. I'll wear it backward.

Hard hats for everybody at Chapman, and a Homecoming win to wear them in. My call: Tulsa Golden Hurricane 37, Florida Atlantic Owls 29.

display.story_text:
Northern Illinois has zero wins and a stadium full of reasons to keep showing up. Saturday is high school senior night for the Huskie Marching Band, and in that Nevada vs Northern Illinois matchup my Week 11 pick against the spread is Northern Illinois Huskies +7 with the Over 46.5.

Nola Brandvik, the DeKalb ag-science grad who talks about wins like corn yields, keeps it dry. "We lost 24-28 to Illinois State and 24-31 at UNLV. Telly Johnson Jr. has 629 rushing yards, DeAree Rogers has 70 catches. The crop is close."

Ridge Corbell, Nevada's ski patroller, shrugs like it's a slow day on the lift. "We beat San José State 28-13 three weeks ago, Nola. EJ Smith has 94 tackles and Dylan LaBarbera has 5.5 sacks. Our defense is fine."

His defense is fine. His offense is the problem, and that's why I'll take the seven. Nevada scored 0 at UCLA and 3 against New Mexico in its last two games, and it has used three quarterbacks this season, Carter Jones, AJ Bianco and Luke Duncan. Jones leads the team with 654 passing yards. The Wolf Pack score 20.8 points a game and are 1-3 on the road. Laying a full touchdown with that offense is asking for trouble.

Northern Illinois is 0-9 for real reasons. It allows 36.8 points a game. But Taron Dickens has thrown for 1,876 yards, and the Huskies just scored 19 at San José State. The market has already moved toward them. DraftKings opened Nevada −10.5, and it is down to −7.

My final is Nevada Wolf Pack 27, Northern Illinois Huskies 21. Six points, inside the seven.

The over/under is the other place I trust the matchup more than the reputations. The number has sat at 46.5 since it opened. Northern Illinois gives up 36.8 a game, so Nevada's sputtering offense should find something. The Huskies have scored at least 17 in six of their nine games. My 27-21 lands at 48, over the 46.5.

The room mostly disagrees with me on the side. The Formula sits on Nevada −7 at 29-21 but likes the Over. Next Man Up and Letdown Watch both have Nevada −7 and the Under at 27-19. In The Trenches likes Northern Illinois +7 at 28-25 and makes no over/under call. Follow The Money is still waiting on a consensus spread, so its side is pending, and it has no total pick.

In The Trenches: "Twenty-eight to twenty-five. Next Man Up and Letdown Watch turned in the same homework."

Next Man Up: "In The Trenches took an 0-9 team. I'll save it a seat at the band's senior night."

A first win would make senior night unforgettable for a lot of kids in red and black. Even without it, I think the Huskies keep this inside a touchdown.

Nevada Wolf Pack 27, Northern Illinois Huskies 21. Northern Illinois Huskies cover the 7. Over 46.5.

display.fanatic_story:
High school band kids from across northern Illinois will be marching at Huskie Stadium on Saturday, because the Huskie Marching Band has made Nevada Wolf Pack vs Northern Illinois Huskies its high school senior night for Week 11. Northern Illinois insider Nola Brandvik wants those seniors to see the first win of the season, while Nevada insider Ridge Corbell has flown in from Reno with a ski jacket and a plan to spoil the party.

Nola: Welcome to DeKalb, Ridge. Kickoff's at 2:30 Central. The band has high school seniors marching with it. Everything is ready except our scoreboard.

Ridge: Nola, I patrol ski slopes for a living. I've seen people lose their skis, their poles and their dignity in one run. An 0-9 season doesn't scare me. It makes me nervous for you.

The record is real. Northern Illinois is 0-9 and 0-5 in conference play. But Nola keeps a notebook of the close ones, and there are a few. The Huskies lost 28-24 to Illinois State in September and 31-24 at UNLV two weeks ago, and they scored 19 at San José State last Saturday.

Nola: A seven-point loss at UNLV isn't a disaster. It's a harvest that came a week late.

Ridge: That's the most Midwestern sentence I've ever heard.

Nevada isn't exactly flying downhill either. The Wolf Pack are 3-6 and have scored three points in their last two games, a 27-0 loss at UCLA and a 31-3 loss to New Mexico. Nevada has used three quarterbacks this year: Carter Jones, AJ Bianco and Luke Duncan. Jones leads the team with 654 throwing yards, while Bianco took most of the throws in each of the last two losses.

Ridge: Three quarterbacks is a full chairlift. We just need one of them to get off at the top.

Nola: We have one quarterback. Taron Dickens. He's thrown for 1,876 yards and nine touchdowns, and he went 26 of 36 for 259 yards at San José State. We don't rotate. We plant.

The Huskies' supporting cast gives Nola something to rest her clipboard on. Telly Johnson Jr. has run for 629 yards and six touchdowns, and DeAree Rogers has 70 catches for 719 yards and five scores. Elijah Porter added 79 rushing yards last week.

Ridge: I'll give you Rogers. Seventy catches is a whole season of snow. But our defense is the real deal. EJ Smith has 94 tackles. Dylan LaBarbera has 5.5 sacks. Those two can turn a sunny day into a whiteout.

Nevada's defense has kept the Wolf Pack in games all fall, allowing 23.6 points a game, and it held San José State to 13 in a 28-13 win in October. Northern Illinois allows 36.8 a game, which is the main reason Nola rubs her temples during the fourth quarter.

Nola: Our defense has been a drought year. Jack Murray has 67 tackles, and he's tried to make every one of them twice.

Ridge: That's a hard-working linebacker.

Nola: That's a DeKalb linebacker. We don't quit. We just keep planting.

Here's the twist neither of them can shake. These programs did not meet at all from 2016 through 2025, so nobody has a recent grudge to carry into the stadium. It's simply the Wolf Pack's road troubles against a Huskies team that badly wants to give its band guests something to celebrate. Nevada is 1-3 in true road games this season, with its only road win coming 30-13 at UTEP.

Ridge: One road win. One. I've had better luck finding a lost glove in a snowbank.

Nola: Then you know how this feels. We've been looking for our glove since September.

When the fourth quarter arrives, Nola wants the ball in Johnson's hands and the band's high school seniors on their feet. Ridge wants LaBarbera chasing Dickens all over the field and the Wolf Pack flying home with a much quieter plane ride.

Ridge: If we win, I'm doing a snowboard backflip on the sideline. Not literally. My knees are not insured.

Nola: If we win, I'm standing in the end zone with the band seniors and singing the fight song off-key until they turn off the lights.

Ridge: Knee-high by the Fourth of July, huh?

Nola: Knee-high by mid-November, Ridge. Some crops take longer.

Band night is loud, but the Huskies still wait on that first win. My call: Nevada Wolf Pack 27, Northern Illinois Huskies 21.

display.story_text:
The third-annual Georgia Grown Bowl puts a farm-state name on a rivalry tied at six wins apiece, per Georgia State Athletics, and the 13th meeting kicks off Saturday at Center Parc Stadium in downtown Atlanta. My Georgia Southern vs Georgia State pick is Georgia State Panthers +5.5 with the Under 56.5, and in Week 11 I want the points with the home team.

Royce Ogeechee grew up on a Bulloch County farm and talks about Georgia Southern like a family heirloom. "Max Johnson went 19 of 26 for 271 yards and four touchdowns against Marshall. Fifteen touchdown throws, two interceptions. That's a harvest, Malik."

Malik Overstreet knows every MARTA stop and every Panthers third-down habit, and he's not impressed. "We just won 39-23 at App State. Ayden Pereira threw three touchdowns, and Lanear McCrary Jr. ran 21 times for 123 yards. Xavier Esqillion has nine sacks. Get off at Georgia State station and wait for us."

Both men have a case, and that's why five and a half points matter. Georgia Southern has won three straight and sits first in the Sun Belt East at 4-1. But the Eagles lost on the road at Jacksonville State 27-31 and won only 31-24 at Coastal Carolina. Georgia State is 3-1 at home, scores 34.4 points a game and has Esqillion to make Johnson move. Rodshaun Dorsey has nine touchdown catches on 29 grabs, the scoring threat Georgia Southern has to find first.

The last ten meetings split 5-5, and Georgia Southern won the most recent two, 38-21 and 41-24. That's real, but nobody has owned this series for long.

My final is Georgia Southern Eagles 28, Georgia State Panthers 25. A three-point game sits well inside the 5.5.

On the over/under, I'm on the Under 56.5. DraftKings opened it at 55.5 and it has ticked up a point. Georgia State's offense is the reason the number is this high, but Georgia Southern's defense has been the steadier group. Anthony Bynum has five sacks, and the Eagles held App State to three points two weeks ago. My 28-25 lands at 53, clear of the 56.5.

The room loves the Panthers. The Formula likes Georgia State +5.5 and likes the Under at 28-25. Next Man Up likes Georgia State +5.5 too, with the Panthers winning 29-28, but has the Over. Letdown Watch has Georgia State +5.5 and likes the Under at 28-25. In The Trenches likes Georgia State +5.5 at 30-22 and makes no over/under call. Follow The Money is still waiting on a consensus spread, so its side is pending, and it has no total pick.

Next Man Up: "Twenty-nine to twenty-eight, Panthers. The Formula and Letdown Watch copied each other's homework again."

In The Trenches: "Next Man Up went Over in a rivalry game. Somebody check its fuel gauge."

Royce wants a third straight win in this series. Malik wants the Georgia Grown trophy staying downtown. I think the Eagles get the win and the Panthers keep it close. Georgia Southern allows 19.7 points per game.

Georgia Southern Eagles 28, Georgia State Panthers 25. Georgia State Panthers cover the 5.5. Under 56.5.

display.fanatic_story:
Georgia's farm brand has its name on a football game again, because Georgia Southern Eagles vs Georgia State Panthers in Week 11 is the third-annual Georgia Grown Bowl. Georgia Southern insider Royce Ogeechee drove up from Statesboro with a cooler of boiled peanuts, and Georgia State insider Malik Overstreet met him at a MARTA station with a map of every shortcut to Center Parc Stadium.

Malik: Welcome to downtown Atlanta, Royce. This is the 13th meeting. Six wins for you, six wins for us. Georgia State Athletics says so. And today it's Heroes Day too, so be on your best behavior.

Royce: Malik, I'm always on my best behavior. I just eat boiled peanuts loudly. That's a Georgia Grown tradition.

The series is dead even, and it has been a seesaw for a decade. Over the last ten meetings, each side won five. Georgia State won 41-33 in 2022, then Georgia Southern answered with 44-27, 38-21 and 41-24 wins. Royce has those three framed above his granddad's tractor.

Royce: Three in a row. Granddad says it's like the old days at Paulson, when the Eagles ran the option and everybody else ran for the exits.

Malik: Your granddad also says the interstate used to be a dirt road. Things change, Royce.

Georgia Southern brings a hot hand. The Eagles have won three straight and lead the Sun Belt East at 4-1 in conference play. Last Saturday, Max Johnson went 19 of 26 for 271 yards and four touchdowns in a 49-13 rout of Marshall, and Jeremiah Ware caught five balls for 94 yards and two scores. Johnson has thrown for 2,195 yards with 15 touchdowns and only two interceptions all season.

Royce: Two interceptions. That boy protects the football like it's the last jar of peach preserves at the church supper.

Malik: Protecting it from Xavier Esqillion is different. Nine sacks, Royce. He finds quarterbacks the way I find parking on game day: fast and with attitude.

Georgia State's offense has a split personality at quarterback, and it is working. Cameran Brown leads the team with 1,356 throwing yards and 14 touchdowns, including a six-touchdown day against Old Dominion. Ayden Pereira has handled most of the throwing the last three games, and he threw three touchdowns in a 39-23 win at App State last Saturday. Lanear McCrary Jr. carried 21 times for 123 yards in that game and leads the Panthers with 526 rushing yards.

Malik: Two quarterbacks, one offense. It's like having the Red and Gold trains both running on time. Wait. Scratch that. Nobody in Atlanta would buy that.

Royce: I was with you till the trains.

The Panthers have one more weapon that keeps Royce awake. Rodshaun Dorsey has 29 catches for 476 yards and nine touchdowns. When Georgia State gets close, Dorsey is usually the guy waving his arms in the end zone.

Royce: Nine touchdowns on 29 catches. That's a lot of fruit off one tree.

Malik: And he's still blooming.

Georgia Southern's defense has been the quiet engine of its run. The Eagles allow 19.7 points a game, and they held App State to three points in a 19-3 win two weeks ago. Anthony Bynum has five sacks, and Brandon Tyson leads the team with 49 tackles. Georgia State gives up 26.2 points a game, but it scores 34.4, and it is 3-1 at home this fall.

Malik: Three and one in the city. The only home loss was Coastal. We don't talk about Coastal.

Royce: We beat Coastal on the road. Just saying.

Here is the matchup in one breath: Johnson's patience against Esqillion's speed, and Georgia Southern's defense against Dorsey near the goal. Whoever wins those fights probably carries the Georgia Grown trophy out of the stadium.

Royce: If we win, I'm handing out boiled peanuts to every Panthers fan on the train home.

Malik: If we win, I'm giving you a MARTA card loaded for one trip. Back to Statesboro.

Royce: That's the nicest thing a city boy ever did for me.

Malik: Don't get used to it.

Royce drives the Georgia Grown Bowl back to Statesboro with an empty cooler. My call: Georgia Southern Eagles 28, Georgia State Panthers 25.

display.story_text:
Western Kentucky's Homecoming theme is Big Red's World Tour, and the first stop on Saturday is a Conference USA leader that keeps winning close games. In Week 11 at Houchens-Smith Stadium in Bowling Green, my Jacksonville State vs Western Kentucky pick is Western Kentucky Hilltoppers +7.5, plus the Under 53.5.

Burl Ashcraft-Neeley cooks brisket in Calhoun County and says Jacksonville State football is the same job. "Low and slow, Thurman. We're 5-0 in conference. Caden Creel threw for 246 yards and ran for 87 against Sam Houston. We won 47-14."

Thurman "Tops" Whitsitt cuts hair in Warren County and has heard every brag in the chair. "Your boys beat Kennesaw State 27-26 and FIU 27-24. You beat Georgia Southern 31-27. That's not low and slow. That's sweating it out."

Thurman is onto something. Jacksonville State is 7-2 and 1st in Conference USA, but three of its seven wins came by four points or fewer. The Gamecocks score 29.1 points a game and allow 19.2. Creel is the whole operation, with 1,987 throwing yards, 15 touchdowns and 800 rushing yards. He also has eight interceptions, and he threw two in each of the wins over Middle Tennessee and New Mexico State.

Western Kentucky is 3-6 and gives up 33.3 points a game, so I'm not pretending the Hilltoppers are good. But they score 23.6, and they put up 42 at Middle Tennessee last week in a 42-51 loss. Ajay Allen ran 15 times for 116 yards in that game, and Jonathan Stafford Jr. caught eight balls for 90 yards. Allen has 535 rushing yards and six touchdowns on the season.

This series has teeth. Jacksonville State won 37-34 last year, and the 2023 meeting ended 20-17. The one rout, 52-12, came in a title game. Homecoming in Bowling Green is not the spot for a blowout.

My final is Jacksonville State Gamecocks 30, Western Kentucky Hilltoppers 23. That's a seven-point game, short of 7.5, so I want the Hilltoppers with the hook.

On the over/under, I'm on the Under 53.5. DraftKings opened it at 52.5 and it has moved up a point. The Gamecocks hold opponents under 20 a game, and Creel's offense chews clock with his legs. My 30-23 lands at 53, half a point under.

The room is split. The Formula has Western Kentucky +7.5 and the Under at 29-23. Next Man Up has Western Kentucky +7.5 but sits on the Over, 31-24. Letdown Watch goes the other way, with Jacksonville State −7.5 and the Under at 30-21. In The Trenches has no side and no over/under call here. Follow The Money is still waiting on a consensus spread, so its side is pending, and it has no total pick.

Letdown Watch: "Seven-two team, three-six team. I don't need a haircut to see this one."

Big Red's World Tour is the Homecoming theme on the Hill this year, and the tour's first big stop is Jacksonville State Gamecocks vs Western Kentucky Hilltoppers in Week 11 at Houchens-Smith Stadium in Bowling Green. Jacksonville State insider Burl Ashcraft-Neeley brought a smoker and a Conference USA lead, and Western Kentucky insider Thurman "Tops" Whitsitt brought his barber clippers and a Homecoming crowd dressed in red.

Burl: Thurman, I've had brisket on since four in the morning. Low and slow. That's how we do football in Calhoun County too.

Thurman: Burl, I've had a chair open since six. Low and slow is how you'll leave Bowling Green. Sit down. You need a trim before the parade.

Jacksonville State is 7-2 and 5-0 in Conference USA play, alone in first place. The Gamecocks opened with a 33-7 loss at North Dakota State and a 29-27 overtime loss at Ohio, and they haven't lost since. Last Saturday they ran past Sam Houston 47-14. Caden Creel completed 18 of 28 throws for 246 yards and two touchdowns, then ran 13 times for 87 yards and another score.

Burl: Creel is the whole pit, Thurman. He's the fire, the wood and the guy holding the tongs.

Thurman: He's also thrown eight interceptions, Burl. That fire sparks a little.

Burl: Watch it, now.

Thurman isn't wrong about the sparks. Creel has 1,987 throwing yards with 15 touchdowns and eight interceptions, plus 800 rushing yards and six touchdowns on the ground. Deondre Johnson is his top deep target, with 520 yards on just 26 catches. And the Gamecocks have lived dangerously in tight games, winning 27-26 at Kennesaw State, 27-24 over FIU and 31-27 over Georgia Southern.

Put plainly, Creel throws the ball well, runs it better than most backs, and gives a few away. Johnson stretches the field. And Jacksonville State has won those close games by one, three and four points.

Burl: Close is close. We win them.

Western Kentucky is 3-6 and 2-3 in Conference USA, and Thurman will tell you the first month was brutal. The Hilltoppers opened at Nevada, at Georgia and at Indiana, and lost all three. But they've shown life. They beat Missouri State 34-13 and won 16-3 at Sam Houston. Last week they lost a wild one at Middle Tennessee, 51-42, and the offense finally hummed.

Thurman: Forty-two points at Murfreesboro, Burl. Ajay Allen ran for 116 yards. Jonathan Stafford Jr. caught eight balls for 90. Brock Glenn didn't throw an interception. I had that game on the shop radio, and three customers walked out with half a haircut.

Burl: That's on you, not on football.

Allen leads the Hilltoppers with 535 rushing yards and six touchdowns. Stafford has 54 catches. Jaylen Lewis has 66 tackles on a defense that has been asked to make a lot of them. Western Kentucky gives up 33.3 points a game, while Jacksonville State allows 19.2.

Burl: That's the difference, Thurman. Our defense shows up. Caleb Nix has 56 tackles from safety.

Thurman: And our offense just put up 42. Somebody has to give.

These two have made a habit of drama. Jacksonville State won 20-17 in 2023, Western Kentucky won 19-17 in late 2024, and the Gamecocks took the league title game a week later, 52-12. Last year Jacksonville State won again, 37-34. Burl says the Gamecocks own the series 3-1 in the recent meetings. Thurman says the 19-17 game is the only one he remembers.

Thurman: Selective memory, Burl. It's a barber's gift. I forget the bad haircuts too.

Burl: I've seen your haircuts. You forget a lot of them.

So here's the Homecoming question in Bowling Green. Can the Hilltoppers run Allen enough to keep Creel on the sideline, or does Creel keep doing Creel things until the Gamecocks pull away late?

Thurman: If we win, I'm giving free haircuts Monday. Gamecocks fans get the bowl cut.

Burl: If we win, I'm bringing brisket to your shop. You'll have to sweep up the burnt ends.

Thurman: Deal. Bring sauce.

Burl brings the brisket. Thurman brings the sauce. The Gamecocks bring home the win. My call: Jacksonville State Gamecocks 30, Western Kentucky Hilltoppers 23.

Middle Tennessee Blue Raiders vs Liberty Flames turns Williams Stadium into Military Appreciation Day, with commemorative military coins for early arrivals before a Conference USA game Lynchburg expects to control. Gideon Fairweather got to Williams Stadium in time for a coin and has not stopped talking about Deshawn Purdie since. Opal Stonebriar answers for Middle Tennessee with Roman Gagliano's touchdown total and a warning that 51 points last week was not a mirage.

Gideon: Purdie has one interception all year. Davis has eight rushing scores. Military Appreciation is our kind of Saturday.

Opal: Gagliano has 16 touchdowns. Martin has 711 yards. Your Saturday still has to stop that.

Liberty is 8-1 after a 30-14 win at New Mexico State. Middle Tennessee just beat Western Kentucky 51-42. The Flames score 33.3 points a game and allow 13.6. The Blue Raiders score 26.9 and allow 31.0. That is the cleanest mismatch on this Conference USA board, and Williams Stadium knows it.

Deshawn Purdie has 1,705 passing yards with 11 touchdowns and one interception. Kam Davis has 666 rushing yards. Makai Jackson has 702 receiving yards and six scores. Brenton Williams has 5 sacks. Derrell Farrar has 53 tackles. When Liberty's front wins early downs, the afternoon starts looking like every other Flames home game that got quiet for the visitor by the third quarter.

Middle Tennessee's counter is volume. Roman Gagliano has 1,899 yards. Cam'ron Lacy has 579 receiving yards. Antonio Martin has four rushing scores. Korey Smith has 80 tackles. Zeion Simpson-Smith has 2 sacks. The Blue Raiders can put up points. They have not yet shown they can keep the other team from putting up more, and that is the problem you bring to Lynchburg on Military Appreciation Day.

Opal: Coins are nice. A stop near the goal is nicer.

Gideon: Coins are nice. Purdie on third down is nicer.

Lynchburg will treat the afternoon like a ceremony that happens to include football. Middle Tennessee will treat it like a chance to prove the Western Kentucky shootout was a beginning, not a one-off. One of those moods usually wins in November, and Williams Stadium will decide which one before the coins get tucked into pockets for the ride home.

Gideon will talk Purdie. Opal will talk Gagliano. Military Appreciation will talk about whether the home team finished the job.

Military Appreciation Day in Lynchburg puts the ceremony first and the mismatch second. The coins matter. The 13.6 points allowed matter more. Middle Tennessee can score with anybody in this league on the right Saturday. Liberty can take that scoring away on almost any Saturday. Williams Stadium is about to ask which identity survives contact.

Gideon keeps talking about Purdie's interception total. Opal keeps talking about Gagliano's touchdowns. The coins will outlast whichever argument loses.

Lynchburg's Military Appreciation crowd will fill Williams Stadium with coins, ceremonies, and an expectation that 8-1 looks like 8-1. Middle Tennessee's 51-point afternoon against Western Kentucky proved the Blue Raiders can trade scores. Liberty's season-long 13.6 points allowed proved the Flames can take those trades off the table. The collision is simple. The execution will not be.

Purdie protects the ball. Gagliano pushes it downfield. Only one of those styles travels well into a Military Appreciation defense.

The coins will outlast the noise. The scoreboard will decide who deserved it.

Lynchburg came for coins and a win. Middle Tennessee came to spoil both.

The ceremony will be sharp. The football has to match it.

Bring the coins. Bring the noise. Finish the job in front of the home crowd.

Bring the coins home in your pockets. The Flames keep the noise going all afternoon. My call: Liberty Flames 37, Middle Tennessee Blue Raiders 14.

Four common Pac-12 opponents tell you almost everything about Saturday in San Marcos, and they say these teams are closer than 9.5 points. My Fresno State vs Texas State pick is Fresno State Bulldogs +9.5, and I'm taking the Under 60.5 too in this Week 11 game at UFCU Stadium, where Texas State is marking Heroes Day and Community Day.

Here's the comparison. Both teams lost to Boise State, Texas State 45-46 on the road and Fresno State 31-38 at home. Both lost at San Diego State, Texas State 29-31 and Fresno State 23-26. Both beat Oregon State, Texas State 42-21 and Fresno State 38-22. The only real split is Utah State, which Texas State beat 20-17 and Fresno State lost to 10-17 last week. That's not a ten-point gap.

Yesenia Calderwood floats the San Marcos River most weekends and isn't worried. "Go with the flow, Roz. Torrance Burgess Jr. ran 28 times for 196 yards at Oregon State. He's got 1,118 on the year. Brad Jackson has 19 touchdown throws. We score 38.6 a game."

Roz Ayala sells the Fresno Valley like a fruit stand owner and pushes back. "And you give up 30.8, Yesenia. We give up 20.6. Jayden Mandal has thrown two interceptions all year. Josiah Freeman caught eight balls for 114 yards at Utah State. Dylan Hampsten has six sacks."

Roz has the stronger defensive argument. Texas State allows 30.8 points a game, Fresno State allows 20.6, and K'vion Thunderbird has 69 tackles in the middle of that Bulldogs group. Fresno State's offense has gone quiet at times, with 10 points at Utah State, but Mandal's 1,857 yards and 11 touchdowns against two interceptions mean the Bulldogs rarely hand games away.

My final is Texas State Bobcats 31, Fresno State Bulldogs 26. The Bobcats win at home, but a five-point game sits well inside 9.5.

On the over/under, I'm on the Under 60.5. DraftKings opened it at 58.5 and it has moved up two points. Texas State's offense is a real threat, but Fresno State hasn't allowed more than 39 in any game. My 31-26 lands at 57, clear of the 60.5.

The room mostly agrees. The Formula likes Fresno State +9.5 and likes the Under at 29-27. Letdown Watch likes Fresno State +9.5 and likes the Under at 30-26. Next Man Up has Fresno State +9.5 but sits on the Over, 35-26. In The Trenches has no side and no over/under call here. Follow The Money is still waiting on a consensus spread, so its side is pending, and it has no total pick.

Letdown Watch: "The Formula and I agree again. Somebody frame it."

Next Man Up: "Thirty-five points from Texas State. Y'all forgot that offense dropped 66 on Colorado State."

The Formula: "Nobody forgot. It also allowed 46 to Boise State."

Yesenia wants the river rolling into a big November. Roz wants the long trip from the Valley to end with a road win. I think Texas State wins a shootout that never quite becomes one.

Heroes Day and Community Day bring a full house to the riverbank in San Marcos, and the guests come all the way from the Valley: Fresno State Bulldogs vs Texas State Bobcats in Week 11 at UFCU Stadium. Texas State insider Yesenia Calderwood came straight from an inner tube at Sewell Park, and Fresno State insider Roz Ayala flew in with a box of Valley fruit and a red Bulldog hoodie.

Roz: Yesenia, I brought you a gift. Fresno grows the food, so I thought I'd feed the hosts before we beat them.

Yesenia: Thanks, Roz. Feeding us won't slow us down. I'll eat it on the river after the game. Go with the flow.

Roz: Your whole personality is a pun about water.

Yesenia: And yours is a fruit basket. We're even.

These two programs are both new to the rebuilt Pac-12, and Texas State already sits second. The Bobcats are 5-4 overall and 3-2 in Pac-12 play. Fresno State is also 5-4, but 2-3 in the league, and both teams are trying to turn a decent season into a strong one.

Texas State's offense is the loudest thing in central Texas outside of Sixth Street. The Bobcats score 38.6 points a game. Torrance Burgess Jr. has 1,118 rushing yards, and last Saturday at Oregon State he carried 28 times for 196 yards in a 42-21 win. Brad Jackson has thrown for 2,147 yards with 19 touchdowns and six interceptions, and he completed 16 of 20 throws against the Beavers.

Yesenia: Torrance runs like the river after a storm, Roz. You don't stop him. You get out of the way and wave.

Roz: Our defense doesn't wave, Yesenia. It tackles.

Fresno State's defense is the reason this game is interesting. The Bulldogs allow 20.6 points a game, while Texas State gives up 30.8. Dylan Hampsten has six sacks, and K'vion Thunderbird leads the team with 69 tackles. And Jayden Mandal, the quarterback, protects the ball like a farmer protects a crop before the frost: 1,857 throwing yards, 11 touchdowns and just two interceptions.

Roz: Two interceptions in nine games. That's a fruit stand with no bruised peaches.

Yesenia: Your stand sold out of points at Utah State, though.

Roz: We had a quiet day. Even orchards have a quiet season.

San Diego State beat Texas State 31-29 and beat Fresno State 26-23. Both teams beat Oregon State. The only split is Utah State, which lost to Texas State 20-17 and beat Fresno State.

Yesenia: So we beat the team that beat you. That's the river flowing my way.

Roz: Or it means we're about the same, and Saturday decides it.

Yesenia: When we get rolling, Roz, we're rolling. That Colorado State game felt like the whole river came over the bank.

Yesenia: If we win, you have to float the river with me. In a maroon tube.

Roz: I'll float. I won't like it.

Yesenia: You'll love it. Everybody does.

display.fanatic_story:
Ole Miss Rebels vs Oklahoma Sooners is American Heritage Saturday in Norman, a late-afternoon kickoff at Gaylord Family Oklahoma Memorial Stadium for two SEC teams carrying very different memories from last week. Langston Fairbanks shows up talking about Trinidad Chambliss like the Georgia loss was a closed book. Savannah Redbird-Lowe arrives with John Mateer's Florida tape and a reminder that Norman still expects the home team to finish.

Langston: Chambliss has 18 touchdowns. Alexander can win the route. We did not come to Norman to be quiet.

Savannah: Mateer just won at Florida. Avant runs between the tackles. Your quiet still has to deal with that.

Ole Miss is coming off a 7-42 loss to Georgia that emptied the air out of an otherwise productive offense. Oklahoma is coming off a 23-7 win at Florida that looked like the version of this team the preseason promised. The Rebels still score 33.8 points a game and allow 26.0. The Sooners score 22.1 and allow 19.2. That is a collision between a visitor that can put up points and a home team that has spent November trying to remember how.

Trinidad Chambliss has 2,359 passing yards with 18 touchdowns and nine interceptions. Deuce Alexander has 669 receiving yards. Kewan Lacy has 388 rushing yards and five scores. Blake Purchase has 4.5 sacks. Keaton Thomas has 55 tackles. When Chambliss is clean, Ole Miss looks like the team that hung crooked numbers earlier this fall. When he is not, Georgia tape starts replaying itself.

Oklahoma's answer is Mateer and a defense that just held Florida to seven. Mateer has 2,042 yards with 15 touchdowns. Isaiah Sategna III has 625 receiving yards. Lloyd Avant has 394 rushing yards. Adepoju Adebawore has 4 sacks. Owen Heinecke has 73 tackles. The Sooners do not need a track meet. They need to keep Chambliss uncomfortable and let Mateer win a one-possession game in front of the home crowd.

Savannah: American Heritage is nice. A third-down sack is nicer.

Langston: Themes are nice. Chambliss on schedule is nicer.

Norman will treat the afternoon like a statement chance after Florida. Ole Miss will treat it like a reset after Georgia. One of those moods usually wins in November, and Memorial Stadium will decide which one before the lights take over the evening.

Langston will talk Chambliss. Savannah will talk Mateer. American Heritage will talk about whether the home team finished the job.

American Heritage Saturday is not Military Appreciation — that theme lands next week against Texas A&M — but it still puts Norman in a reflective mood before a game that feels like a measuring stick. Ole Miss wants to prove Georgia was an outlier. Oklahoma wants to prove Florida was a beginning. Those two proofs cannot both be true by the end of the night.

Langston keeps talking about Chambliss. Savannah keeps talking about Mateer. Memorial Stadium will decide which November story gets to keep going.

Norman in mid-November is loud even when the theme is reflective. American Heritage Saturday puts history on the pregame board and then asks two quarterbacks to write a new chapter anyway. Chambliss has the volume numbers. Mateer has the fresher win. Ole Miss has the higher scoring pace. Oklahoma has the home crowd and the harder defense. That is enough material for a one-possession game that will not feel decided until somebody blinks on fourth down.

The Georgia hangover is real. The Florida bounce is real. Memorial Stadium gets to choose which one was louder.

One possession. Two quarterbacks. A Norman evening that will not feel settled early.

Norman never settles down, and the Rebels fly home anyway. My call: Ole Miss Rebels 25, Oklahoma Sooners 22.

Michigan State walked out of Ann Arbor with a 15-6 win last Saturday, and a team that was 2-6 suddenly has a reason to fill Spartan Stadium for Military Appreciation Day. My Washington vs Michigan State pick is Michigan State Spartans +4 with the Over 43.5 for Week 11 in East Lansing.

Shay Kowalczyk caught softball for 11 years around Lansing and calls this game like a pitch sequence. "Alessio Milivojevic went 21 of 32 for 188 yards and didn't throw a pick in the Big House. Brandon Tullis carried 25 times. That's how you work a count, Vangie."

Vangie Tollefsrud rowed crew at Washington and brings coffee and rain gear everywhere. "We lost to Penn State 25-28, Shay. Three points. Demond Williams Jr. threw two touchdowns, and Chris Lawson has 727 receiving yards. We've beaten you 39-28 and 41-7 the last two times we met."

Both are right, and that's why four points is a lot here. Washington is 5-4 and 2-4 in Big Ten play, and its losses have been close: 24-27 to Minnesota, 21-25 at USC and 25-28 to Penn State. The Huskies score 26.3 and allow 21.9. Michigan State is 3-6, but it lost 37-38 in overtime to Illinois and 21-24 to Northwestern before the Michigan win. These teams live in one-score games.

The Huskies also have a road problem. They are 2-1 away from home, but those wins came 38-26 at Purdue and 17-10 at Nebraska, not exactly a blowout run. A cross-country trip for a late-afternoon kick in November is a fair test.

My final is Washington Huskies 24, Michigan State Spartans 22. Washington wins by two, and the Spartans stay inside the 4.

On the over/under, I'm on the Over 43.5. DraftKings opened it at 45.5 and it has dropped two points, mostly because Michigan State held Michigan to six. But the Spartans scored 37 against Illinois and 35 against Eastern Michigan, and Washington has topped 20 in seven of nine games. My 24-22 lands at 46, above 43.5.

The room is all over the map. The Formula has Michigan State +4 and likes the Over at 24-23. Next Man Up likes Michigan State +4 and has the Over at 23-21. Letdown Watch goes with Washington −4 and the Over at 26-20. In The Trenches likes Washington −4 and makes no over/under call. That's two cards on each side, so the tiebreaker is the one-score history above. Follow The Money is still waiting on a consensus spread, so its side is pending, and it has no total pick.

Next Man Up: "Two of us on the Spartans, two on the Huskies. Somebody in this room is wrong, In The Trenches."

In The Trenches: "Not me. I like the Huskies' front."

Shay wants a two-game winning run and a Dairy Store cone after. Vangie wants her Huskies to row through the November cold. I think Washington wins it and Michigan State makes them earn every yard.

Washington Huskies 24, Michigan State Spartans 22. Michigan State Spartans cover the 4. Over 43.5.

display.fanatic_story:
Military Appreciation Day at Spartan Stadium arrives with a little extra noise, because Washington Huskies vs Michigan State Spartans in Week 11 comes one week after the Spartans won 15-6 in Ann Arbor. Michigan State insider Shay Kowalczyk is still hoarse from that one, and Washington insider Vangie Tollefsrud flew in from Seattle with a rain shell, a thermos of coffee and a quiet worry about November in East Lansing.

Shay: Gear on, mask down. Vangie, welcome to the stadium where we just kicked off a winning run. A run of one, but a run.

Vangie: Shay, one win is a run? On Lake Washington, one stroke is not a race.

Shay: In softball, one hit is a rally if you want it bad enough.

Michigan State is 3-6 and 1-5 in Big Ten play, and for most of October the Spartans kept leaving empty. They lost 38-37 in overtime to Illinois, then 24-21 to Northwestern, then 28-10 at UCLA. Then came Michigan. Alessio Milivojevic completed 21 of 32 throws for 188 yards, didn't throw an interception, and the defense held the Wolverines to two field goals.

Shay: Six points, Vangie. We gave up six points in the Big House. That's a catcher blocking every pitch in the dirt for four quarters.

Vangie: I'll give you that. That was a gutsy one. Our team plays a lot of gutsy ones too.

Washington is 5-4 and 2-4 in the league, and Vangie will tell you that the Huskies are three plays from a great season. They lost 27-24 to Minnesota, 25-21 at USC and, last Saturday, 28-25 to Penn State at Husky Stadium. Demond Williams Jr. threw two touchdowns against the Nittany Lions, and Chris Lawson caught five balls for 89 yards.

Vangie: Three losses by a combined ten points, Shay. That's a boat that keeps finishing a seat behind.

Shay: You mean it hurts.

Vangie: It hurts.

The Huskies have their weapons. Lawson leads them with 727 receiving yards on 49 catches. Williams has thrown for 1,667 yards with 11 touchdowns and four interceptions, and when Elijah Brown took the snaps in October, he threw three touchdowns at Purdue. Alex McLaughlin, a safety, leads the defense with 63 tackles. Washington allows 21.9 points a game.

Michigan State's defense is more surprising. The Spartans allow 23.6 points a game, and they were at their best in Ann Arbor. Devin Vaught has 53 tackles from safety, and Anelu Lafaele leads the team with three and a half sacks. On offense, Chrishon McCray caught six balls for 92 yards at Michigan, and Jaziun Patterson leads the team with 327 rushing yards and five touchdowns.

Shay: Patterson's our cleanup hitter. Tullis carried it 25 times last week, too. We'll run it right at you, Vangie, in the cold.

Vangie: I row in the rain at six in the morning, Shay. Cold is just a mood.

Shay: It's going to be a very big mood around here.

The history between these two is short and one-sided. Washington won 39-28 in Seattle in 2022 and 41-7 in East Lansing in 2023. Vangie has both box scores saved on her phone. Shay says neither one counts, because both happened before the Spartans' new run of one.

Vangie: That's not how history works.

Shay: That's how catchers work. Short memory. Next pitch.

This one comes down to a simple question. Can Michigan State's defense keep playing like it did in Ann Arbor, or does Washington's passing game, with Lawson running free, finally close out one of these tight finishes?

Shay: If we win, Vangie, you're buying me a cone at the Dairy Store. Two scoops.

Vangie: If we win, you're drinking a Seattle coffee, black, and you're not allowed to make a face.

Shay: I'll make a face. I always make a face.

Vangie: Then I'll take a picture of it.

Shay makes the face. Washington makes the play. My call: Washington Huskies 24, Michigan State Spartans 22.

Ruston is turning red on Saturday, with Louisiana Tech calling it a Red Out and a chance to clinch the Sun Belt West against an old regional rival. My Southern Miss vs Louisiana Tech pick at Joe Aillet Stadium in Week 11 is Southern Miss Golden Eagles +17.5, and I'm on the Under 55.5 as well.

Booker "Champ" Tullos grew up on a peach farm and played fullback for Tech, so he likes football that moves one hard yard at a time. "Blake Baker has 14 touchdown throws and one interception. One. He went 16 of 19 at Troy in a 41-17 win. We're 5-0 in the league, Dee."

Dee Broussard scouts the Golden Eagles from the Hattiesburg stands and smiles while she pushes back. "Brag all you want, Champ. We beat Louisiana 35-31. Y'all beat them 32-31. And Steven Robinson has 782 rushing yards and ten touchdowns."

Dee's point matters. Louisiana Tech is 7-2 and the better team, but its league wins over Army and Louisiana came by two points and one point. The Bulldogs score 33.6 points a game and allow 20.4, and Alonzo Jackson Jr. has nine sacks and 68 tackles. That defense also has two shutouts, 24-0 at UL Monroe and 26-0 over Old Dominion.

Southern Miss is 3-6, and the 23-54 loss to James Madison was ugly. The Golden Eagles allow 33.6 points a game. But they have a real runner in Robinson, a real target in Mario Sanders, who has 698 receiving yards, and a tackling machine in Mathis Haygood, with 83 stops. They lost 21-24 at Tulane, and they won 35-21 at UL Monroe.

The series has been tight for a decade. Southern Miss won four of the seven meetings in that stretch, including 21-20 in 2018, and Louisiana Tech won 31-30 in 2020 before last year's 30-20. Dee will tell you three of those games were decided by seven points or fewer.

My final is Louisiana Tech Bulldogs 35, Southern Miss Golden Eagles 20. Tech wins comfortably, and fifteen points stays short of 17.5.

On the over/under, I'm on the Under 55.5. DraftKings opened it at 54.5 and it has moved up a point. Louisiana Tech has held four of its last five opponents under 21, and Baker doesn't give the ball away. My 35-20 lands at 55, half a point under.

The room is split down the middle. The Formula likes Southern Miss +17.5 and has the Under at 35-20. In The Trenches likes Southern Miss +17.5 at 29-22 and makes no over/under call. Letdown Watch has Southern Miss +17.5 and the Under at 36-19. Next Man Up likes Louisiana Tech −17.5 and likes the Over at 39-19. Follow The Money is still waiting on a consensus spread, so its side is pending, and it has no total pick.

Next Man Up: "Thirty-nine points. Baker throws one interception a season. Y'all are scared of a shadow."

In The Trenches: "Twenty-nine to twenty-two. I'm scared of nothing. I'm just realistic."

display.fanatic_story:
Experience Ruston is handing out 2,000 Red Out shirts at the gates, and the whole town will be wearing them for Southern Miss Golden Eagles vs Louisiana Tech Bulldogs in Week 11 at Joe Aillet Stadium, with a Sun Belt West title in reach for the home side. Louisiana Tech insider Booker "Champ" Tullos drove in from the peach orchard at dawn, and Southern Miss insider Dee Broussard rolled up from Hattiesburg in a gold scarf with a grin that means trouble.

Champ: Dee, welcome to Ruston. We've got a Makers Market on the Thomas Assembly Center steps, a frisbee dog show at halftime and a red shirt with your name on it.

Dee: Champ, I wouldn't be caught dead in red. But I'll buy a candle at the market and smile at every dog.

Champ: Mighty neighborly of you.

Dee: Don't start.

He started. Louisiana Tech is 7-2 and 5-0 in Sun Belt play, first in the West, and the Bulldogs have won six straight since their September trips to LSU and Baylor. Last Saturday they rolled at Troy, 41-17. Blake Baker completed 16 of 19 throws, and Marcus Calwise Jr. caught nine balls for 137 yards and a touchdown.

Champ: Baker's got one interception all year, Dee. One. My granddaddy's tractor has more mistakes in it than that boy.

Dee: Good for the tractor. Is it playing on Saturday too?

The Bulldogs' defense might be even better than Baker. Tech allows 20.4 points a game, and it has two shutouts, 24-0 at UL Monroe and 26-0 over Old Dominion. Alonzo Jackson Jr. leads the team with nine sacks and 68 tackles. That's a linebacker doing two jobs and making both look easy.

Champ: Alonzo plays like a fullback on defense. Head down, full speed, somebody's getting knocked into next week.

Southern Miss is 3-6 and 2-3 in the league, and the Golden Eagles are coming off a rough Thursday night. James Madison beat them 54-23 in Hattiesburg. John White threw for 266 yards in that game, and Kaden Saunders caught six balls for 122 yards. But Dee has better memories from October, and she wants everyone to remember them.

Dee: We beat Louisiana 35-31, Champ. Y'all beat them 32-31. And we won by 14 at UL Monroe. So who's the better team against Louisiana teams?

Champ: Well, that's a trick question.

Dee: It's not a trick. It's a scouting report.

Dee's scouting report has some real names in it. Steven Robinson has 782 rushing yards and ten touchdowns. Mario Sanders has 50 catches for 698 yards and six scores. Mathis Haygood, a linebacker, has 83 tackles, and Jameer Lewis has four sacks. Southern Miss allows 33.6 points a game, though, and Tech will test that every snap.

Champ: Our offense is like a peach orchard in July, Dee. It just keeps giving.

Dee: Then it'll go soft by August. To the top, y'all.

These programs have known each other a long time. Louisiana Tech's athletics office says the first meeting was a 27-0 Bulldog win in Ruston in 1935, and the two schools played every season from 2013 through 2021. Tech has won three of the last four, including a 30-20 win at Joe Aillet last fall. But Southern Miss won 21-20 in 2018 and 35-19 in 2021, and Tech won a 31-30 thriller in 2020.

Dee: Look at those scores, Champ. One point, one point, and then we roll you. We've been here before.

Champ: And we've been home before. This is home.

The red shirts, the rally towels and the frisbee dogs are all nice. But the real question is whether Southern Miss can run Robinson enough to keep Baker off the field, or whether Tech's defense turns this into another long afternoon for an opponent.

Champ: If we win, Dee, I'm bringing you a peach cobbler and doing my fullback dive on the 50.

Dee: If we win, you're wearing gold in Ruston and singing our fight song on the steps of the Assembly Center.

Champ: I'd sooner eat that frisbee at halftime.

Dee: Then bring a fork, Champ.

Ruston wears red head to toe, and the West moves a step closer for the Bulldogs. My call: Louisiana Tech Bulldogs 35, Southern Miss Golden Eagles 20.

No Kansas game this season has climbed past 66.5 combined points, and that's exactly where the over/under sits for Saturday in Morgantown. My Kansas vs West Virginia pick is Kansas Jayhawks +3 with the Under 66.5 for Week 11 at Milan Puskar Stadium, where West Virginia closes Mountaineer Week with its Heroes Day game.

Jolene Buckhannon captained the rifle team at West Virginia and talks in short bursts. "Cam Cook. 1,072 yards. Michael Hawkins Jr. Twelve touchdowns, two interceptions. TaRon Francis caught three balls for 169 at Texas Tech. We score 37.2 a game. Load up."

Fitz Calloway grew up a Kansas basketball person and keeps a spreadsheet out of spite. "You also give up 34.6, Jolene. You lost 48-53 in Lubbock. Isaiah Marshall ran for 125 yards and two touchdowns against UCF. Leroy Harris III has six and a half sacks. And we beat you 41-10 last year."

That's where the Under case begins. Kansas games have stayed below this number all year, because the Jayhawks allow 24.8 a game and Marshall's offense doesn't sprint. West Virginia games are wilder, with the 48-53 loss at Texas Tech and a 45-42 win over Cincinnati, but the Mountaineers also played 24-20 at TCU. DraftKings opened at 64.5 and moved up two points to 66.5. My 29-28 lands at 57, well under.

The side is tighter. Kansas is 3-6, but the Jayhawks lost 32-33 to UCF, 16-22 at TCU and 17-24 to Arizona State. They're a few plays from a winning record. West Virginia is 5-4, and its last four Big 12 results were a 31-52 loss to Arizona, a 45-42 win over Cincinnati, a 24-20 win at TCU and the 48-53 loss at Texas Tech. Home field matters, but not by much more than a field goal.

The series has belonged to West Virginia across the last decade, 7-2 in that stretch, though Kansas won two of the last four, 55-42 and 41-10.

My final is West Virginia Mountaineers 29, Kansas Jayhawks 28. A one-point game stays inside the 3.

Jolene wants a Heroes Day win and Country Roads ringing through the stadium. Fitz wants a road win he can turn into a basketball score. I think the Mountaineers win it late, and the Jayhawks stay close. West Virginia is 2-4 in Big 12 play.

Mountaineer Week wraps up in Morgantown with Heroes Day at Milan Puskar Stadium, as West Virginia honors active and former military members during Kansas Jayhawks vs West Virginia Mountaineers in Week 11. West Virginia insider Jolene Buckhannon showed up in a gold beanie with a bag of pepperoni rolls, and Kansas insider Fitz Calloway arrived with a laptop full of spreadsheets and a basketball conversion for everything.

Jolene: Fitz. Welcome to Morgantown. Short version. We shoot, we score, we sing.

Fitz: Jolene, I appreciate a short version. In basketball terms, you're a team that runs and guns and forgets to box out.

Jolene: Box out what?

Fitz: Exactly my point.

West Virginia is 5-4 and 2-4 in Big 12 play, and its games are not for the faint of heart. The Mountaineers score 37.2 points a game and allow 34.6. Last Saturday they lost 53-48 at Texas Tech, even with Michael Hawkins Jr. throwing for 303 yards on only 16 attempts. TaRon Francis caught three balls for 169 yards and a touchdown. Three catches. One hundred sixty-nine yards.

Jolene: Three shots. Three bullseyes. That's TaRon.

Fitz: In basketball, that's three half-court shots in a row. Nobody does that. Honestly, I'm a little scared.

Cam Cook is the steady part of the West Virginia offense. He has 1,072 rushing yards and eight touchdowns, and he ran 23 times for 149 yards in Lubbock. Hawkins has 1,901 throwing yards with 12 touchdowns and just two interceptions, and DJ Epps has 564 receiving yards on only 23 catches.

Jolene: Cook doesn't miss. He just keeps firing.

Kansas comes in at 3-6 and 1-5 in the league, and Fitz will tell you the record lies a little. The Jayhawks lost 33-32 to UCF last Saturday, 22-16 at TCU and 24-17 to Arizona State. Isaiah Marshall ran 13 times for 125 yards and two touchdowns against UCF. He also has 1,716 throwing yards with 11 touchdowns and seven interceptions.

Fitz: We're a coin flip from 6-3, Jolene. Maybe two coin flips. I have it in a tab.

Jolene: Your tab can't tackle.

Fitz: My tab has feelings.

The Jayhawks' defense is better than its record. Kansas allows 24.8 points a game, about ten fewer than West Virginia. Leroy Harris III has six and a half sacks off the end, and Trey Lathan leads the team with 62 tackles. Dylan Edwards leads the offense on the ground with 595 rushing yards, and Nik McMillan has 497 receiving yards and five touchdowns.

Fitz: And don't forget last year, Jolene. Forty-one to ten. That's a 31-point win in a football game. In basketball, that's a 20-point win at halftime and the walk-ons get minutes.

Jolene: I remember. I'm still mad. Mad helps my aim.

The longer history belongs to the Mountaineers. Since 2016, West Virginia has won seven of nine against Kansas, including 48-21, 56-34 and 38-17 wins. But Kansas won 55-42 in 2022 and 41-10 last year, and Fitz treats those two like national titles.

Jolene: Two wins. Seven losses. Do the math, Fitz.

Fitz: I did the math. I made a chart. The chart is trending up, Jolene.

So here's the question as the last day of Mountaineer Week ends under the lights. Can Kansas' defense keep Cook in front of it and make Hawkins throw into traffic, or does West Virginia's offense pile up points the way it did against Cincinnati, when it won a 45-42 shootout?

Jolene: If we win, you sing Country Roads. Every verse. On the field.

Fitz: If we win, you wear a Kansas basketball jersey to the pepperoni roll stand.

Jolene: Deal. I don't miss.

Fitz: That's what scares me.

Mountaineer Week ends the only way Morgantown knows: one point, no sleep. My call: West Virginia Mountaineers 29, Kansas Jayhawks 28.

display.fanatic_story:
Oregon State Beavers vs Boise State Broncos is the Week 11 night the blue turf in Boise gets the whole stadium dressed to match it. Boise State has spent this entire season throwing a 40th birthday party for The Blue, and with Saturday billed as a Wear Blue game at Albertsons Stadium, Oregon State forestry PhD Juniper Ostrowski is walking into the brightest field in the West while Treasure Valley lifer Thatcher Bluestem swears the color was the first word he ever said.

Thatcher: Forty years, Juniper. Gene Bleymaier put a blue field down in 1986, everybody laughed, and now it's the most famous patch of ground in Idaho.

Juniper: I study forests for a living. I know what grows naturally and what doesn't. That field does not.

Thatcher: Neither does an 8-1 season, and we've got one of those too.

Thatcher has the better hand coming in, and he knows it. Boise State is 8-1, unbeaten in conference play at 5-0, and sitting first in the Pac-12. The only loss came in the opener at Oregon, 34-27. Since then the Broncos have handled Memphis, Utah State, Fresno State and Washington State, survived a 46-45 thriller with Texas State on Halloween, and then went to Fort Collins last Saturday and put up 64 on Colorado State.

Juniper: Sixty-four is rude.

Thatcher: Sixty-four is Dylan Riley.

That's mostly true. Riley ran for 192 yards and two scores in Fort Collins and has 1,241 yards with 11 touchdowns on the season. He's the engine of everything Boise wants to do, because every carry that falls forward sets up the deep shot off a run fake to Rasean Jones, who caught six balls for 116 yards against the Rams. Maddux Madsen has thrown for 1,681 yards with 15 touchdowns and just one interception, and Max Cutforth threw for 317 and four scores in Fort Collins. Whoever takes the snap, the Broncos have scored 39.0 points a game.

Juniper: You know what else scores? Braden Atkinson.

She's earned that one. Atkinson has 3,169 throwing yards, 25 touchdowns and only three interceptions, and in October he looked like the best quarterback in the league. He went 31 of 34 for 427 yards and five touchdowns at Colorado State, then threw five more against San Diego State in a 66-14 rout. Jesse Legree is the guy on the other end of most of it, with 61 catches for 1,209 yards and 14 touchdowns. If you're a Boise safety, Legree is the name on the whiteboard in red marker.

Thatcher: I'll give you October. November's been colder in Corvallis.

That's the part Juniper doesn't want to talk about. Oregon State dropped its last two, 38-22 at Fresno State and 42-21 at home to Texas State, and last Saturday Atkinson threw for 192 yards without a touchdown. The Beavers are 5-4 and still second in the conference, but the shine came off fast.

Juniper: Two bad weeks. In forestry we call that a dry spell, not a fire.

Thatcher: In Boise we call it a chance.

The trench fight decides how this goes. Oregon State linebacker Takari Hickle has seven sacks and Aiden Sullivan has 69 tackles, so the Beavers can get after a quarterback. If Hickle wins early downs and forces Boise to throw on third and long, Juniper's dry spell ends on the blue. If Riley keeps falling forward for five and six yards a pop, Hickle never gets to pin his ears back, and that's when the stadium turns into one big wall of blue noise.

Boise's defense has something to prove too. The Broncos gave up 45 to Texas State and 38 to Colorado State, and Lopez Sanusi, with 4.5 sacks, plus linebacker Boen Phelps, with 52 tackles, have to keep Legree in front of them. Oregon State has scored 38.0 points a game. Nobody's shutting this offense out.

The last time Oregon State came to Boise, in November of 2024, the Broncos won 34-18. Juniper remembers the cold. Thatcher remembers the noise.

Juniper: I'm wearing orange and black into a stadium full of blue. I'll be the one tree in the clearing.

Thatcher: You'll be easy to find, then. I'll wave.

Juniper: Wave all you want. Legree's going to make your secondary look like a stand of lodgepole after a windstorm.

Thatcher: He'll get his catches. Riley gets the fourth quarter, and on a blue field that's turning forty, the fourth quarter belongs to the home team.

So the plan for Saturday is simple. Thatcher wears blue on blue on blue. Juniper wears orange and tries not to blink. And the field that began as a joke four decades ago gets one more November night to prove it was never one.

The Blue turns forty, and Juniper finally blinks. My call: Boise State Broncos 36, Oregon State Beavers 25.

App State vs Marshall prediction: Huntington spends Saturday morning at the Memorial Fountain, and Saturday night it plays its annual remembrance game on the fifty-sixth anniversary of the Marshall plane crash. I'm on Marshall Thundering Herd +1.5 and Under 53.5, with Marshall Thundering Herd 27, App State Mountaineers 26 as my final.

The ceremony begins at 10 a.m. on the Memorial Student Center plaza, and kickoff at Joan C. Edwards Stadium is 6 p.m. ET. That day has a way of filling this building. Mercy Holderby, the Huntington nurse who grew up on the story of the program's rebirth, puts it simply. "We remember in the morning. We play at night. The Herd has won the last four times App has come here." Zeb Coldiron, down from Boone, doesn't argue the history. "Fine. But Malachi Singleton has 2,156 yards, and Jaquari Lewis has eight rushing touchdowns. The Mountaineers can play a little too."

The history is Mercy's best card. App State leads the series 17-11, but the Mountaineers have not won in Huntington since Marshall joined the top division, and the Herd won 52-37 in this stadium in 2024. The four meetings since 2022 split two and two.

DraftKings opened App State −2.5 with 53.5 points on the over/under, and the number has come down to App State −1.5. That move points the same way I do. App has lost three of its last four, scored three points twice in that stretch, and Singleton has four interceptions in his last two games. Marshall got crushed 49-13 at Georgia Southern and has bounced between Carlos Del Rio-Wilson and Zion Turner at quarterback, so this isn't a love letter. It's a coin flip with the crowd on one side. My one-point Marshall win clears the 1.5.

The Under fits both offenses. App State scores 26.3 points a game and Marshall scores 22.3. The Herd gave up 31.9 a game, but that number is inflated by the 45-0 opener at Penn State and the 45-17 loss at James Madison. Marshall's 20-13 win over South Alabama is the version that shows up when the stadium is loud. My 53 combined points slip under 53.5.

The room tilts hard toward the Herd on the side. The Formula takes App State Mountaineers −1.5 and has the Under at 27-25 App. Next Man Up has Marshall Thundering Herd +1.5 with App winning 28-27, and it takes the Over. Letdown Watch likes Marshall Thundering Herd +1.5 and the Under. In The Trenches likes Marshall Thundering Herd +1.5 too. Follow The Money is still waiting on a consensus spread, so its side is pending, and it has no total pick.

Next Man Up, to The Formula: "You're laying points with a team that scored three in Statesboro?" The Formula: "You're taking the Herd and then calling for a shootout. Pick a lane."

Zeb plans to take his hat off at ten and put his game face on at six. Mercy says Huntington does both of those better than anybody, and I'll trust a home crowd on this date to find one more stop.

Marshall Thundering Herd 27, App State Mountaineers 26. Marshall Thundering Herd cover the 1.5. Under 53.5.
