display.fanatic_story:
App State Mountaineers vs Marshall Thundering Herd kicks off at 6 p.m. ET in Huntington on Nov. 14, the 56th anniversary of the night Southern Airways Flight 932 went down and took 75 lives with it. Marshall nurse Mercy Holderby will be at the Memorial Fountain at 10 that morning before she ever thinks about football, and Watauga County's Zeb Coldiron, who drove up from Boone, already told her he's going with her.

Mercy: You don't have to come, Zeb. It's a Huntington morning.

Zeb: My granddad said you take your hat off for a thing like that no matter whose colors you wear. I'll be there.

That is the right way to begin a day like this one. Marshall calls Saturday its 75 game. The annual Memorial Fountain Ceremony begins at 10 a.m. on the plaza of the Memorial Student Center, and this year's speaker is Jeff Heath, who was a 19-year-old sophomore in 1970 when he lost both of his parents on that flight. He told the university the town carried his family after that, and he put it plainly: "we were definitely raised by the city of Huntington." Mercy grew up on stories like that one. Every Huntington kid did.

Mercy: People outside of here think the story ends with the crash. It doesn't. It ends with this town refusing to let the program die. That's what I think about every Nov. 14.

Zeb: Then let's go give them a game worth the day.

By 6 p.m. the plaza will be quiet and the lights will be on at Joan C. Edwards Stadium, and it's a real football game, too. These two have met 29 times now. App State leads the series 17-11, but here's what Mercy keeps bringing up: the Mountaineers haven't won in Huntington since Marshall moved up to the top level, and the Herd has won the last four games in this building, including a 52-37 shootout in 2024.

Zeb: You had to mention that one.

Mercy: You came to my town, Zeb. I get to mention it.

Both teams are 5-4, both are 2-3 in the Sun Belt, and both sit third in the East. Nobody's walking in hot. App State has dropped three of its last four, including a 19-3 loss at Georgia Southern and a 39-23 home loss to Georgia State last weekend. Malachi Singleton has thrown for 2,156 yards and 11 touchdowns, but six interceptions have crept in, four of them in the last two games.

Zeb: Malachi's fine. He threw for 241 and two scores last week. Sam Pickett has 590 receiving yards, and Chris Lofton went for 117 against Georgia State. We just have to quit handing the ball away.

Mercy: Please don't quit on my account.

Marshall's problems are louder. The Herd got pounded 49-13 at Georgia Southern last week, and the quarterback job has bounced between Carlos Del Rio-Wilson and Zion Turner all season. Del Rio-Wilson has 1,107 throwing yards with six touchdowns. Turner had the ball last Saturday and threw two interceptions. The defense has given up 31.9 points a game.

Mercy: I'm a nurse. I know a rough week when I see one. We had a rough week. We also beat South Alabama 20-13 on a Tuesday night in this stadium, and that was a defense that hit people.

She's right about the hitting. Safety Caleb Clark-Glover has 63 tackles and Kelvon McBride leads the team in sacks. App counters with linebacker Colton Phares and his 70 tackles and Caleb Sandstrom's six sacks, so whoever wins the trenches on third down probably wins the night.

Zeb: Jaquari Lewis has eight rushing touchdowns. If we get him going in the red zone, I'm whittling a little Herd and setting it on your porch.

Mercy: If Judah Price and the Herd get the last drive, you're whittling me a fountain.

That's the whole argument, really. Two programs that know each other cold, two teams that need a win to steady the season, and a stadium that will have been thinking about other things since sunrise. Huntington doesn't play this game on Nov. 14 to forget. It plays it to remember out loud, and the place has a way of finding one more stop when the clock's running down.

Zeb: Hats off this morning. Helmets on tonight.

Mercy: That's the Huntington way. Now go find your seat, and keep it warm for the fourth quarter.

Quiet morning at the fountain. Loud night for the Herd. My call: Marshall Thundering Herd 27, App State Mountaineers 26.

Florida vs Kentucky prediction: Kroger Field is sold out for the Black Out, and Lexington will be dressed in black when the No. 24 Gators visit the No. 6 Wildcats at 6:15 p.m. ET. I'm on Florida Gators +3 and Over 51.5, with Kentucky Wildcats 28, Florida Gators 27 as my final.

Rhett Abernathy-Coyle, the Kentucky horse-country man, likes the crowd. "Kenny Minchey has 14 touchdowns and two interceptions. We beat LSU and South Carolina in overtime. A full barn in black is our kind of night." Dax Marchetti, Florida's herpetology minor, likes his back. "Jadan Baugh has 14 rushing touchdowns. A gator waits in the water. We went to Austin and beat Texas 27-24."

DraftKings opened Kentucky −1.5 with 55.5 points on the over/under, and the market has moved to Kentucky −3 and 51.5. I'm taking both moves back. The spread went up after Kentucky lost 34-6 at Tennessee, which is a strange time to pay more for the Wildcats, and the over/under dropped four points after Florida scored 8 and 7 against Georgia and Oklahoma.

On the side, my number is one point. Kentucky's two biggest wins this year, at South Carolina and against LSU, were both 35-34 in overtime. The Wildcats win close, and close is what I see here. Florida has a real road win in Austin, and Baugh's 836 rushing yards give the Gators a way to shorten the game. Kentucky by one keeps Florida Gators +3 alive with room to spare.

On the over/under, the low-scoring Florida stretch is the reason the number dropped, and I think it dropped too far. Before the slump, Florida games finished 66-21, 52-28 and 44-39. Kentucky allows 25.8 points a game and Florida allows 27.6. The September Gators scored 52 twice. Minchey has led 34 or more three times in league play. My 55 combined points sit above 51.5.

The room agrees with me more than it argues. The Formula has Florida Gators +3 and the Over with Kentucky 28-27. Next Man Up also takes Florida Gators +3, likes the Over, and has Kentucky winning 30-28. Letdown Watch is on Florida Gators +3 and the Over as well. In The Trenches goes the other way and likes Kentucky Wildcats −3. Follow The Money is still waiting on a consensus spread, so its side is pending, and it has no total pick.

In The Trenches, to The Formula: "Three of you on the Gators? Somebody has to defend the barn." The Formula: "You can have the barn. We'll take the field goal."

Black jackets, a sold-out stadium, a one-score SEC game under the lights. Rhett gets his win. Dax gets his back-door chance at the wire, and Florida is at 32.4 points per game this season.

Kentucky Wildcats 28, Florida Gators 27. Florida Gators cover the 3. Over 51.5.

display.fanatic_story:
Florida Gators vs Kentucky Wildcats is the Week 11 sellout at Kroger Field, and Lexington has been told to show up dressed in black for a night game against a ranked SEC visitor. Kentucky horse-country kid Rhett Abernathy-Coyle has his black jacket pressed for the Black Out, and Florida's Dax Marchetti, the herpetology minor who measures every defense against some reptile, says he'll be the only splash of orange and blue in a stadium that looks like a moonless pasture.

Rhett: Sold out, Dax. Every seat. Kentucky told folks to come early, park where they're told and wear black.

Dax: Black is fine. Plenty of things hunt at night in Florida.

Rhett: Name one that wins in Lexington.

Dax: Last year? Not us. Two years ago? Us, 48-20.

That's the back-and-forth these two have lived for a decade. Over the last ten meetings it's five and five, and the swings are wild. Kentucky won 38-7 last season. Florida won 48-20 the year before. Kentucky won 33-14 the year before that. Nobody in either town gets comfortable about this game, and nobody should.

Kentucky comes in at 7-2, ranked sixth, second in the SEC, and freshly bruised. The Wildcats went to Knoxville last Saturday and lost 34-6, the worst the offense has looked all year.

Rhett: One bad night. Everybody gets one. Before that we won at South Carolina and beat LSU, both 35-34 in overtime, and won at Oklahoma 21-13. You don't do that without a horse that can run all day.

Kenny Minchey is the horse. He's thrown for 1,979 yards with 14 touchdowns and just two interceptions, and he went 26 of 34 at Tennessee even on the bad night. CJ Baxter has 541 rushing yards and eight touchdowns, and Kenny Darby is the top target with 576 receiving yards. Linebacker Grant Godfrey has 78 tackles, and Mi'Quise Humphrey-Grace has six sacks off the defensive front.

Dax: You know what Godfrey reminds me of? A snapping turtle. Patient. Then it's over.

Rhett: That's the nicest thing a Gator's ever said about Kentucky.

Dax: Don't get used to it.

Florida's year has two halves. In September the Gators scored 66 on Florida Atlantic, 52 on Campbell, 44 at Auburn and 52 on Ole Miss, with Aaron Philo running the show. Then things went sideways. They lost at Missouri and to South Carolina, went to Austin and stole a 27-24 win over Texas, and then lost to Georgia and Oklahoma while scoring 8 and 7. Tramell Jones Jr. has taken the most throws the last three games.

Dax: People forget the Texas game. We went into that stadium and walked out with it. That's a gator that knows how to wait in the water.

Rhett: People also remember 7 points against Oklahoma.

Dax: Jadan Baugh has 14 rushing touchdowns. Fourteen. He's the gator. Everything else is just water.

He has a point. Baugh's 836 yards and 14 scores make him the most dangerous back in this game, and Florida's defense has its own snapper in linebacker Myles Graham, who has 70 tackles. If Baugh gets loose on first down, Florida can keep Minchey on the sideline and make Kroger Field nervous.

The night itself belongs to Kentucky. The game is part of the program's Night Ops and Salute to Veterans weekend, and this is the fourth home sellout of the season. A sold-out black crowd under the lights is a different animal from the one Florida saw in September.

Rhett: My granddad used to say you can tell a good yearling by how it handles a crowd. Minchey handles a crowd.

Dax: My professor used to say you can tell a gator by how long it waits. We'll wait.

Rhett: Wait all night, then. The barn door closes at the final horn.

Dax: Leave it cracked. This one's going to the wire.

He might be right about that part. This has the look of a game that comes down to one drive, one kick or one stop, and in a stadium painted black, the home crowd gets the loudest vote.

Kroger Field stays black, loud and one point happy. My call: Kentucky Wildcats 28, Florida Gators 27.

Louisville vs North Carolina prediction: Kenan Stadium hosts its third straight night game, a 7 p.m. ET kickoff for a program that played its first five games at noon, and Louisville arrives in Chapel Hill for the first time since 2017. I'm on Louisville Cardinals −3 and Under 60.5, with Louisville Cardinals 30, North Carolina Tar Heels 25 as my final.

Bianca Thornberry, the Louisville Derby-party hostess, has a four-week parade to show off. "Florida State 44-20. Stanford 52-24. Georgia Tech 44-17. Lincoln Kienholz has 14 touchdowns and three interceptions." Ainsley Pemberton, the Tar Heels kinesiology PhD, has two painful nights at Kenan to answer for. "Syracuse beat us by one in overtime and Miami beat us by three. Billy Edwards Jr. threw four touchdowns against Miami. We're close."

Close is the problem. North Carolina lost both of those night games at home, and the one-point and three-point losses tell me the Heels compete but don't finish. Louisville has won four in a row by 24, 8, 28 and 27. DraftKings opened Louisville −2.5 with 59.5 points on the over/under, and it ticked up to −3 and 60.5. My five-point Louisville win clears the field goal.

The Cardinals have the run game to close it. Isaac Brown has 745 rushing yards and eight touchdowns, and Kienholz ran for 81 at Georgia Tech. North Carolina's Derek McDonald, with 89 tackles, is the best defender on the field, but he can't be in two places on a read option.

The Under is about the Tar Heels. North Carolina allows 22.8 points a game, and four of its nine games ended with neither team reaching 30. Louisville scores 40.8 a game, but the Heels drag opponents into their kind of game, the kind that ends 21-17 at Pittsburgh and 24-20 at Duke. My 55 combined points stay under 60.5, and the number has crept up a point from the open.

Every card in the room with an over/under call is on the Under, and the side splits two and two. The Formula has North Carolina Tar Heels +3 and likes the Under, with Louisville 29-27. Next Man Up also has North Carolina Tar Heels +3 and the Under, and its 30-29 Louisville score is about as close as it gets. Letdown Watch likes Louisville Cardinals −3 and likes the Under. In The Trenches likes Louisville Cardinals −3 and keeps quiet on the over/under. Follow The Money is still waiting on a consensus spread, so its side is pending, and it has no total pick.

Letdown Watch, to Next Man Up: "Thirty to twenty-nine and you're taking the home team? That's a coin flip in a bow tie." Next Man Up: "Better than your Derby hat theory."

Ainsley swears the first two night games taught the Heels something. Bianca thinks a hot team on the road in prime time is the best lesson in the sport, and I'm with the hat.

display.fanatic_story:
Louisville Cardinals vs North Carolina Tar Heels is Kenan Stadium's third straight night game, and Chapel Hill has officially retired its old nickname as the noon crew. Tar Heels kinesiology PhD Ainsley Pemberton has already rearranged her whole Saturday around a 7 p.m. ET kickoff, while Derby-party hostess Bianca Thornberry is bringing Louisville's four-game winning run to Kenan for the first time since 2017.

Ainsley: Five noon kickoffs to open the season, Bianca. Five. I ate so many hot dogs in the stands I started keeping score with the wrappers.

Bianca: And now?

Ainsley: Now we play under the lights. Syracuse, then Miami, now you.

Bianca: How did the first two go?

Ainsley: We don't talk about the first two.

That's fair, because they hurt. North Carolina lost 31-30 to Syracuse in overtime on Oct. 24 and 38-35 to Miami on Halloween, both at night at Kenan, both games the Tar Heels could have won. Billy Edwards Jr. threw for 341 yards and four touchdowns against Miami and still walked off a loser. Then the Heels went to UConn and won 38-21, with Jelani Thurman catching two touchdowns, and the mood in Chapel Hill came back up off the floor.

Ainsley: The body remembers what it's trained to do. We trained all fall to play close games. Now we finish one.

Bianca: Ainsley, I mean this kindly. We finish all of ours by halftime lately.

She's not wrong. Louisville is 6-3, third in the ACC at 5-2, and the last four weeks have been a parade. The Cardinals beat Florida State 44-20, won 34-26 at Syracuse, ran Stanford out of the building 52-24, and then went to Atlanta last Saturday and won 44-17 at Georgia Tech. They score 40.8 points a game.

Bianca: Lincoln Kienholz has 14 touchdowns and three interceptions. Isaac Brown has 745 rushing yards. Tre Richardson has 685 receiving yards. And Clev Lubin has seven sacks, which is about how many hats I own for the first Saturday in May.

Ainsley: Only seven?

Bianca: Seven I wear in public.

The Heels have their own case, and it's built on the defense. North Carolina allows 22.8 points a game. Linebacker Derek McDonald has 89 tackles, and Xavier Lewis matches Lubin with seven sacks. Edwards has 18 touchdown throws, and Jordan Shipp has 50 catches for 642 yards.

Ainsley: Here's the science. Kienholz runs. He ran for 81 yards at Georgia Tech. If McDonald keeps him in the pocket and Lewis gets home on third down, your parade turns into a slow walk.

Bianca: And if Brown gets to the second level?

Ainsley: Then I'm buying the first round of iced tea after the game.

The history here is short and loud. The last time Louisville came to Chapel Hill, in 2017, the Cardinals won 47-35. Ainsley was in the student section. Bianca was in a hat with a full-size rose on it.

Ainsley: That hat blocked three rows.

Bianca: Those rows thanked me.

The matchup that decides the night is Louisville's run game against a North Carolina defense that has been better than its losses. Brown has eight rushing touchdowns, and Louisville has turned short fields into points all month. If the Heels can make the Cardinals throw on third down, Edwards gets the ball back with a crowd behind him. If they can't, it's going to be a long walk to Franklin Street.

Ainsley: Saturday night, home crowd, three straight under the lights. We learned something from the first two.

Bianca: You learned how much the last minute hurts. I'm here to teach the rest of the lesson.

Ainsley: You'll be back in Kentucky by breakfast.

Bianca: With a win on the bus home and my hat still on.

Kenan gets its lights, and Louisville steals the show under them. My call: Louisville Cardinals 30, North Carolina Tar Heels 25.

Minnesota vs Penn State prediction: Beaver Stadium turns Saturday into Military Appreciation night, with ROTC cadets, veterans and military families honored and donated tickets flowing through the Seats for Servicemembers program. display.fanatic_story:
Minnesota Golden Gophers vs Penn State Nittany Lions is Military Appreciation night at Beaver Stadium, a 7 p.m. ET kickoff in Happy Valley with ROTC cadets, veterans and military families honored during the game. Former Penn State setter Luann Kessler bought two extra tickets through the Seats for Servicemembers program before she bought her own, and Minnesota's Tor Engebretsen, who learned his football on a frozen lake next to his grandpa, says he's never been colder than he'll feel in that stadium if the Lions get rolling.

Luann: You're going to love it, Tor. We honor the folks who served, the student section gets loud, and then we go to the Creamery.

Tor: In November?

Luann: Especially in November. You can't melt what's already frozen.

Tor: Spoken like a woman who's never sat on a bucket over an ice hole for six hours.

The weather talk hides nerves on both sides, because neither of these teams has had the season it wanted. Both are 5-4. Penn State is 2-4 in the Big Ten and sits 11th, which is a strange place for a program that opened by beating Marshall 45-0 and Buffalo 55-13. A four-game slide in late September and October took the air out of Happy Valley, with losses to Wisconsin, Northwestern, USC and Michigan by a combined 36 points.

Luann: And then we got up off the mat. Beat Purdue 31-17. Went to Seattle and won 28-25 at Washington. Carson Hansen ran for 119. Chase Sowell caught four balls for 125. That's a team that remembered who it is.

Tor: Or a team that played Purdue.

Luann: Watch your mouth on Military Appreciation night.

Minnesota is going the other way. The Gophers won at Washington 27-24 in September, beat Michigan 20-14 and edged Iowa 13-10, so Tor has had some very good Saturdays. But they've lost two straight, 23-16 in overtime at Indiana and 34-20 at home to UCLA, and the offense has gone quiet. Minnesota has scored 20 points or fewer in five straight games.

Tor: Drake Lindsey is a gamer. He's thrown for 1,797 yards and 11 touchdowns. But seven interceptions? My grandpa would say he keeps setting his tip-ups on ice that will not hold.

Luann: Your grandpa sounds smart.

Tor: He also says the Gophers are due.

The fight that matters is Penn State's defense against a Minnesota offense that needs to find a rhythm. The Lions allow 19.3 points a game, and linebacker Tony Rojas is everywhere, leading the team with 65 tackles and five sacks. Minnesota counters with TJ Bush Jr., who has six sacks, and linebacker Maverick Baranowski, who has 69 tackles. Both defenses can get after the quarterback. It's the offenses that have to prove something.

Rocco Becht is the guy who decides the night. He's thrown for 2,079 yards and 15 touchdowns with five interceptions, and when he's sharp, like the 271-yard, four-touchdown opener against Marshall, Penn State looks like the team everybody expected in August. When he's not, like the 114-yard day against Wisconsin, Beaver Stadium gets quiet in a hurry.

Tor: You know these two have played some real games. 2019, we won 31-26 in Minneapolis and the whole state lost its mind.

Luann: And 2022 we won 45-17 here, and 2024 we won 26-25 at your place, and I still replay the ending in my sleep.

Tor: I replay it too. Different ending in mine.

Luann: That's called a dream, Tor.

There's no trophy in this one, which is about the only time all fall Tor doesn't have one to talk about. What's at stake is a bowl trip and a little pride. Penn State gets home cooking, a crowd that honors its veterans before it gets loud, and a defense that has been the steady part of the season. Minnesota gets the chance to wreck that plan with one interception at the right time.

Tor: I'll give you this much, Luann. If you're buying the ice cream, I will stand when the veterans are honored.

Luann: I'm buying. You're standing. And you're going to watch Becht throw to Sowell over your safeties all night.

Tor: Fine. But I'm bringing my own bucket.

Is Tor's bucket big enough for Becht to Sowell all night? My call: Penn State Nittany Lions 29, Minnesota Golden Gophers 19.

display.fanatic_story:
San José State Spartans vs Air Force Falcons is the first home game in Colorado Springs since the Falcons won the Commander-in-Chief's Trophy, and Falcon Stadium gets to say thank you at a 7 p.m. ET kickoff. Retired instructor pilot Marissa Okonkwo-Hale wants every seat in the stadium to get a look at that trophy, while San José State product lead Tessa Nakagawa-Ruiz has flown in from the Bay Area with a laptop full of notes on how to slow down an option offense.

Marissa: First time since 2022, Tessa. We beat Navy 14-9, then went to West Point in the rain last Saturday and won 24-21. That's our 22nd Commander-in-Chief's Trophy. Nobody else at an academy has that many.

Tessa: Congratulations. I ran the numbers on the flight. You've got three quarterbacks.

Marissa: We've got three weapons.

That's the Air Force way, and it's been working. The Falcons are 7-2 and fourth in the Mountain West. Evan Medders leads the team with 549 rushing yards and seven touchdowns, and he threw the go-ahead touchdown to tight end Simon Kibbee at Army. Kemper Hodges ran for 119 yards in that game. Liam Szarka has taken snaps, and so has Howard Fisher IV. If you're a linebacker, you have no idea who's coming next, and that's the point.

Tessa: In my world we'd call that an unclear product owner.

Marissa: In my world we call it a three-ship formation.

The day itself is a show. Falcon Alley opens three hours before kickoff, the Drum and Bugle Corps welcomes the team in, the Wings of Blue parachute team jumps about 20 minutes before kickoff, weather permitting, and there's a military flyover right before the game. At halftime the Academy's live falcons fly over the crowd with their cadet falconers.

Tessa: I'll admit, the falcons are good. We don't have a halftime bird in San José.

Marissa: You have a lot of tech companies.

Tessa: We have a defense, too. That's what I came to talk about.

She has a point. San José State is 5-5, but the Spartans give up 22.0 points a game and have kept two of their losses to five points or fewer. They lost 16-13 in overtime to Wyoming and 21-16 to New Mexico, and they just beat Northern Illinois 30-19 at home. Linebacker Dylan Lee has 88 tackles, and Jayland McGlothen has seven sacks off the defensive front. Against an option team, that's where the game is won, at the point of attack, in the gap you're responsible for.

Tessa: Every play, Lee has a job. He does it, we win the snap. He guesses, Medders is gone. I've got a dashboard for it.

Marissa: Medders doesn't read dashboards.

The Spartans have their own quarterback question. Luke Weaver leads them with 1,810 throwing yards and 11 touchdowns, and Daniel Rolovich threw for 231 yards and a touchdown in the win over Northern Illinois. Carson Clark is the go-to receiver with 61 catches for 689 yards. Jabari Bates has 682 rushing yards, and Viliami Teu scored twice last week.

Tessa: We've played you six times in the last decade. We won two of them, including 17-7 in 2024. We know how to make this ugly.

Marissa: And you lost 26-16 last year. We know how to make it ugly too.

That 17-7 game is the blueprint for the Spartans: keep the Falcons off the field with long drives, tackle in the open field, and make every Air Force possession a grind. The Falcons' answer is to keep the chains moving the way they did against UNLV and UConn, when they scored 41 and 35 here at home, and let the fourth quarter belong to an offense that never stops pounding.

Marissa: Blake Fletcher has 84 tackles for us. Our defense can play too. Weaver throws into traffic, Fletcher's there.

Tessa: You're going to tell me Fletcher reads dashboards?

Marissa: Fletcher reads quarterbacks.

The altitude is the quiet extra guest at Falcon Stadium, and the visitors always feel it in the second half. Tessa says she's been training on the stairs at her office. Marissa says those aren't the same stairs.

Tessa: I'll be fine. I've got a water bottle and a good attitude.

Marissa: Bring two of each. The falcons fly at halftime. The Falcons run in the fourth.

Tessa drinks both water bottles, and the trophy stays in Colorado Springs. My call: Air Force Falcons 29, San José State Spartans 19.

Troy Trojans vs South Alabama Jaguars is the Battle for the Belt, a Saturday night in Mobile at Hancock Whitney Stadium with a 7 p.m. ET kickoff and a belt waiting for whichever side survives. Mobile Mardi Gras float-builder Azalea Fairhope-Grice has been polishing the case where she plans to keep that belt, and Troy's Marlo Pickens, the old long snapper and peanut farmer's son drove down to Mobile reminding her that his school has held it far more often.

Marlo: Ten wins to four, Azalea. That's the series. You can look it up.

Azalea: I did. Then I looked at 2024. We beat you 25-9 right here, in this stadium.

Marlo: And then last year we beat you 31-24 in overtime at our place.

Azalea: I don't remember that.

Marlo: You remember it fine.

That's the Battle for the Belt in a nutshell. It's the in-state Sun Belt fight that both towns treat like a family argument at Thanksgiving, and the belt itself is the prop that keeps it personal. Troy has had it more often over the last decade, winning eight of the last ten meetings, but Azalea brings up the 2024 win in Mobile every chance she gets.

The records tell you how even this is. Both teams are 4-5. Both are 2-3 in the conference and third in the West. Neither has much margin left to fix the season.

Troy's year swung hard. The Trojans hung 55 on Southern Miss, then lost 33-6 at Louisiana and 21-14 to UL Monroe, then stunned James Madison 24-21 in overtime on the road, then lost 41-17 to Louisiana Tech last Saturday. The quarterback job has moved between Goose Crowder, who has nine touchdown throws, and Tucker Kilcrease, who has had the ball the last two games.

Marlo: We beat James Madison on their field. That's a real team. People forget that.

Azalea: People remember the 41 last week.

Marlo: Fair.

South Alabama's year has been a roller coaster on the other end of the scoreboard. The Jaguars put up 52 on UL Monroe and won a 56-49 track meet at Arkansas State, but they've dropped three straight since, by seven at Marshall, 35-20 to Louisiana Tech and 28-26 at Louisiana last weekend. Bishop Davenport threw for 210 yards and ran for two scores in that last one, and Jared Hollins leads the team with 1,195 throwing yards and nine touchdowns.

Azalea: We score. We score 32.4 points a game. Keenan Phillips has 595 rushing yards. Brendan Jenkins went for 101 yards last week. We just have to stop people.

Marlo: You give up 32.2.

Azalea: I said we just have to stop people.

That's the matchup. Troy's best player might be defensive back Donnie Smith, who has eight sacks, a ridiculous number for a defensive back, and linebacker Keno Jones has 70 tackles. If Smith keeps getting home on blitzes, South Alabama's quarterbacks will be throwing off their back foot all night. South Alabama safety Cole Blaylock leads the Jaguars with 46 tackles, and that tells you how often the ball has gotten to the third level against this defense.

Marlo: Smith is the best blitzer in this league. I snapped for twelve years and I never saw a DB time it like that.

Azalea: Then we'll throw it before he gets there. Jenkins runs, Davenport throws, and Phillips mops up the rest.

Marlo: Gavin Griffin has 465 yards for us. We can run too.

The belt has a way of making these games weird. Six of the last ten meetings were decided by eight points or more, and then last year's went to overtime. Mobile on a November night, with a belt at stake and two teams that know each other too well, points to another tight one.

Azalea: When we win, I'm putting that belt on the lead float in February. Front and center.

Marlo: The belt doesn't ride floats.

Azalea: It will this year. I've already built the stand.

Marlo: Then you'd better hope Davenport throws it before Donnie Smith gets there.

Azalea gets her belt for the stand, and Marlo drives back to Troy grumbling. My call: South Alabama Jaguars 30, Troy Trojans 27.

display.fanatic_story:
Utah Utes vs Arizona Wildcats is the biggest night Casino Del Sol Stadium has had in a long time. No. 3 Utah, unbeaten at 9-0, comes to Tucson to face No. 22 Arizona at 5:30 p.m. local time, and the school says it's the highest-ranked opponent to visit since 2007. The ask for the crowd is "Stripe the Sol," with sections assigned colors so the whole bowl comes out striped. Tucson native Inez Paloverde, who played piccolo in the marching band for four years and still hums the fight song in the grocery store, has her stripe assignment and she's taking it seriously. Utah's Aspen Mortensen, a former ski racer who treats every road trip like a downhill course, flew down in a parka and took it off at the airport.

Aspen: It's seventy degrees in November. How does anybody here get anything done?

Inez: We get plenty done. Ask your team about the last two times we played.

Aspen: I knew you'd say that.

She was always going to say that. Arizona won the last two meetings, 42-18 and 23-10, and for a Utah program that went 6-2 against the Wildcats across the last decade, those two still sting. The difference now is that Utah hasn't lost to anybody this year.

The Utes have been about as steady as a team can be. They've beaten Arkansas 43-10, shut out Utah State 33-0, won 27-24 at Colorado and 49-25 at Cincinnati, and handled BYU 28-20 last week. Devon Dampier has 20 touchdown throws and ran for two more against BYU. Wayshawn Parker has 762 rushing yards and nine scores. Braden Pegan has eight touchdown catches, two of them last Saturday.

Aspen: Dampier's like a good slalom skier. He doesn't do anything flashy. He just never misses a gate.

Inez: He threw two interceptions against Houston.

Aspen: And we still won. That's the point.

Arizona's season has been louder. The Wildcats put up 52 at West Virginia, beat Iowa State 39-3, and beat Cincinnati 34-7, the same Cincinnati team Utah beat by 24 on the road. They lost at BYU and lost 34-26 at Texas Tech, but they've won all five home games, and last week they survived TCU 29-28 on a Friday night here. Noah Fifita has 2,794 throwing yards and 21 touchdowns. He went for 417 yards at Texas Tech. Isaiah Mizell has 753 receiving yards, and Giovanni Richardson caught 11 balls for 171 yards against TCU.

Inez: Fifita is the best quarterback in this league. I'll argue that with anyone, including you.

Aspen: I'm not arguing. I'm just saying our defense gives up 16.3 points a game.

Inez: Ours gives up 19.9, and we've played better offenses.

Aspen: Have you?

Inez: We played Texas Tech.

That's the matchup in a sentence. Utah wants to run Parker and Dampier, keep the clock moving and keep Fifita on the sideline. Arizona wants to throw early and often and turn the game into a shootout. Utah's front has been good against the run all season, and that's where Arizona's offense is weakest. Kedrick Reescano leads the Wildcats with 373 rushing yards, which tells you the offense lives in Fifita's arm. Linebacker Chase Kennedy has six sacks for Arizona, and Utah's blockers will have to account for him on every snap.

Aspen: When you race downhill, the one thing you never do is panic in the middle of the course. You stay in your tuck, so to speak.

Inez: So to speak.

Aspen: Fine. You stay calm. Utah doesn't panic.

Inez: Arizona doesn't panic either. We just make noise. You'll hear it.

She's right about that. A striped stadium, a top-five opponent and the Wildcats' best home crowd of the year will make Tucson loud. Utah's going to have to handle the noise on third downs, especially in the second half when Arizona's defense feeds off the crowd.

Inez: When we win, I'm bringing my piccolo to the student section and playing "Bear Down" until security asks me to stop.

Aspen: And when Utah wins?

Inez: I'll still play it. Just slower.

Aspen: I'll take slower.

This feels like a game decided by one drive late, maybe by a kick. Utah has the steadier résumé and the better defense. Arizona has the crowd, the quarterback and a two-game run against the Utes that nobody in Salt Lake has forgotten. I'll take the unbeaten team, by just enough.

Stripe the Sol all you want, Tucson. The Utes leave unbeaten. My call: Utah Utes 28, Arizona Wildcats 25.

Baton Rouge socialite Celestine "Cece" Thibodeaux has been on the phone since Sunday arranging enough crawfish to feed half of Tigerland, out of season or not. Caroline "Caro" Whitfield, who carries herself with rodeo-queen polish and runs her Texas fandom like a consulting project, arrived with a binder.

Cece: A binder. You brought a binder to Tiger Stadium.

This is Lane Kiffin's first season at LSU, and it's been a ride. The Tigers opened by beating Clemson 51-10, crushed Texas A&M 35-6 and shut out Mississippi State 31-0. They lost at Ole Miss, lost 35-34 in overtime at Kentucky, and then last week Alabama came to Baton Rouge and won 31-13. Sam Leavitt threw for 380 yards in that game and still didn't get the Tigers into the end zone through the air. Jackson Harris caught 11 balls for 166 yards.

Cece: We moved the ball all night. We just didn't finish. That won't happen twice in a row in this building.

Caro: You said that about Kentucky, too.

Cece: Kentucky was a road game. This is home. Different animal.

Texas comes in at 7-2, and almost every game has been tight. The Longhorns beat Ohio State 24-23, won 20-17 at Tennessee and beat Ole Miss 34-27. Their two losses were both by three, to Oklahoma and Florida. Arch Manning has 18 touchdown throws, including three in each of his last two games, and last week he went 28 of 38 for 297 yards at Missouri. Raleek Brown has 537 rushing yards, and Ryan Wingo leads the receivers.

Caro: Arch is playing the best football of his life right now. Seven touchdown throws in his last three games is not an accident.

Cece: Seven in three. You did that in your head?

Caro: It's on tab five.

The matchup to watch is up front. Texas has Colin Simmons, who has 10.5 sacks and wrecks plans on his own. LSU has Princewill Umanmielen with 8.5. Both defenses have been stingy all year, holding opponents under 18 points a game. Leavitt has thrown nine interceptions, so the Texas defense will be waiting for a mistake, with Jelani McDonald and his 67 tackles patrolling the back end.

Cece: Leavitt's going to throw it down the field. You can't sit back against Jackson Harris all night. He has 800 yards.

Caro: We don't have to sit back. We have Colin.

Cece: Then I'll have Dilin Jones run right at him.

Dilin Jones has 713 rushing yards and seven scores, and if LSU can rely on the run early, the crowd gets into it, and Tiger Stadium at night gets loud enough to rattle a visiting quarterback.

Caro: We played at Tennessee. Loud doesn't scare us.

Cece: Tennessee isn't loud. Tennessee is a hum compared with here.

Caro: I'll update the binder.

The last time these teams played was 2019 in Austin, a 45-38 LSU win that people in both towns still talk about. This one probably won't have that many points. It'll be closer to a slugfest with a few big throws mixed in, and the last possession might decide it.

Cece: When we win, I'm bringing you a plate and you're going to eat it with your hands like a Louisiana girl.

Caro: And when Texas wins?

Cece: You still eat with your hands. That's not optional down here.

Caro: Then I'll add it to the binder.

Does crawfish taste better after a one-point night at Tiger Stadium? Ask Cece. My call: LSU Tigers 25, Texas Longhorns 24.

display.fanatic_story:
Stanford Cardinal vs Virginia Tech Hokies brings a Saturday night in November to Lane Stadium, 7:30 kickoff, Blacksburg cold, and a game theme built around Ag Day and Veterans Day. It's also Stanford's last regular-season trip to the East Coast this year, which is a relief to Ignatius "Iggy" Yamamoto-Ross, the Palo Alto founder whose last four apps all failed and who still describes each one as "a learning." Ruthanne Dellinger, a former drum major in the Corps of Cadets who carries a real lunch pail to every home game, met him in the parking lot with a thermos.

Ruthanne: You look cold.

Iggy: I'm wearing three layers. One of them is a fleece vest with a company logo on it.

Ruthanne: Which company?

Iggy: It doesn't exist anymore.

That's Iggy. He's an optimist who has learned to live with crashes. This Stanford season has tested both halves of that.

The Cardinal are 4-5, and the wins have been real. They beat Hawai'i 37-27, beat Georgia Tech 34-27 with Davis Warren throwing for 396 yards, and beat NC State 31-28 with four touchdown throws from Warren. But the road has been brutal. Stanford lost 35-7 at Duke, 57-3 at Wake Forest, 58-7 at Notre Dame and 52-24 at Louisville. The Cardinal give up 37.3 points a game, and most of the damage has come away from home.

Iggy: We call those beta tests.

Ruthanne: Losing by fifty-one is a beta test?

Iggy: A rough one.

Stanford did get an extra week to prepare. Its last game was Oct. 31, and Iggy insists that matters. Virginia Tech, meanwhile, played last Friday night at SMU and came home with a 51-28 loss that Ruthanne doesn't want to discuss.

Ruthanne: We don't talk about Dallas. We talk about Clemson.

She means the 20-16 win at Clemson in October, the best day of the Hokies' season. Virginia Tech is 6-3, with wins at Maryland, at Boston College and over Georgia Tech, plus that Clemson game. The losses were 35-33 to Pitt, 25-20 at Cal and the SMU game. Ethan Grunkemeyer has been efficient all year, with 18 touchdown throws and only three interceptions, and Jeffrey Overton Jr. ran for 123 yards and two scores at SMU. Aycen Stevens has 8.5 sacks up front.

Ruthanne: That's Lunch Pail football. Show up, do the job, go home. Stevens is the whole philosophy in one guy.

Iggy: We have Micah Ford. He has 751 rushing yards. That's not nothing.

Ruthanne: It's not nothing. It's just not Overton.

The matchup is about whether Stanford can make this a game early. Warren has only three interceptions, so the Cardinal don't beat themselves through the air. The trouble is what happens on the other side. If Virginia Tech can run Overton and let Grunkemeyer choose his spots to Que'Sean Brown, who has 722 receiving yards, the Stanford defense is going to spend a long night on the field. Warren will need to keep pace, and in road games this season, the Stanford offense hasn't scored more than 24.

Iggy: We're due. Every founder is due eventually. That's the whole pitch.

Ruthanne: How many have hit?

Iggy: Define hit.

The last meeting, in 2024, was a 31-7 Virginia Tech win, and the Hokies have been 8-2 in their military appreciation games, a number Ruthanne recited from memory. Lane Stadium on a cold night, with the crowd jumping to "Enter Sandman" when the team runs out, is not the place a team with Stanford's road résumé wants to be.

Ruthanne: When we win, I'm opening my lunch pail on the sideline and eating a ham biscuit in your honor.

Iggy: And if Stanford wins?

Ruthanne: Then I'll eat it slower and think about my life.

Iggy: That's what I do after every product launch.

The Hokies should handle this one. Stanford will throw it around and get some points, but Virginia Tech has the better back, the better front and the home crowd on a night built for it.

Cold, loud and exactly what Blacksburg ordered. My call: Virginia Tech Hokies 37, Stanford Cardinal 20.

display.fanatic_story:
Purdue Boilermakers vs Iowa Hawkeyes is a Saturday night at Kinnick Stadium with a Military Appreciation theme, a crowd that will turn and wave to the children's hospital after the first quarter, and a November chill rolling off the cornfields. Orrin Kalvelage, who farms a few miles outside Iowa City and has missed exactly one home game in his adult life, for a calving, is sitting in his usual seats. Barnaby Wolcott-Reese, a Purdue mechanical engineer who spent two winters building a scale replica of the Boilermaker Special in his garage, drove over from West Lafayette with the replica in his trunk.

Orrin: You brought a train.

Barnaby: It's a locomotive. Scale replica. Working whistle.

Orrin: Don't blow it in here.

Barnaby: No promises.

That's the matchup in a nutshell. Purdue arrives with something loud and clever. Iowa arrives with defense and a long memory.

The Hawkeyes are 7-2 and No. 19, and the defense has been the whole story. They give up 12.2 points a game. They shut out Northern Illinois, Northern Iowa and Wisconsin at Kinnick. They held Iowa State to 13, won 20-19 at Michigan and held Northwestern to 10 last week. Linebacker Cam Buffington has 82 tackles, and Joseph Anderson leads the front with four sacks.

Orrin: You know how many points Wisconsin scored here? None. Zero. They drove home quiet.

Barnaby: That's Wisconsin.

Orrin: That's a Big Ten team.

Barnaby: Debatable this year.

Purdue is 3-6, but the offense can move. The Boilermakers score 29.4 points a game. Ryan Browne has 2,260 throwing yards, Fame Ijeboi has 10 rushing touchdowns, and Asaad Waseem has 709 receiving yards. They beat Minnesota 41-13 and won at Illinois. The trouble is the other side. Purdue gives up 32.3 a game and has lost three straight, the last one 34-29 to Maryland.

Barnaby: We lost to Maryland by five. That's an engineering tolerance.

Orrin: It's a loss.

Barnaby: A tight one.

The key is whether Browne can handle the Iowa pressure. He went 10 of 29 at Penn State, and Iowa's defense is built to make quarterbacks look like that. If Purdue can get Ijeboi going early and stay in third-and-short, the Boilermakers can keep the crowd from taking over. If not, Kinnick at night is a long place to be behind.

Orrin: You know what Iowa does? We punt, we play defense, we kick field goals, and we win. People laugh at it. We don't care.

Barnaby: I don't laugh. I respect it. It's like a well-designed bridge. Ugly, but it holds.

Orrin: Ugly?

Barnaby: Functional.

Iowa's offense isn't pretty. Hank Brown has 1,316 throwing yards, and the Hawkeyes scored 10 in a loss at Minnesota. But they put up 41 at Washington, Kamari Moulton has 541 rushing yards, and L.J. Phillips Jr. ran for 128 yards at Northwestern last week. That's enough when the defense is this good.

Barnaby has one thing to hang on to. Purdue went into Iowa City in 2021 and beat the No. 2 Hawkeyes 24-7. He brings it up every time, and Orrin has never fully recovered.

Orrin: That was five years ago. I've had five harvests since then. Let it go.

Barnaby: I'll let it go when you stop doing the wave at me.

Barnaby: Fair. Then I'll wave too.

UNLV Rebels vs New Mexico Lobos is a Saturday night in Albuquerque with first place in the Mountain West at stake for the home team, a 5:30 p.m. kickoff at University Stadium and an Indigenous Heritage theme for the night. Paloma Begaye-Ortiz, a hot-air balloon pilot who flies the October fiesta every year and has a Lobo painted on her basket, says this is the best New Mexico team she's ever seen. Monroe-Kalani, the UNLV loyalist who flew in wearing a red visor she swears has never lost a road game, came to remind her about last fall.

Monroe-Kalani: You know we've won four of the last six against you.

Paloma: We won last year.

Monroe-Kalani: By five.

Paloma: Still counts. We go up in balloons at dawn. We know how to wait for the right wind.

That's the vibe in Albuquerque this week. The Lobos are 8-1 and 5-0 in the league, and it's been a long time since anyone around here felt this calm about a November game.

New Mexico's defense has been the reason. The Lobos give up 10.9 points a game. They beat Central Michigan 38-7, UTEP 61-7 and Mercyhurst 70-7 at home, and they just went to Nevada and won 31-3. Even their lone loss was respectable, 14-6 at Oklahoma. Defensive end Brett Karhu has 7.5 sacks, and linebacker Mercury Swaim has 55 tackles.

Paloma: When the wind is right, a balloon goes exactly where you want it. When the defense is right, so does the other team. Backwards.

Monroe-Kalani: Is that a real balloon saying?

Paloma: It is now.

The offense is built around the run. Scottre Humphrey has 647 rushing yards and 13 touchdowns, and he ran for 107 yards and two scores at Nevada. Toa Fa'avae doesn't throw it much, but tight end Cade Keith has 358 receiving yards and caught a touchdown last week.

UNLV is 5-4 and has been a coin flip all year. The Rebels beat Cal 39-31 and Northern Illinois 31-24, but they lost 41-31 at Air Force and 41-35 at home to Wyoming last Saturday. Jai'Den Thomas has 753 rushing yards and ran for two scores against Wyoming. Jackson Arnold has 15 touchdown throws but went 7 of 18 last week. Kayden McGee has six touchdown catches, and safety Jake Pope has 76 tackles.

Monroe-Kalani: Arnold had a bad night. Everybody has a bad night.

Paloma: Fa'avae threw three interceptions at San José State and we still won.

Monroe-Kalani: That's my point. You're beatable.

Paloma: Beatable isn't beaten.

That's the question for Saturday. New Mexico has won close games when the offense sputters, 21-16 twice in a row before Nevada, and UNLV will try to make it another one of those. The Rebels need Thomas to run and Arnold to avoid the big mistake. The Lobos need Humphrey to wear the defense down and the crowd to show up loud.

The crowd should be there. The Kids Free Initiative is in place for the game, and tickets run from $16 to $88, so it'll be a family night as much as a football night. Paloma has already promised her nieces and nephews a balloon ride at the fiesta next year if the Lobos win the league.

Monroe-Kalani: That's a lot of pressure on a football team.

Paloma: They can handle it. They're 8-1.

The New Mexico defense should be the difference. UNLV can score some, and Thomas will get his yards, but the Lobos are a different team this year, and they've been better than this opponent all season.

Monroe-Kalani: If UNLV wins, you take me up in the balloon.

Paloma: And if New Mexico wins?

Monroe-Kalani: I still want the balloon ride.

Paloma: Then wear the visor. Let's see if it works at a thousand feet.

Paloma lifts off with a Lobo on her basket and first place in her pocket. My call: New Mexico Lobos 33, UNLV Rebels 16.

South Carolina Gamecocks vs Arkansas Razorbacks is a Saturday night on The Hill in Fayetteville, 6:45 p.m. local, with No. 21 South Carolina riding a four-game winning run into Razorback Stadium. Bubba Fayette-Dorsey, an Ozark middle-school science teacher who calls the Hogs at every meal and once built a volcano in the shape of a razorback for a class project, has been teaching his students the physics of a loud stadium all week. Beau Cheraw, who played snare in the Gamecock drumline and still can't hear "2001" without standing up, drove in from Columbia with his sticks in the glove box.

Bubba: You brought drumsticks to Fayetteville.

Beau: I bring them everywhere. You never know when "2001" is going to come on.

Bubba: Nobody's playing that here.

Beau: I'll hum it.

This is the 25th meeting, and Arkansas leads the series 14-10. The last time these two met in Fayetteville, in 2022, the Razorbacks won 44-30, and Bubba has the highlights saved on his phone.

Bubba: Forty-four points. I showed that game in class as a lesson on momentum.

Beau: That was four years ago. We're a different team.

He's right about that. South Carolina is 6-3 and playing its best football. The Gamecocks won 38-19 at Florida, beat Tennessee 27-24, won 42-25 at Oklahoma and then held Texas A&M to nine points in a 17-9 win last Saturday. LaNorris Sellers is the whole engine, with 2,100 throwing yards, 17 touchdown throws, 637 rushing yards and seven more scores on the ground. Mazeo Bennett Jr. leads the receivers.

Beau: Sellers is the best player on the field every week. When he runs, it's like a drum solo. You don't know where it's going, but you know it's going to end loud.

Bubba: KJ Jackson has 1,853 throwing yards for us.

Beau: That's nice.

Bubba: Don't do that.

Arkansas is 3-6, and it's been a rough year in the Ozarks. The Razorbacks lost 43-10 at Utah, 45-17 to Georgia and 34-10 to Missouri at home. They won at Vanderbilt 31-21, though, and they lost by only three at Auburn last week, with Cam Settles running for 100 yards. Chris Marshall has 698 receiving yards, and linebacker Ben Bogle has 56 tackles.

Bubba: We played Auburn tough. We played Tennessee tough. We just can't close.

Beau: We've closed four straight.

Bubba: I noticed.

The matchup to watch is Sellers against the Arkansas front. When he gets out of the pocket, the Gamecocks score. Arkansas has to keep him inside and make him throw from the pocket, and that's easier said than done. On the other side, South Carolina's defense has been up and down. It gave up 41 to Mississippi State and 35 to Kentucky, but it held Texas A&M to nine. Linebacker Fred Johnson has 70 tackles, and Tomiwa Durojaiye has four sacks.

Bubba: Here's the science lesson. Sound travels faster in cold air.

Beau: I don't think that's right.

Bubba: It's slower, actually. But it feels louder. That's psychology.

Beau: You teach science.

Bubba: I teach eighth graders. They trust me.

Night games on The Hill can get strange. Arkansas has won four of the previous five meetings on The Hill dating back to 2007, and Bubba is counting on the crowd calling the Hogs loud enough to rattle Sellers early.

Beau: He played at Oklahoma two weeks ago. He's not rattling.

Bubba: Oklahoma doesn't call the Hogs.

Beau: Fair.

This should be South Carolina's game. The Gamecocks are better at quarterback, better on defense, and they're riding the kind of swagger that a four-game run gives a team. Arkansas will make it loud, but Sellers should make enough plays.

Bubba: If we win, you're playing "2001" on my kitchen table with those sticks.

Beau: And if South Carolina wins?

Bubba: Then you play it anyway. But I get to call the Hogs over it.

Call the Hogs all night, Bubba. The Gamecocks crow last. My call: South Carolina Gamecocks 31, Arkansas Razorbacks 22.

display.fanatic_story:
North Texas Mean Green vs UTSA Roadrunners is Homecoming at the Alamodome, an 8 p.m. kickoff in San Antonio and the 15th meeting in what has become the most-played series in UTSA history. The first 10,000 fans get homecoming jerseys, so the building should be a sea of the same shirt. Marisol Ybarra, who wears her Fiesta medals on a sash she's been adding to since high school, plans to wear the jersey over the sash. Grady Mayhew-Ochoa, a Denton jazz drummer who has played every dive on Fry Street, came down I-35 with a pair of brushes in his back pocket.

Marisol: You brought brushes to a football game.

Grady: Brushes are for ballads. I brought them as a joke. This game's not going to be a ballad.

Marisol: What is it, then?

Grady: Bebop. Fast, loud, and nobody knows the chord changes.

That might be the best description of this matchup anyone's going to give. North Texas is 7-2 and scores 44.7 points a game. UTSA is 7-2 and scores 33.0. Both defenses have been leaky, and the last two meetings ended 48-27 and 55-17.

Grady: Fifty-five to seventeen last year. I still have the ticket stub framed.

Marisol: That one hurt. Here's the thing, though. We lead the series 8-6, and we're 5-1 at home.

Grady: In San Antonio?

Marisol: In San Antonio.

Grady: I didn't know that.

Marisol: Nobody in Denton does.

The North Texas offense is the headliner. Jahiem White has 1,186 rushing yards and 16 touchdowns, and he ran for 139 yards and three scores against Rice last week. Tayven Jackson has 2,880 throwing yards and 23 touchdowns, including a 492-yard night at Texas State. Justin Stevenson has 898 receiving yards. The Mean Green beat Navy 49-39 on the road, beat Florida Atlantic 48-41 and won 45-44 in overtime at Tulsa.

Grady: White runs like a drummer playing double-time. You can't keep up with him.

Marisol: We have Darion White.

Grady: Different White.

Marisol: Same name. Different attitude. He has 59 tackles.

UTSA has been steadier than its scores suggest. The Roadrunners won 31-26 at Texas State, beat Navy 38-34, won 42-19 at Tulane and beat Colorado State 59-45. Owen McCown has 2,016 throwing yards and threw for 359 against Navy. Will Henderson III has 682 rushing yards. The low point was last week, a 60-29 loss at Florida Atlantic, but UTSA played that one on a Thursday and has had nine days to fix it.

Marisol: Nine days is a long time. You can rebuild a whole defense in nine days.

Grady: You can rebuild a whole band in nine days. Doesn't mean it'll swing.

Marisol: It'll swing.

The key is whether UTSA can slow White at all. North Texas allows 30.9 points a game, so the Roadrunners will score. But if White gets to the second level all night, the Mean Green can match whatever UTSA puts up and then some. McCown needs a big night, and Mekhi Anderson, who caught two touchdowns at Florida Atlantic, needs to be part of it.

Marisol: The Alamodome on Homecoming is loud. Our alumni come back for this one.

Grady: North Texas fans travel too. We'll be in the upper deck, making noise.

Marisol: The upper deck is very far away.

Grady: We'll be loud and far away.

The series has swung back and forth for a decade, with neither side owning it. This year both teams are good enough to make it close. North Texas has the better offense and the better back, and UTSA has the crowd.

Marisol: When we win, you're playing a drum solo at my cousin's quinceañera next month.

Grady: And if North Texas wins?

Marisol: Then you still play. But you play a cumbia.

Grady: I know two cumbias. That's enough.

Grady plays both of his cumbias on the way out of the Alamodome. My call: North Texas Mean Green 35, UTSA Roadrunners 32.

display.fanatic_story:
Texas Tech Red Raiders vs Oklahoma State Cowboys is a late Saturday night in Stillwater, 8:30 p.m. local at Boone Pickens Stadium, with No. 15 Texas Tech coming up from Lubbock at 8-1 and Oklahoma State coming off one of the wildest nights in program history. Dusty, an Oklahoma State ag-economist who runs the timing clock at rodeos across the state on summer weekends, says he's never seen the Cowboys play like this. Bodie Ratliff, who rode bareback for the Texas Tech rodeo team and still walks like he just got off a horse, has heard all about it.

Bodie: Sixty-six points at Kansas State. Everybody in Lubbock heard about it.

Dusty: It was a program record in Manhattan. Sixty-six to twenty-eight.

Bodie: We scored 53 the same night.

Dusty: Against West Virginia. They scored 48.

Bodie: We still won.

That's this matchup. Two offenses that can score on anybody, and two fan bases that keep a running count of each other's points.

Oklahoma State is 6-3, and Drew Mestemaker has become one of the most dangerous quarterbacks in the country. He has 2,962 throwing yards and 29 touchdowns, and he threw four more at Kansas State. Caleb Hawkins went past 1,000 rushing yards in that game, with 175 yards and three scores. Justin Bowick has 10 touchdown catches. The Cowboys beat Oregon 39-31 at home and Colorado 57-24, but they also lost 51-49 at Iowa State and 35-32 at Houston.

Dusty: I've timed a lot of events. Mestemaker gets the ball out faster than any calf roper I've ever clocked.

Bodie: That's a weird compliment.

Dusty: It's the best one I've got.

Texas Tech is 8-1, with the only loss at Cincinnati. The Red Raiders beat Arizona State 53-25, won 29-7 at Colorado and held off Arizona 34-26. Thomas Castellanos has taken over at quarterback the last two weeks, and he threw for 362 yards and five touchdowns against West Virginia. J'Koby Williams has 954 rushing yards, and he ran for 160 against the Mountaineers. Linebacker Austin Romaine has 81 tackles, and A.J. Holmes Jr. has 7.5 sacks.

Bodie: Castellanos plays like a bareback rider. He holds on with one hand and lets the rest of him fly.

Dusty: That's how you get thrown.

Bodie: Not if you hold on for eight seconds.

Dusty: Football games are longer than eight seconds.

Bodie: Then he'll hold on longer.

The last two meetings went Texas Tech's way, 56-48 in 2024 and 42-0 last year, and Bodie brings up the shutout constantly. Dusty would like everyone to know that Oklahoma State is a different team now.

Dusty: Last year was last year. We had a bad year. This year we can score on anybody.

Bodie: You gave up 51 at Iowa State.

Dusty: And we scored 49.

Bodie: You still lost.

Dusty: By two. That's a rounding error.

The key is the Texas Tech defense against Mestemaker. If Holmes and the Red Raider front can get pressure, Mestemaker has thrown eight interceptions and can be forced into mistakes. If not, the Cowboys will score at home, the way they have all year. On the other side, Williams needs to control the clock and keep Mestemaker on the sideline.

Bodie: When we win, you're timing my next ride, and you're not allowed to round down.

Dusty: And if Oklahoma State wins?

Bodie: Then you time it anyway. And I'll know you rounded down.

Dusty: I never round down.

Bodie: You just told me two points was a rounding error.

This feels like a game decided in the last two minutes. Texas Tech has the better season and the better defense. Oklahoma State has the hotter offense and the home crowd. I'll take the Red Raiders, barely.

Eight seconds? Lubbock hangs on for every one of them. My call: Texas Tech Red Raiders 33, Oklahoma State Cowboys 32.

display.fanatic_story:
Utah State Aggies vs San Diego State Aztecs is Senior Night in Mission Valley, and the Aztecs' seniors get their moment on the field before the ball is kicked at 6:30 p.m. at Snapdragon Stadium. Kai Delgado-Sorensen, an Ocean Beach surfer who checks the swell report before he checks the score, paddled out at dawn and will be in his seat by kickoff with salt still in his hair. Hyrum Tolleson, who runs a dairy outside Logan and milked his cows at four in the morning before driving to the airport, is still adjusting to the weather.

Hyrum: It's seventy degrees. In November. My cows would riot.

Kai: Your cows would love it here. Everybody loves it here.

Hyrum: My cows are from Cache Valley. They don't love anything.

That's Hyrum. He's practical, a little grumpy and very sure Utah State has this series figured out. He has reason. The Aggies have won three straight meetings, including the Mountain West title game in 2021 and a 41-20 win in 2024. San Diego State still leads the all-time series 13-5, but Hyrum doesn't count the old ones.

Kai: Thirteen to five, man. That's the all-time count.

Hyrum: The all-time count has a lot of years before I was born in it.

Kai: Still counts.

Hyrum: Not to me.

Both teams are 4-5, and both have had rough years. San Diego State lost 66-14 at Oregon State and 41-16 at Toledo, and the quarterback job has gone back and forth between Jayden Denegal and Stone Saunders. But the Aztecs have been better at home. They beat Texas State 31-29, Fresno State 26-23 and Washington State 26-20, and they had last week off to get healthy for this one. Javion Kinnard has 613 rushing yards, and Lucky Sutton ran for 115 against Washington State. Linebacker Sione Hala has 90 tackles. Jaylon Hawkins has three kickoff returns for touchdowns this year, so Utah State's kicker has a decision to make on every kickoff.

Kai: Hawkins on a kick return is like catching a perfect set. You see it coming, and then it's just gone.

Hyrum: We'll kick it out of the end zone.

Kai: You'll try.

Utah State has been a different story. The Aggies lost their opener to Idaho State, then lost close ones at Washington and Texas State. But they've figured something out lately. McCae Hillstead has taken over at quarterback, and the Aggies beat Colorado State 31-14 and Fresno State 17-10 in his two games. The defense is the strength. Brevin Hamblin has 71 tackles from safety, and the Aggies allow 20.6 points a game. Eli Wood leads the receivers with 479 yards and five touchdowns.

Hyrum: Our defense is like a good milking schedule. Same time every day. No surprises.

Kai: That sounds boring.

Hyrum: Boring wins.

Kai: Not in San Diego. Here, fun wins.

The question is whether Utah State can win on the road. The Aggies haven't yet this season, and they've had trouble scoring away from Logan. San Diego State's defense has been up and down, but the Aztecs' offense should find some room against a team that has had to grind for every point.

Kai: Senior Night is huge for us. These guys have been through a lot. They're going out with a win.

Hyrum: Everybody says that on Senior Night.

Kai: And sometimes it's true.

This feels like a close, low-key game that comes down to a big play late. Maybe a kick return, maybe a Kinnard run. San Diego State is at 26.4 points per game this season, and on a calm night at home after a week off, that should be enough.

Hyrum: If Utah State wins, you're coming up to Logan to milk a cow at four in the morning.

Kai: And if San Diego State wins?

Hyrum: Then I'm going surfing. Once. And I'm not getting in past my knees.

Kai: Deal.

Who's going surfing after this? Hyrum, knee-deep and grumbling. My call: San Diego State Aztecs 24, Utah State Aggies 21.

display.fanatic_story:
Wyoming Cowboys vs UTEP Miners is Senior Night at the Sun Bowl, an 8 p.m. kickoff in El Paso, and the first time UTEP has hosted Wyoming since Nov. 25, 1995. This is the 34th meeting between the two schools, and it's been a long gap. Neto Galindo, whose father spent thirty years as an ironworker and who sizes up everything in his life like a chunk of ore, has been waiting for this one. Colter Sprague, who runs cattle on a ranch outside Laramie and wears the same Carhartt jacket in every weather, flew down and is already complaining that nothing is blowing sideways.

Colter: No wind. How do you people know which way is north?

Neto: We look at the mountains. Franklin Mountains, right there. They don't move.

Colter: Back home, the wind tells you which way is north. And which way your hat went.

That's the matchup in a sentence. Wyoming is built for bad weather and grinding games. UTEP is hoping for one good night.

The Miners are 1-8, and Neto isn't pretending otherwise. They lost 51-0 at Oklahoma, 61-7 at New Mexico and 31-7 at North Dakota State. But they've been getting closer. They lost 30-13 to Nevada, 24-11 to San José State and then 17-14 to Hawai'i last Saturday, a three-point game.

Neto: My dad used to say you can tell good ore by how it holds together under heat. We're holding together. Better every week.

Colter: That's a nice way to say you're 1-8.

Neto: It's a nice way to say we're not quitting.

Raymond Moore III has been the quarterback lately and leads the team with 522 rushing yards. EJ Colson Jr. has also played, with seven touchdown throws. Jaden Smith leads the receivers, and linebacker Jayden Wilson has 57 tackles. Sterling Miles has four sacks.

Wyoming is 6-3 and has won four straight. The Cowboys beat Northern Illinois 41-23, Air Force 28-14 and then won 41-35 at UNLV last week. Tyler Hughes runs the offense from quarterback and leads the team with 676 rushing yards, and Samuel Harris ran for 128 yards and two scores at UNLV. Ethan Stuhlsatz has 68 tackles, and Esaia Bogar has 5.5 sacks.

Colter: Hughes is like a good cow horse. He doesn't look fancy, but he gets you where you're going.

Neto: You compare everybody to animals.

Colter: You compare everybody to rocks.

Neto: Ore. Not rocks. Ore is worth something. Rocks are just rocks.

Colter: I'll take that back to Laramie.

The question for Saturday is whether Wyoming can play on the road the way it has at home. The Cowboys lost at Colorado State, Central Michigan and North Dakota State, and they needed overtime to win at San José State. The UNLV win was a good sign. UTEP's chance is to keep it close, the way it did against Hawai'i, and hope a senior makes one big play on his last night at the Sun Bowl.

Neto: Senior Night does something to a team. These guys have lost a lot. They want to go out right.

Colter: I respect that.

Neto: You'd better.

Colter: I do. I'm a rancher. I respect anybody who keeps showing up.

The Sun Bowl at night in November is cool and quiet compared with Laramie, but the crowd will come out for the seniors. Wyoming should win, but UTEP has played better at home lately, and this one could stay closer than people think.

Neto: If UTEP wins, you're wearing a Miners hard hat on the flight home.

Colter: And if Wyoming wins?

Neto: Then I'm wearing your jacket. Just for a day.

Colter: It's never been washed.

Neto: I'll take my chances.

Neto takes his chances. The Cowboys take the Sun Bowl. My call: Wyoming Cowboys 27, UTEP Miners 18.

Colorado State vs Washington State prediction: Colorado State, 3-6, makes the trip to Martin Stadium in Pullman to play 1-8 Washington State, and the kickoff is 10:30 p.m. ET Saturday. I'm on Colorado State Rams +9.5 and Under 67.5, with Washington State Cougars 35, Colorado State Rams 27 as my final.

Hank Palouse, who grows wheat outside Pullman and has sat through every one of these losses, thinks this is the week. "We had last week off. Owen Eshelman threw for 299 at San Diego State. Colorado State gives up 44.8 a game." Ansel Rimrock, the Fort Collins trail runner, isn't buying a 1-8 favorite. "Hauss Hejny has 16 touchdown throws and two picks. We scored 38 on Boise State last week. Your team scores 19 a game."

The side is about what Washington State can actually produce. The Cougars score 19.0 points a game and have scored 24 or fewer in seven of nine. They lost 26-6 to Fresno State and 31-10 to Boise State at home. Covering 9.5 would take a big offensive night from a team that hasn't had many. Colorado State has scored 23 or more in eight of nine games, including 45 at UTSA and 56 against San Diego State. The market opened Washington State −6.5 and climbed to −9.5, which feels like a reaction to how bad the Rams' defense is. I have Washington State by eight.

The Under is a Washington State call. Cougar games have stayed under 67.5 in eight of nine, and the only exception was a 48-30 loss at Oregon State. Colorado State's games go high, but this one is in Pullman in November against an offense that doesn't push the pace. The posted number climbed from 62.5 to 67.5. My 62 combined points land under it.

The risk is the Colorado State defense. The Rams allow 44.8 points a game, gave up 64 to Boise State last week and 66 at Texas State. If Washington State's offense finally wakes up against the worst defense it's seen, the Cougars could win by three scores and push this over by themselves.

The cards are split. The Formula likes Colorado State Rams +9.5 and likes the Under at Washington State 32-27. Next Man Up has Washington State Cougars −9.5 and the Over at 39-29. Letdown Watch likes Washington State Cougars −9.5 and likes the Under at 37-22. In The Trenches likes Colorado State Rams +9.5 and stays out of the over/under. Follow The Money is still waiting on a consensus spread, so its side is pending, and it has no total pick.

Next Man Up, to Letdown Watch: "A 1-8 team laying nine and a half, and you like it?" Letdown Watch: "I like the other team's defense even less."

Hank says the Cougars are due for one good night. Ansel says the Rams can outrun anybody's bad season. I think Washington State wins and Colorado State keeps it inside the number.

Washington State Cougars 35, Colorado State Rams 27. Colorado State Rams cover the 9.5. Under 67.5.

display.fanatic_story:
Colorado State Rams vs Washington State Cougars is a cold Saturday night on the Palouse, a 7:30 p.m. kickoff at Martin Stadium for the Native American and Military Appreciation Game, and the first time these teams have met in Pullman since 2022. Hank Palouse, whose family has grown wheat on the rolling hills outside town for three generations, says this has been the hardest season he can remember. Ansel Rimrock, a Fort Collins trail runner who logs his miles on the foothills above Horsetooth Reservoir, drove up with a thermos of coffee and a headlamp.

Hank: You brought a headlamp to a football game.

Ansel: I'm running the hills behind the stadium at halftime.

Hank: It's going to be dark and cold.

Ansel: That's the best time to run.

That's Ansel. Colorado State's season has been hard too, but he keeps moving.

Washington State is 1-8, and Hank isn't hiding from it. The Cougars have lost six straight, and it's their toughest year since 2009. The only win came against Duquesne. They lost 17-16 at Utah State, 26-20 at San Diego State and 34-24 to Arizona, so they've been close a few times. They had last week off, and Owen Eshelman has taken over at quarterback, throwing for 299 yards at San Diego State.

Hank: You know what a bad wheat year teaches you? You still plant in the fall. You don't stop.

Ansel: That's beautiful, man.

Hank: It's not beautiful. It's just farming.

Colorado State is 3-6 under Jim Mora, and its problem is obvious. The Rams give up 44.8 points a game, the worst in the country. They gave up 64 to Boise State last week, 66 at Texas State and 59 at UTSA. But they can score. Hauss Hejny has 16 touchdown throws and only two interceptions, and the Rams put up 56 against San Diego State and 45 at UTSA. RJ Vick leads the receivers, and linebacker Oumar Diomande has 85 tackles.

Ansel: We score like we're running downhill. We defend like we're running uphill.

Hank: Into the wind.

Ansel: Into the wind, with a backpack.

Washington State won 20-3 in Fort Collins last year, and the Cougars have won all three meetings since 2022. Hank remembers every one.

Hank: Twenty to three. We held you to a field goal.

Ansel: That was last year. We have Hejny now.

Hank: And we have Eshelman.

Ansel: Eshelman has no touchdown throws in his last two games.

Hank: He has two rushing touchdowns at San Diego State.

Ansel: That's a fair point.

The matchup is simple. Washington State has to score, and it hasn't done much of that, putting up 19.0 points a game. Colorado State's defense should give the Cougars a chance to have their best offensive night of the year. On the other side, Hejny needs to keep the Rams in it, because the Cougar defense, led by Keith Brown and his 71 tackles, is the better group.

Hank: The crowd's going to be small but loud. People who show up for a 1-8 team are the real ones.

Ansel: I respect that. I run ultras. Nobody shows up for those either.

Hank: Then you understand.

Pullman in November is no place for a team from out of town, and the Cougars should finally get one. But Colorado State will score, and this probably won't be comfortable for Hank until late.

Ansel: If Colorado State wins, you're running the hills with me at halftime.

Hank: And if Washington State wins?

Ansel: Then I still run them. You just hold the headlamp.

Hank: Deal. But I'm wearing my coat.

Hank keeps his coat on, and the Cougars warm up the Palouse. My call: Washington State Cougars 35, Colorado State Rams 27.

North Dakota State vs Hawai'i prediction: North Dakota State, 7-2, flies all the way to Honolulu to play 3-6 Hawai'i at the Clarence T.C. Ching Athletics Complex, the last kickoff of the night at 11 p.m. ET Saturday. I'm on North Dakota State Bison −6.5 and Over 38.5, with North Dakota State Bison 25, Hawai'i Rainbow Warriors 18 as my final.

Inga Halvorsen, the Fargo ag-economist who keeps a spreadsheet of Bison titles, opens with defense. "We allow 11.9 points a game. We shut out Fordham and Wyoming. We won at Air Force." Kainoa Akana-Baird, the big-wave surf instructor, has a home crowd and a hot hand. "We've won two straight, 56-21 at Northern Illinois and 17-14 at UTEP. Micah Alejado has 2,489 throwing yards."

The side comes from the North Dakota State defense. The Bison have held seven of nine opponents to 17 points or fewer, and they beat Wyoming 28-0, the same Wyoming team that beat Hawai'i 27-10. Hawai'i has lost three of four at home, scoring 6 against UNLV, 16 against San José State and 10 against New Mexico. North Dakota State scored 28 or more in seven of nine and had last week off. The market opened North Dakota State −9.5 and dropped to −6.5, so the price got better. I have the Bison by seven.

The Over needs North Dakota State's offense, and it's been steady. Nathan Hayes has 13 touchdown throws, and Jackson Williams has 614 receiving yards. Hawai'i allows 23.3 points a game, and the Rainbow Warriors just put up 56 at Northern Illinois, so they can score in bunches when Alejado gets going. The posted number fell from 42.5 to 38.5. My 43 combined points clear it.

The risk is the trip. This is about as long a road trip as college football has, and North Dakota State's two losses came on the road, 13-7 at UNLV and 21-16 at New Mexico. Hayes threw three interceptions at UNLV. If the Bison sputter after a long flight, Hawai'i can keep it inside a touchdown.

The cards are split on the side. The Formula has North Dakota State Bison −6.5 and likes the Over at 26-19. Next Man Up likes North Dakota State Bison −6.5 but has the Under at 24-12. Letdown Watch likes Hawai'i Rainbow Warriors +6.5 and likes the Over at North Dakota State 23-19. In The Trenches likes Hawai'i Rainbow Warriors +6.5 and makes no over/under call. Follow The Money is still waiting on a consensus spread, so its side is pending, and it has no total pick.

Letdown Watch, to Next Man Up: "A four-hour time change, a bye week and an island. That's a letdown spot." Next Man Up: "It's a bye week. They're rested, not sunburned."

Kainoa says Honolulu at night does strange things to visiting teams. Inga says the Bison have won in a lot of strange places. I think the defense travels.

display.fanatic_story:
North Dakota State Bison vs Hawai'i Rainbow Warriors has never happened before. These programs have never played, and their debut comes on Military Night in Honolulu at 6 p.m. local, with military bands, an aircraft flyover for Veterans Day weekend and a Timmy Chang bobblehead for the first 3,000 fans. Kainoa Akana-Baird, who teaches big-wave surfing on the North Shore and has been tossed by more waves than he can count, says the island is ready. Ingeborg "Inga" Halvorsen, a Fargo agricultural economist who can tell you the price of durum wheat and every Bison title by year, landed with a winter coat she won't need.

Inga: It's eighty degrees. I packed for Fargo.

Kainoa: You packed for the wrong planet.

Inga: It was nineteen degrees when I left.

Kainoa: Then you're welcome.

That's the matchup in a nutshell. A team from the northern plains meets a team from the middle of the Pacific, and both think the other one is crazy.

North Dakota State is 7-2, and the defense has been ridiculous. The Bison allow 11.9 points a game. They shut out Fordham and Wyoming, won 38-32 at Air Force and beat Nevada 31-17. Their two losses were close, 13-7 at UNLV and 21-16 at New Mexico, and both came on the road. Donovan Woolen has 66 tackles, and Kelton McCaslin has five sacks. Nathan Hayes has 13 touchdown throws, and Jackson Williams has 614 receiving yards.

Inga: Bison football is like wheat futures. Boring, steady, and over time it always goes up.

Kainoa: That's the least exciting thing I've ever heard.

Inga: It works.

Hawai'i is 3-6, but the Rainbow Warriors have won two straight. They put up 56 at Northern Illinois and then won 17-14 at UTEP last week. Micah Alejado has 2,489 throwing yards and threw for 303 at UTEP. Kainoa Carvalho leads the receivers, and Titan Lacaden caught 11 balls last week. Linebacker Jamih Otis has 64 tackles.

Kainoa: Alejado is like a good surfer on a big day. He doesn't panic. He waits for the right wave.

Inga: And if the wave doesn't come?

Kainoa: Then he waits some more. It always comes.

Inga: That's not how football works.

Kainoa: It's how Alejado works.

The challenge for Hawai'i is the Bison defense. Alejado throws a lot, and North Dakota State has been very good at stopping teams that throw. Hawai'i lost 21-6 to UNLV and 21-10 to New Mexico at home, and the Rainbow Warriors need their quarterback to be sharp against a defense that rarely gives anything away. The Bison also had last week off, so they've had time to adjust to the trip.

Kainoa: The bobblehead is Timmy Chang. You know who he is?

Inga: The quarterback with all the records.

Kainoa: The quarterback with all the records. Every kid in Honolulu wants one.

Inga: I want one too.

Kainoa: You have to get here early. The first 3,000.

Inga: I've been here since Thursday.

The Bison have won a lot of games in a lot of places, and Inga has a shelf at home with a trophy replica for every title. But they've never played here, and this is a long way from Fargo. On a night built around the military, with the bands playing and the flyover overhead, Honolulu should give them a full taste of the island before the first snap.

Kainoa: When Hawai'i wins, you're coming out to the North Shore and paddling out with me.

Inga: And if North Dakota State wins?

Kainoa: Then you still paddle out. I'll keep you on the small waves.

Inga: I'll bring my coat.

Turns out the Bison can travel. Inga still keeps her coat on. My call: North Dakota State Bison 25, Hawai'i Rainbow Warriors 18.
